1. NORMAL USER PORTAL + DASHBOARD
1.1 Required functionality

A newly authenticated normal user should get:

User Portal
│
├── Dashboard
│   ├── Overview
│   ├── My Tasks
│   ├── Notifications
│   ├── Recent Activity
│   ├── Quick Actions
│   └── Search
│
├── My Work
│
├── Notifications
│
├── Profile
│
├── Security
│   ├── Password
│   ├── MFA
│   ├── Sessions
│   └── Devices
│
└── Settings

The dashboard should be populated from:

PostgreSQL
    ↓
Authenticated user
    ↓
Authorized records
    ↓
Dashboard service
    ↓
API
    ↓
Next.js dashboard

There should be no code such as:

users = [...]
tasks = [...]
notifications = [...]

in production.

1.3 Database models
users/models.py
from datetime import datetime
from enum import StrEnum
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import Boolean, DateTime, String
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.database import Base


class UserRole(StrEnum):
    USER = "USER"
    SYSTEM_ADMIN = "SYSTEM_ADMIN"


class UserStatus(StrEnum):
    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
    SUSPENDED = "SUSPENDED"
    DISABLED = "DISABLED"


class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4
    )

    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(320),
        unique=True,
        index=True,
        nullable=False,
    )

    password_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    first_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    last_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    role: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(30),
        nullable=False,
        default=UserRole.USER,
    )

    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(30),
        nullable=False,
        default=UserStatus.ACTIVE,
    )

    email_verified: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

    last_login_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True)
    )

        DateTime(timezone=True)

        DateTime(timezone=True),

1.7 Dashboard response
from datetime import datetime
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel


class DashboardTask(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    title: str
    status: str
    due_at: datetime | None


class DashboardNotification(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    title: str
    body: str
    created_at: datetime
    read: bool


class DashboardActivity(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    action: str
    resource_type: str | None
    resource_id: UUID | None
    created_at: datetime


class DashboardResponse(BaseModel):
    user_id: UUID

    pending_task_count: int
    unread_notification_count: int

    tasks: list[DashboardTask]
    notifications: list[DashboardNotification]
    recent_activity: list[DashboardActivity]
1.8 Dashboard service
from sqlalchemy import func, select


class DashboardService:

    def __init__(self, db):
        self.db = db

    async def get_dashboard(
        self,
        user_id,
    ):

        task_count = await self.db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(UserTask)
            .where(
                UserTask.user_id == user_id,
                UserTask.status.in_(["PENDING", "IN_PROGRESS"]),
            )
        )

        unread_count = await self.db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(Notification)
            .where(
                Notification.user_id == user_id,
                Notification.read_at.is_(None),
            )
        )

        task_rows = (
            await self.db.scalars(
                select(UserTask)
                .where(UserTask.user_id == user_id)
                .order_by(UserTask.due_at.asc().nullslast())
                .limit(10)
            )
        ).all()

        notification_rows = (
            await self.db.scalars(
                select(Notification)
                .where(Notification.user_id == user_id)
                .order_by(Notification.created_at.desc())
                .limit(10)
            )
        ).all()

        activity_rows = (
            await self.db.scalars(
                select(UserActivity)
                .where(UserActivity.user_id == user_id)
                .order_by(UserActivity.created_at.desc())
                .limit(20)
            )
        ).all()

        return DashboardResponse(
            user_id=user_id,
            pending_task_count=task_count or 0,
            unread_notification_count=unread_count or 0,
            tasks=[
                DashboardTask(
                    id=x.id,
                    title=x.title,
                    status=x.status,
                    due_at=x.due_at,
                )
                for x in task_rows
            ],
            notifications=[
                DashboardNotification(
                    id=x.id,
                    title=x.title,
                    body=x.body,
                    created_at=x.created_at,
                    read=x.read_at is not None,
                )
                for x in notification_rows
            ],
            recent_activity=[
                DashboardActivity(
                    id=x.id,
                    action=x.action,
                    resource_type=x.resource_type,
                    resource_id=x.resource_id,
                    created_at=x.created_at,
                )
                for x in activity_rows
            ],
        )
1.9 Authentication dependency
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status


async def require_user(
    current_user=Depends(get_current_user),
):
    if current_user.status != "ACTIVE":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Account is not active.",
        )

    if current_user.role != "USER":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="This account must use the system administrator portal.",
        )

    return current_user

This is important.

A SYSTEM_ADMIN account cannot enter the normal user application.

1.10 Dashboard API
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

router = APIRouter(
    prefix="/api/user",
    tags=["User Dashboard"],
)


@router.get("/dashboard")
async def dashboard(
    current_user=Depends(require_user),
    db=Depends(get_db),
):

    service = DashboardService(db)

    return await service.get_dashboard(
        current_user.id
    )
1.11 Normal login

The normal login endpoint must reject system admins.

@router.post("/login")
async def login(
    payload: LoginRequest,
    db=Depends(get_db),
):

    user = await authenticate_user(
        db,
        payload.email,
        payload.password,
    )

    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=401,
            detail="Invalid credentials.",
        )

    if user.status != "ACTIVE":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403,
            detail="Account is not active.",
        )

    if user.role == "SYSTEM_ADMIN":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403,
            detail="Use the system administrator portal.",
        )

    access_token = create_access_token(
        user_id=user.id,
        portal="USER",
    )

    return {
        "access_token": access_token,
        "token_type": "bearer",
    }
1.12 Token portal separation

Do not only check role.

Also place the intended portal inside the token:

{
    "sub": "actual-user-uuid",
    "role": "USER",
    "portal": "USER",
    "exp": "actual-expiry"
}

For administrators:

{
    "sub": "actual-user-uuid",
    "role": "SYSTEM_ADMIN",
    "portal": "ADMIN",
    "exp": "actual-expiry"
}

Then your authorization layer checks both.

1.13 Next.js user dashboard
web/
└── app/
    ├── login/
    │   └── page.tsx
    │
    └── dashboard/
        ├── page.tsx
        ├── components/
        │   ├── OverviewCards.tsx
        │   ├── TaskList.tsx
        │   ├── Notifications.tsx
        │   ├── RecentActivity.tsx
        │   └── QuickActions.tsx
        └── loading.tsx
dashboard/page.tsx
"use client";

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

type Dashboard = {
  pending_task_count: number;
  unread_notification_count: number;
  tasks: {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    status: string;
    due_at: string | null;
  }[];
  notifications: {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    body: string;
    created_at: string;
    read: boolean;
  }[];
  recent_activity: {
    id: string;
    action: string;
    resource_type: string | null;
    resource_id: string | null;
    created_at: string;
  }[];
};

export default function DashboardPage() {
  const [data, setData] = useState<Dashboard | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    async function load() {
      try {
        const token = localStorage.getItem("user_access_token");

        if (!token) {
          window.location.href = "/login";
          return;
        }

        const response = await fetch(
          `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/user/dashboard`,
          {
            headers: {
              Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
            },
            cache: "no-store",
          }
        );

        if (response.status === 401 || response.status === 403) {
          localStorage.removeItem("user_access_token");
          window.location.href = "/login";
          return;
        }

        if (!response.ok) {
          throw new Error("Unable to load dashboard.");
        }

        const result = await response.json();

        setData(result);
      } catch (err) {
        setError(
          err instanceof Error
            ? err.message
            : "Unable to load dashboard."
        );
      }
    }

    load();
  }, []);

  if (error) {
    return <main>{error}</main>;
  }

  if (!data) {
    return <main>Loading...</main>;
  }

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Dashboard</h1>

      <section>
        <article>
          <h2>Pending Tasks</h2>
          <strong>{data.pending_task_count}</strong>
        </article>

        <article>
          <h2>Unread Notifications</h2>
          <strong>{data.unread_notification_count}</strong>
        </article>
      </section>

      <section>
        <h2>My Tasks</h2>

        {data.tasks.map((task) => (
          <article key={task.id}>
            <strong>{task.title}</strong>

            <div>{task.status}</div>

            {task.due_at && (
              <time>
                {new Date(task.due_at).toLocaleString()}
              </time>
            )}
          </article>
        ))}
      </section>

      <section>
        <h2>Notifications</h2>

        {data.notifications.map((notification) => (
          <article key={notification.id}>
            <strong>{notification.title}</strong>
            <p>{notification.body}</p>
          </article>
        ))}
      </section>
    </main>
  );
}

The actual available tools should later be populated from the real modules in your startup application.

2. SYSTEM ADMIN PORTAL

This is a separate application surface, not simply /dashboard/admin.

Use:

https://admin.yourdomain.com

and:

https://app.yourdomain.com

The normal user portal should not contain the administrator login form.

2.1 Admin functionality

A production system administrator portal should provide at least:

System Admin
│
├── Overview
│   ├── Users
│   ├── Active users
│   ├── Suspended users
│   ├── System events
│   └── Recent admin activity
│
├── User Management
│   ├── Search
│   ├── View
│   ├── Suspend
│   ├── Reactivate
│   ├── Disable
│   └── Role management
│
├── Security
│   ├── Authentication events
│   ├── Failed logins
│   ├── Active sessions
│   ├── Security alerts
│   └── Access reviews
│
├── Audit
│   ├── Admin actions
│   ├── User actions
│   └── System events
│
├── System
│   ├── Health
│   ├── Queue status
│   ├── Database status
│   ├── Integration status
│   └── Storage status
│
└── Configuration
    ├── Application settings
    ├── Authentication policy
    ├── Feature flags
    └── System configuration

A normal user trying the administrator portal gets rejected.

An administrator trying the normal portal also gets rejected.

2.4 Admin audit model
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import DateTime, ForeignKey, String, Text
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column


class AdminAuditEvent(Base):
    __tablename__ = "admin_audit_events"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4
    )

    admin_user_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

    action: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    target_user_id: Mapped[UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id")
    )

    target_type: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(100)
    )

    target_id: Mapped[UUID | None]

    metadata_json: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

Every administrative action should create one.

2.5 Admin dashboard API
@router.get("/admin/dashboard")
async def admin_dashboard(
    admin=Depends(require_system_admin),
    db=Depends(get_db),
):

    total_users = await db.scalar(
        select(func.count()).select_from(User)
    )

    active_users = await db.scalar(
        select(func.count())
        .select_from(User)
        .where(User.status == "ACTIVE")
    )

    suspended_users = await db.scalar(
        select(func.count())
        .select_from(User)
        .where(User.status == "SUSPENDED")
    )

    recent_events = (
        await db.scalars(
            select(AdminAuditEvent)
            .where(
                AdminAuditEvent.admin_user_id == admin.id
            )
            .order_by(
                AdminAuditEvent.created_at.desc()
            )
            .limit(20)
        )
    ).all()

    return {
        "total_users": total_users or 0,
        "active_users": active_users or 0,
        "suspended_users": suspended_users or 0,
        "recent_admin_events": [
            {
                "id": str(event.id),
                "action": event.action,
                "target_user_id": (
                    str(event.target_user_id)
                    if event.target_user_id
                    else None
                ),
                "created_at": event.created_at,
            }
            for event in recent_events
        ],
    }

All numbers come from PostgreSQL.

2.6 Admin user search
@router.get("/admin/users")
async def list_users(
    search: str | None = None,
    limit: int = 50,
    offset: int = 0,
    admin=Depends(require_system_admin),
    db=Depends(get_db),
):

    limit = min(max(limit, 1), 100)
    offset = max(offset, 0)

    query = select(User)

    if search:
        search_value = f"%{search.strip()}%"

        query = query.where(
            User.email.ilike(search_value)
            | User.first_name.ilike(search_value)
            | User.last_name.ilike(search_value)
        )

    result = await db.scalars(
        query
        .order_by(User.created_at.desc())
        .offset(offset)
        .limit(limit)
    )

    return result.all()
2.7 Suspend user
@router.post("/admin/users/{user_id}/suspend")
async def suspend_user(
    user_id: UUID,
    admin=Depends(require_system_admin),
    db=Depends(get_db),
):

    if admin.id == user_id:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Administrator cannot suspend own account.",
        )

    user = await db.get(User, user_id)

    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail="User not found.",
        )

    user.status = "SUSPENDED"

    event = AdminAuditEvent(
        admin_user_id=admin.id,
        action="USER_SUSPENDED",
        target_user_id=user.id,
        target_type="USER",
        target_id=user.id,
        metadata_json={},
        created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    )

    db.add(event)

    await db.commit()

    return {
        "status": "SUSPENDED",
        "user_id": str(user.id),
    }
2.8 Reactivate user
@router.post("/admin/users/{user_id}/reactivate")
async def reactivate_user(
    user_id: UUID,
    admin=Depends(require_system_admin),
    db=Depends(get_db),
):

    user = await db.get(User, user_id)

    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail="User not found.",
        )

    user.status = "ACTIVE"

    db.add(
        AdminAuditEvent(
            admin_user_id=admin.id,
            action="USER_REACTIVATED",
            target_user_id=user.id,
            target_type="USER",
            target_id=user.id,
            metadata_json={},
            created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )
    )

    await db.commit()

    return {
        "status": "ACTIVE",
        "user_id": str(user.id),
    }
2.9 Role changes need extra protection

Do not allow:

normal admin UI → freely make anybody system admin

For production, add a separate privileged operation.

@router.post("/admin/users/{user_id}/role")
async def update_role(
    user_id: UUID,
    payload: RoleUpdateRequest,
    admin=Depends(require_system_admin),
    db=Depends(get_db),
):
    ...

But impose:

SYSTEM_ADMIN
      ↓
privileged action
      ↓
re-authentication / MFA
      ↓
audit event
      ↓
role change

For a high-security deployment, require two-person approval for creation or removal of system administrators.

2.10 Bootstrap the first system administrator

Do not hardcode:

email = "admin@example.com"
password = "admin123"

Instead, promote an already-created real user through a protected deployment/operations command.

Example:

export ADMIN_EMAIL="the-real-admin-email"
python -m app.cli.promote_system_admin
cli/promote_system_admin.py
import asyncio
import os

from sqlalchemy import select

from app.core.database import AsyncSessionLocal
from app.users.models import User


async def promote():

    email = os.environ.get("ADMIN_EMAIL")

    if not email:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "ADMIN_EMAIL environment variable is required."
        )

    async with AsyncSessionLocal() as db:

        result = await db.scalar(
            select(User).where(
                User.email == email
            )
        )

        if not result:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Specified user does not exist."
            )

        result.role = "SYSTEM_ADMIN"

        await db.commit()

        print(
            f"System administrator role assigned to "
            f"{result.email}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(promote())

This uses an actual database user.

There is no demo account.

2.12 Admin login page
"use client";

import { FormEvent, useState } from "react";

export default function AdminLoginPage() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState("");

  async function submit(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();

    setError("");

    const response = await fetch(
      `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/admin/login`,
      {
        method: "POST",
        headers: {
          "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          email,
          password,
        }),
      }
    );

    if (!response.ok) {
      const body = await response.json().catch(() => null);

      setError(
        body?.detail ?? "Unable to authenticate."
      );

      return;
    }

    const data = await response.json();

    localStorage.setItem(
      "admin_access_token",
      data.access_token
    );

    window.location.href = "/dashboard";
  }

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>System Administration</h1>

      <form onSubmit={submit}>
        <input
          type="email"
          autoComplete="username"
          value={email}
          onChange={(event) =>
            setEmail(event.target.value)
          }
          required
        />

        <input
          type="password"
          autoComplete="current-password"
          value={password}
          onChange={(event) =>
            setPassword(event.target.value)
          }
          required
        />

        <button type="submit">
          Sign in
        </button>

        {error && (
          <p role="alert">
            {error}
          </p>
        )}
      </form>
    </main>
  );
}
2.13 Admin dashboard
"use client";

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

type AdminDashboard = {
  total_users: number;
  active_users: number;
  suspended_users: number;
  recent_admin_events: {
    id: string;
    action: string;
    target_user_id: string | null;
    created_at: string;
  }[];
};

export default function AdminDashboardPage() {
  const [data, setData] =
    useState<AdminDashboard | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    async function load() {
      const token =
        localStorage.getItem(
          "admin_access_token"
        );

      if (!token) {
        window.location.href = "/login";
        return;
      }

      const response = await fetch(
        `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/admin/dashboard`,
        {
          headers: {
            Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
          },
          cache: "no-store",
        }
      );

      if (response.status === 401 ||
          response.status === 403) {
        localStorage.removeItem(
          "admin_access_token"
        );

        window.location.href = "/login";
        return;
      }

      if (!response.ok) {
        throw new Error(
          "Unable to load administrator dashboard."
        );
      }

      setData(await response.json());
    }

    load();
  }, []);

  if (!data) {
    return <main>Loading...</main>;
  }

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>System Administration</h1>

      <section>
        <article>
          <h2>Total Users</h2>
          <strong>{data.total_users}</strong>
        </article>

        <article>
          <h2>Active Users</h2>
          <strong>{data.active_users}</strong>
        </article>

        <article>
          <h2>Suspended Users</h2>
          <strong>{data.suspended_users}</strong>
        </article>
      </section>

      <section>
        <h2>Recent Admin Activity</h2>

        {data.recent_admin_events.map((event) => (
          <article key={event.id}>
            <strong>{event.action}</strong>

            <time>
              {new Date(
                event.created_at
              ).toLocaleString()}
            </time>
          </article>
        ))}
      </section>
    </main>
  );
}
2.14 Do not rely on frontend security

This is critical.

This is not enough:

if (user.role === "SYSTEM_ADMIN") {
    showAdminMenu();
}

The real protection must be:

Browser
   ↓
API
   ↓
JWT validation
   ↓
portal validation
   ↓
role validation
   ↓
permission validation
   ↓
database authorization
   ↓
operation

The frontend only controls visibility.

The backend controls access.

ON users(status);

ON user_tasks(user_id, status);

ON notifications(user_id, read_at);

ON user_activity(user_id, created_at DESC);

);
2.16 Admin sessions

For production, do not keep only a single long-lived JWT.

Use:

Admin login
   ↓
short-lived access token
   +
rotating refresh token
   ↓
session database

Session model:

class UserSession(Base):
    __tablename__ = "user_sessions"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

    user_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

    refresh_token_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    portal: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(20),
        nullable=False,
    )

    expires_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

    revoked_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True)
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

This allows an administrator to revoke a compromised session.

2.17 Admin MFA

For a shipping system, I strongly recommend:

SYSTEM_ADMIN
      ↓

      ↓
MFA / Passkey
      ↓

And require step-up authentication for:

change administrator role
disable user
delete data
change authentication policy
change security settings
rotate sensitive credentials

A normal user cannot enter those functions through API authorization, even if they manually type the URLs.

3.0 — Production User Onboarding, Workspace & Access Management

This is the next foundation your standalone Agreement startup needs.

Right now you have:

User
  ↓
Login
  ↓
Dashboard

A shipping agreement product needs:

User
  ↓
Authentication
  ↓
Onboarding
  ↓
Create Workspace OR Join Workspace
  ↓
Workspace Membership
  ↓
Role / Permissions
  ↓
Dashboard
  ↓
Agreement features

The important change is that user identity and workspace identity become separate.

A person can belong to one or more organizations/workspaces, while access to actual agreement data is controlled through their workspace membership and permissions.

3.0.1 What this milestone adds
Onboarding
├── New user detection
├── Profile completion
├── Create workspace
├── Join workspace
├── Invitation acceptance
├── Workspace switching
└── Onboarding completion

Workspace
├── Organization profile
├── Members
├── Roles
├── Permissions
├── Invitations
├── Workspace settings
└── Security settings

Access
├── RBAC
├── Workspace membership
├── Permission checks
├── Session/workspace binding
└── Revocation

Dashboard
└── Becomes workspace-aware

3.0.5 Roles

Do not hardcode authorization decisions throughout the application.

Create database-backed roles.

class OrganizationRole(Base):
    __tablename__ = "organization_roles"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

    organization_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey(
            "organizations.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
    )

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(500)
    )

    system_role: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
    )

Possible system roles:

OWNER
ADMIN
MEMBER
VIEWER

These are application roles, not system administrators.

That distinction matters:

SYSTEM_ADMIN
    = operates the platform

ORGANIZATION_ADMIN
    = operates one customer's workspace

3.0.10 Onboarding flow

When a new real user logs in:

LOGIN
 ↓
Is profile complete?
 ├── NO → Profile Setup
 └── YES
      ↓
Does user belong to workspace?
 ├── NO → Create or Join
 └── YES
      ↓
Dashboard

Backend:

async def determine_entry_point(
    user,
    onboarding,
    memberships,
):

    if not user.email_verified:
        return "EMAIL_VERIFICATION"

    if not onboarding.profile_completed:
        return "PROFILE_SETUP"

    if not memberships:
        return "WORKSPACE_SETUP"

    if len(memberships) == 1:
        return "DASHBOARD"

    return "WORKSPACE_SELECTOR"

@router.post("/onboarding/profile")
async def complete_profile(

):

    current_user.first_name = payload.first_name.strip()

    }

3.0.13 Create workspace

Endpoint:

@router.post("/onboarding/workspace")
async def create_workspace(
    payload: CreateWorkspaceRequest,
    current_user=Depends(require_user),
    db=Depends(get_db),
):
    service = WorkspaceService(db)

    return await service.create_for_user(
        user=current_user,
        name=payload.name,
        legal_name=payload.legal_name,
        country_code=payload.country_code,
        timezone=payload.timezone,

Service:

from datetime import datetime, timezone


class WorkspaceService:

    async def create_for_user(
        self,
        *,
        user,
        name,
        legal_name,
        country_code,
        timezone,
    ):

        organization = Organization(
            name=name.strip(),
            legal_name=(
                legal_name.strip()
                if legal_name
                else None
            ),
            country_code=country_code,
            timezone=timezone,
            active=True,
            created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
            updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )

        self.db.add(organization)

        await self.db.flush()

        owner_role = await self.role_repository.get_or_create_owner_role(
            organization.id
        )

        member = OrganizationMember(
            organization_id=organization.id,
            user_id=user.id,
            role_id=owner_role.id,
            active=True,
            joined_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        )

        self.db.add(member)

        onboarding = await self.onboarding_repository.get(
            user.id
        )

        onboarding.workspace_created_or_joined = True
        onboarding.completed = True
        onboarding.completed_at = datetime.now(
            timezone.utc
        )

        await self.db.commit()

        return organization
3.0.14 Important correction

The previous code uses:

timezone

as a parameter name, which conflicts with:

from datetime import timezone

Do not ship that version.

Use:

from datetime import datetime, timezone as dt_timezone


async def create_for_user(
    self,
    *,
    user,
    name,
    legal_name,
    country_code,
    timezone_name,
):

    now = datetime.now(dt_timezone.utc)

    organization = Organization(
        name=name.strip(),
        legal_name=(
            legal_name.strip()
            if legal_name
            else None
        ),
        country_code=country_code,
        timezone=timezone_name,
        active=True,
        created_at=now,
        updated_at=now,
    )

    ...

That is the production-safe version.

3.0.16 Invitation validation

The service should:

hash token
 ↓
find invitation
 ↓
check revoked_at
 ↓
check accepted_at
 ↓
check expiry
 ↓
check email ownership
 ↓
create membership
 ↓
mark invitation accepted
 ↓
audit
 ↓
commit

Example:

async def accept(
    self,
    *,
    token,
    user,
):

    token_hash = hash_invitation_token(token)

    invitation = await self.repository.find_by_hash(
        token_hash
    )

    if not invitation:
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    if invitation.revoked_at:
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    if invitation.accepted_at:
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    if invitation.expires_at <= self.clock.now():
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    if invitation.email.lower() != user.email.lower():
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    existing = await self.membership_repository.get(
        invitation.organization_id,
        user.id,
    )

    if existing:
        raise AlreadyMember()

    membership = OrganizationMember(
        organization_id=invitation.organization_id,
        user_id=user.id,
        role_id=invitation.role_id,
        active=True,
        joined_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(membership)

    invitation.accepted_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.db.commit()

    return membership
3.0.17 Workspace switching

A user can belong to:

Workspace A
Workspace B
Workspace C

The session should carry the currently selected workspace.

Don't trust:

localStorage.organization_id

as authorization.

The backend must verify the membership every time.

GET /api/user/dashboard

to:

GET /api/user/dashboard?workspace_id=<uuid>

But the server must verify:

membership = await membership_repo.get(
    organization_id=workspace_id,
    user_id=current_user.id,
)

If no active membership:

403 Forbidden

Then all dashboard queries are scoped:

.where(
    UserTask.user_id == current_user.id,
    UserTask.organization_id == workspace_id,
)
3.0.20 Every business table needs workspace ownership

For example:

class Agreement(Base):
    __tablename__ = "agreements"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

    organization_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey(
            "organizations.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

    created_by: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(50),
        nullable=False,
    )

Do the same for every workspace-owned object.

This is one of the most important multi-tenant protections.

3.0.21 Permission dependency
async def require_permission(
    permission: str,
    *,
    user,
    organization_id,
    membership_repository,
    permission_service,
):

    membership = await membership_repository.get(
        organization_id=organization_id,
        user_id=user.id,
    )

    if not membership or not membership.active:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403,
            detail="Workspace access denied.",
        )

    allowed = await permission_service.has_permission(
        role_id=membership.role_id,
        permission=permission,
    )

    if not allowed:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403,
            detail="Permission denied.",
        )

    return membership
3.0.22 Agreement example
@router.post("/agreements")
async def create_agreement(
    payload: CreateAgreementRequest,
    organization_id: UUID,
    current_user=Depends(require_user),
    db=Depends(get_db),
):

    membership = await require_permission(
        "agreements.create",
        user=current_user,
        organization_id=organization_id,
        membership_repository=membership_repository,
        permission_service=permission_service,
    )

    return await agreement_service.create(
        organization_id=organization_id,
        created_by=current_user.id,
        payload=payload,
    )

Now the API cannot create an agreement in another customer's workspace just by changing an ID.

3.0.23 Row-level security

For a real SaaS deployment, add PostgreSQL RLS as defense-in-depth.

Example:

ALTER TABLE agreements ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

Then use a transaction-scoped tenant context.

Conceptually:

CREATE POLICY agreement_tenant_isolation
ON agreements
USING (
    organization_id = current_setting(
        'app.current_organization_id'
    )::uuid
);

Your backend transaction establishes:

SET LOCAL app.current_organization_id = 'actual-organization-uuid';

before querying tenant-owned records.

The application authorization layer still remains mandatory.

3.0.24 Prevent cross-workspace object access

Never implement:

agreement = await db.get(
    Agreement,
    agreement_id,
)

and immediately return it.

Instead:

agreement = await db.scalar(
    select(Agreement)
    .where(
        Agreement.id == agreement_id,
        Agreement.organization_id == organization_id,
    )
)

This simple rule prevents a large class of tenant-isolation bugs.

3.0.30 Workspace switcher
"use client";

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

type Workspace = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
};

export function WorkspaceSwitcher() {
  const [workspaces, setWorkspaces] =
    useState<Workspace[]>([]);

  const [selected, setSelected] =
    useState<string>("");

  useEffect(() => {
    async function load() {
      const token =
        localStorage.getItem(
          "user_access_token"
        );

      if (!token) return;

      const response = await fetch(
        `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/user/workspaces`,
        {
          headers: {
            Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
          },
          cache: "no-store",
        }
      );

      if (!response.ok) return;

      const data = await response.json();

      setWorkspaces(data);

      if (data.length > 0) {
        setSelected(data[0].id);
      }
    }

    load();
  }, []);

  async function switchWorkspace(
    organizationId: string
  ) {
    const token =
      localStorage.getItem(
        "user_access_token"
      );

    await fetch(
      `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/user/workspaces/${organizationId}/select`,
      {
        method: "POST",
        headers: {
          Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
        },
      }
    );

    setSelected(organizationId);

    window.location.reload();
  }

  return (
    <select
      value={selected}
      onChange={(event) =>
        switchWorkspace(
          event.target.value
        )
      }
    >
      {workspaces.map((workspace) => (
        <option
          key={workspace.id}
          value={workspace.id}
        >
          {workspace.name}
        </option>
      ))}
    </select>
  );
}

For the final production version, bind the selected workspace to the authenticated server session rather than treating the browser's selected value as trusted authorization.

This should absolutely exist:

async def test_cross_workspace_id_cannot_bypass_authorization():

    user = await create_real_test_user()

    workspace_b = await create_test_workspace()

        user=user,

3.0.38 Recommended request flow

Every business request should follow:

HTTP request
    ↓
Authentication
    ↓
User active?
    ↓
Correct portal?
    ↓
Workspace supplied/resolved
    ↓
Membership exists?
    ↓
Membership active?
    ↓
Required permission?
    ↓
Resource belongs to workspace?
    ↓
Business validation
    ↓
Database transaction
    ↓
Audit
    ↓
Response

This should become a standard pattern throughout the application.

3.1.7 Why immutable versions matter

Suppose:

Agreement #27
Version 1

gets edited.

Do not change Version 1.

Create:

Version 2

Then:

Version 1 → immutable
Version 2 → current

The history remains:

Version 1
Version 2
Version 3
Version 4

This becomes essential when you later add approvals, signatures, negotiation, or dispute evidence.

3.1.8 Hash version content

Use canonical JSON before hashing.

import hashlib
import json


def canonicalize_content(content: dict) -> bytes:
    return json.dumps(
        content,
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")


def calculate_content_hash(
    content: dict,
) -> str:

    canonical = canonicalize_content(
        content
    )

    return hashlib.sha256(
        canonical
    ).hexdigest()

Now every published version can be verified.

3.1.10 Agreement creation service
from datetime import datetime, timezone as dt_timezone


class AgreementService:

    async def create(
        self,
        *,
        actor,
        payload: CreateAgreementRequest,
    ):

        membership = await self.membership_repository.get(
            organization_id=payload.organization_id,
            user_id=actor.id,
        )

        if not membership or not membership.active:
            raise PermissionError(
                "Workspace access denied."
            )

        await self.permission_service.require(
            role_id=membership.role_id,
            permission="agreements.create",
        )

        agreement_type = await self.db.scalar(
            select(AgreementType).where(
                AgreementType.id ==
                payload.agreement_type_id,
                AgreementType.active.is_(True),
            )
        )

        if not agreement_type:
            raise ValueError(
                "Agreement type is unavailable."
            )

        now = datetime.now(dt_timezone.utc)

        agreement = Agreement(
            organization_id=payload.organization_id,
            agreement_type_id=agreement_type.id,
            title=payload.title.strip(),
            reference_number=(
                payload.reference_number.strip()
                if payload.reference_number
                else None
            ),
            description=payload.description,
            status=AgreementStatus.DRAFT,
            created_by=actor.id,
            created_at=now,
            updated_at=now,
        )

        self.db.add(agreement)

        await self.db.flush()

        initial_content = {
            "title": agreement.title,
            "description": agreement.description,
            "sections": [],
        }

        version = AgreementVersion(
            agreement_id=agreement.id,
            version_number=1,
            content=initial_content,
            content_hash=calculate_content_hash(
                initial_content
            ),
            created_by=actor.id,
            created_at=now,
        )

        self.db.add(version)

        await self.db.flush()

        agreement.current_version_id = version.id

        await self.audit.record(
            actor_id=actor.id,
            action="AGREEMENT_CREATED",
            resource_type="AGREEMENT",
            resource_id=agreement.id,
        )

        await self.db.commit()

        return agreement
3.1.11 Important transaction rule

Do not do:

create agreement
commit

then create version
commit

Use one transaction.

Otherwise you could accidentally create:

agreement exists
but
initial version missing

The code above uses one database transaction.

3.1.12 Agreement editing

Only the current draft should be editable.

class UpdateAgreementRequest(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str | None = None
    content: dict

Service:

async def update_draft(
    self,
    *,
    agreement_id,
    actor,
    expected_version_id,
    payload,
):

    agreement = await self.repository.get_for_update(
        agreement_id
    )

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=agreement.organization_id,
        permission="agreements.update",
    )

    if agreement.status != AgreementStatus.DRAFT:
        raise ValueError(
            "Only draft agreements can be directly edited."
        )

    if (
        agreement.current_version_id
        != expected_version_id
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            "Agreement version has changed."
        )

    current_version = await self.version_repository.get(
        expected_version_id
    )

    next_number = current_version.version_number + 1

    content = payload.content

    new_version = AgreementVersion(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        version_number=next_number,
        content=content,
        content_hash=calculate_content_hash(
            content
        ),
        created_by=actor.id,
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
        parent_version_id=current_version.id,
    )

    self.db.add(new_version)

    agreement.title = payload.title.strip()
    agreement.description = payload.description
    agreement.current_version_id = new_version.id
    agreement.updated_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.db.commit()

    return new_version
3.1.13 Optimistic concurrency

This protects against:

User A editing
+
User B editing

at the same time.

Request includes:

{
  "expected_version_id": "actual-version-uuid"
}

If another user has created Version 6 after the client loaded Version 5:

Client expects Version 5
Actual current = Version 6

Return:

409 Conflict

The frontend then asks the user to refresh/review the newer version.

if payload.organization_id:

    organization = await db.scalar(
        select(Organization)

            OrganizationMember,
            OrganizationMember.organization_id
            == Organization.id,

3.1.18 Search

Start with PostgreSQL full-text search.

ALTER TABLE agreements
ADD COLUMN search_vector tsvector
GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
    to_tsvector(
        'simple',
        coalesce(title, '') || ' ' ||
        coalesce(description, '')
    )
) STORED;

Index:

CREATE INDEX ix_agreements_search_vector
ON agreements
USING GIN(search_vector);

Search:

from sqlalchemy import func


query = select(Agreement).where(
    Agreement.organization_id == workspace_id,
    Agreement.search_vector.op("@@")(
        func.plainto_tsquery(
            "simple",
            search_text,
        )
    ),
)

This is real database search, not a list generated in the frontend.

3.1.21 Version comparison

Do not simply compare strings.

Represent changes structurally.

class ContentChange(BaseModel):
    path: str
    change_type: str
    before: object | None = None
    after: object | None = None

Example:

{
  "path": "sections.2.title",
  "change_type": "MODIFIED",
  "before": "Payment Terms",
  "after": "Payment and Billing Terms"
}

This can later feed your negotiation UI.

3.1.22 Version diff service
def compare_content(
    old: dict,
    new: dict,
):
    changes = []

    old_sections = old.get("sections", [])
    new_sections = new.get("sections", [])

    max_len = max(
        len(old_sections),
        len(new_sections),
    )

    for index in range(max_len):

        if index >= len(old_sections):
            changes.append(
                ContentChange(
                    path=f"sections.{index}",
                    change_type="ADDED",
                    after=new_sections[index],
                )
            )
            continue

        if index >= len(new_sections):
            changes.append(
                ContentChange(
                    path=f"sections.{index}",
                    change_type="REMOVED",
                    before=old_sections[index],
                )
            )
            continue

        if old_sections[index] != new_sections[index]:
            changes.append(
                ContentChange(
                    path=f"sections.{index}",
                    change_type="MODIFIED",
                    before=old_sections[index],
                    after=new_sections[index],
                )
            )

    return changes

This is a simple starting point. The production version can use a richer JSON structural diff library after evaluating it.

3.1.23 Validation

Before a draft moves to review:

class AgreementValidator:

    async def validate(
        self,
        agreement,
        version,
    ):

        errors = []

        if not agreement.title.strip():
            errors.append("TITLE_REQUIRED")

        if not version.content:
            errors.append(
                "AGREEMENT_CONTENT_REQUIRED"
            )

        parties = await self.party_repo.list(
            agreement.id
        )

        if len(parties) < 2:
            errors.append(
                "AT_LEAST_TWO_PARTIES_REQUIRED"
            )

        return errors

Do not hardcode a two-party rule if your product will support one-party documents. Make this configurable by agreement type.

A better design is:

agreement_type.require_multiple_parties

Then validation follows actual product configuration.

3.1.25 Status transitions

Do not allow arbitrary status changes.

ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS = {
    "DRAFT": {"IN_REVIEW"},
    "IN_REVIEW": {
        "DRAFT",
        "READY",
    },
    "READY": {
        "IN_REVIEW",
        "ARCHIVED",
    },
    "ARCHIVED": set(),
}

Service:

def validate_transition(
    current: str,
    target: str,
):

    if target not in ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.get(
        current,
        set(),
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid transition: "
            f"{current} -> {target}"
        )

Service:

async def submit_review(
    self,
    *,
    agreement_id,
    workspace_id,
    actor,
):

    agreement = await self.repository.get_for_update(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
        permission="agreements.update",
    )

    if agreement.status != "DRAFT":
        raise InvalidTransition()

    version = await self.version_repository.get(
        agreement.current_version_id
    )

    errors = await self.validator.validate(
        agreement,
        version,
    )

    if errors:
        raise ValidationError(
            errors
        )

    agreement.status = "IN_REVIEW"

    await self.audit.record(
        actor_id=actor.id,
        action="AGREEMENT_SUBMITTED_FOR_REVIEW",
        resource_type="AGREEMENT",
        resource_id=agreement.id,
    )

    await self.db.commit()

    return agreement

3.1.30 Draft autosave

The frontend can autosave, but the backend remains authoritative.

async function saveDraft(data: DraftAgreement) {
  const response = await fetch(
    `${API_URL}/api/agreements/${data.id}`,
    {
      method: "PATCH",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        ...data,
        expected_version_id:
          data.versionId,
      }),
    }
  );

  if (response.status === 409) {
    throw new Error(
      "This agreement was changed elsewhere."
    );
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(
      "Unable to save agreement."
    );
  }

  return response.json();
}

Use debouncing in the frontend to avoid sending a request for every keystroke.

3.1.33 Agreement repository

Create a repository abstraction.

class AgreementRepository:

    def __init__(self, db):
        self.db = db

    async def get(
        self,
        *,
        agreement_id,
        organization_id,
    ):

        return await self.db.scalar(
            select(Agreement)
            .where(
                Agreement.id == agreement_id,
                Agreement.organization_id
                == organization_id,
            )
        )

    async def list(
        self,
        *,
        organization_id,
        status=None,
        limit=50,
        offset=0,
    ):

        query = (
            select(Agreement)
            .where(
                Agreement.organization_id
                == organization_id
            )
        )

        if status:
            query = query.where(
                Agreement.status == status
            )

        query = (
            query
            .order_by(
                Agreement.updated_at.desc()
            )
            .offset(offset)
            .limit(limit)
        )

        return (
            await self.db.scalars(query)
        ).all()
3.1.34 Deletion

For a shipping product, avoid immediately physically deleting agreements through the regular user interface.

Instead:

ACTIVE
 ↓
ARCHIVED

and maintain controlled deletion/retention policies later.

For now:

@router.post(
    "/agreements/{agreement_id}/archive"
)

This prevents accidental destructive deletion.

3.1.35 Archive service
async def archive(
    self,
    *,
    agreement_id,
    actor,
    workspace_id,
):

    agreement = await self.repository.get(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
        permission="agreements.delete",
    )

    if agreement.status == "ARCHIVED":
        return agreement

    agreement.status = "ARCHIVED"
    agreement.archived_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.audit.record(
        actor_id=actor.id,
        action="AGREEMENT_ARCHIVED",
        resource_type="AGREEMENT",
        resource_id=agreement.id,
    )

    await self.db.commit()

    return agreement

3.2 — Agreement Content Editor & Structured Document Builder

This milestone builds the actual agreement editing experience on top of 3.1.

The core architecture becomes:

Agreement
   ↓
Current Version
   ↓
Structured Document
   ↓
Sections / Blocks
   ↓
Rich Content
   ↓
Autosave
   ↓
Validation
   ↓
New Immutable Version

The important rule is:

The editor edits a draft representation; once a version is saved/published, its content and hash are immutable.

3.2.1 What this milestone adds
Agreement Editor
├── Title
├── Sections
├── Paragraphs
├── Headings

├── Structured JSON schema

3.2.2 Do not store the document as raw HTML

Avoid:

content = "<h1>Agreement</h1><p>...</p>"

as the authoritative representation.

Use a structured document model.

Example:

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "actual-block-id",
      "type": "heading",
      "level": 1,
      "text": "Agreement"
    },
    {
      "id": "actual-block-id",
      "type": "paragraph",
      "text": "Actual user-entered content."
    }
  ]
}

This makes future:

DOCX generation
PDF rendering
redlining
search
section analysis
AI extraction

much easier.

3.2.3 Document block model

Create:

backend/app/document_editor/
├── models.py
├── schemas.py
├── validator.py
├── normalizer.py
├── service.py
├── repository.py
├── renderer.py
└── router.py
3.2.4 Block types

Start with a controlled set.

from enum import StrEnum


class BlockType(StrEnum):
    HEADING = "heading"
    PARAGRAPH = "paragraph"
    BULLET_LIST = "bullet_list"
    NUMBERED_LIST = "numbered_list"
    TABLE = "table"
    QUOTE = "quote"
    DIVIDER = "divider"

Don't allow arbitrary executable content or arbitrary embedded HTML.

3.2.5 Pydantic document schema
from typing import Literal
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class TextMarks(BaseModel):
    bold: bool = False
    italic: bool = False
    underline: bool = False


class TextRun(BaseModel):
    text: str
    marks: TextMarks = TextMarks()


class HeadingBlock(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    type: Literal["heading"]
    level: int = Field(ge=1, le=6)
    runs: list[TextRun]


class ParagraphBlock(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    type: Literal["paragraph"]
    runs: list[TextRun]


class ListItem(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    runs: list[TextRun]


class ListBlock(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    type: Literal[
        "bullet_list",
        "numbered_list",
    ]
    items: list[ListItem]


class TableCell(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    runs: list[TextRun]


class TableRow(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    cells: list[TableCell]


class TableBlock(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    type: Literal["table"]
    rows: list[TableRow]


class QuoteBlock(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    type: Literal["quote"]
    runs: list[TextRun]


class DividerBlock(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    type: Literal["divider"]


DocumentBlock = (
    HeadingBlock
    | ParagraphBlock
    | ListBlock
    | TableBlock
    | QuoteBlock
    | DividerBlock
)


class AgreementDocument(BaseModel):
    schema_version: int = 1
    blocks: list[DocumentBlock]
3.2.6 Why blocks need IDs

Each section/block needs a stable ID.

Example:

paragraph
    id = actual UUID

paragraph
    id = actual UUID

heading
    id = actual UUID

Without stable IDs, later comparison becomes much harder.

You need to know:

same paragraph changed

versus:

old paragraph removed
new paragraph added
3.2.7 Database storage

The structured document remains inside the agreement version.

You already have:

AgreementVersion.content

So don't duplicate the full document into another table unless required for a specific query.

Use:

AgreementVersion
   └── content JSONB

Add schema validation before persistence.

3.2.8 JSONB

PostgreSQL should use JSONB.

from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB

Then:

content: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
    JSONB,
    nullable=False,
)

This is preferable to storing arbitrary document text in a large text field.

3.2.9 Document validator

Create:

class DocumentValidator:

    def validate(
        self,
        document: AgreementDocument,
    ) -> list[str]:

        errors: list[str] = []

        if document.schema_version != 1:
            errors.append(
                "UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION"
            )

        for block in document.blocks:

            if hasattr(block, "runs"):
                for run in block.runs:
                    if not run.text:
                        errors.append(
                            f"EMPTY_TEXT_RUN:{block.id}"
                        )

            if block.type == "table":
                if not block.rows:
                    errors.append(
                        f"EMPTY_TABLE:{block.id}"
                    )

        return errors
3.2.10 Normalize the document

Users can generate structurally messy editor content.

Normalize before saving:

class DocumentNormalizer:

    def normalize(
        self,
        document: AgreementDocument,
    ) -> AgreementDocument:

        normalized_blocks = []

        for block in document.blocks:

            if block.type == "paragraph":

                if (
                    len(block.runs) == 1
                    and not block.runs[0].text.strip()
                ):
                    continue

            normalized_blocks.append(block)

        return document.model_copy(
            update={
                "blocks": normalized_blocks
            }
        )

This avoids storing unnecessary empty blocks.

3.2.11 Canonical serialization

Use one canonical representation for hashing.

import json


def canonical_document(
    document: AgreementDocument,
) -> bytes:

    payload = document.model_dump(
        mode="json"
    )

    return json.dumps(
        payload,
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")

Hash:

import hashlib


def document_hash(
    document: AgreementDocument,
) -> str:

    return hashlib.sha256(
        canonical_document(document)
    ).hexdigest()

3.2.13 Document service
class DocumentEditorService:

    async def update(
        self,
        *,
        agreement_id,
        workspace_id,
        actor,
        expected_version_id,
        document,
    ):

        agreement = await self.agreement_repo.get_for_update(
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            organization_id=workspace_id,
        )

        if not agreement:
            raise NotFoundError(
                "Agreement not found."
            )

        await self.authorization.require(
            actor=actor,
            organization_id=workspace_id,
            permission="agreements.update",
        )

        if agreement.status != "DRAFT":
            raise DomainError(
                "Only draft agreements can be edited."
            )

        if (
            agreement.current_version_id
            != expected_version_id
        ):
            raise ConflictError(
                "Agreement has changed. Refresh before saving."
            )

        document = self.normalizer.normalize(
            document
        )

        errors = self.validator.validate(
            document
        )

        if errors:
            raise ValidationError(errors)

        current_version = (
            await self.version_repo.get(
                agreement.current_version_id
            )
        )

        next_version = (
            current_version.version_number + 1
        )

        version = AgreementVersion(
            agreement_id=agreement.id,
            version_number=next_version,
            content=document.model_dump(
                mode="json"
            ),
            content_hash=document_hash(
                document
            ),
            created_by=actor.id,
            created_at=self.clock.now(),
            parent_version_id=current_version.id,
        )

        self.db.add(version)

        await self.db.flush()

        agreement.current_version_id = version.id
        agreement.updated_at = self.clock.now()

        await self.audit.record(
            actor_id=actor.id,
            action="AGREEMENT_DOCUMENT_UPDATED",
            resource_type="AGREEMENT",
            resource_id=agreement.id,
            metadata={
                "version_id": str(version.id),
            },
        )

        await self.db.commit()

        return version
3.2.14 Autosave architecture

Don't save every keystroke immediately.

Use:

Editor change
   ↓
300–1000 ms debounce
   ↓
local editor state
   ↓
autosave request
   ↓
version check
   ↓
server save

Example:

import { useEffect } from "react";

useEffect(() => {
  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    saveDraft(currentDocument);
  }, 800);

  return () => clearTimeout(timer);
}, [currentDocument]);

The exact interval should be configurable after observing actual load/performance.

3.2.15 Don't create a permanent version on every keystroke

This would create:

Version 1
Version 2
Version 3
Version 4
...
Version 8,923

Instead distinguish:

EDITOR_DRAFT_STATE

from:

IMMUTABLE_AGREEMENT_VERSION
3.2.16 Draft editing state

Add:

class AgreementDraftState(Base):
    __tablename__ = "agreement_draft_states"

    id: Mapped[UUID]

    agreement_id: Mapped[UUID]

    editor_user_id: Mapped[UUID]

    base_version_id: Mapped[UUID]

    content: Mapped[dict]

    content_hash: Mapped[str]

    updated_at: Mapped[datetime]

This allows continuous autosave without polluting the legal version history.

3.2.17 Draft state uniqueness
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_agreement_draft_editor
ON agreement_draft_states(
    agreement_id,
    editor_user_id
);

This means each editor can have one current autosave state.

3.2.19 Autosave service
async def autosave(
    self,
    *,
    agreement_id,
    workspace_id,
    actor,
    base_version_id,
    document,
):

    agreement = await self.agreement_repo.get(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    if agreement.status != "DRAFT":
        raise DomainError(
            "Agreement is no longer editable."
        )

    if (
        agreement.current_version_id
        != base_version_id
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            "Base version is no longer current."
        )

    document = self.normalizer.normalize(
        document
    )

    errors = self.validator.validate(
        document
    )

    if errors:
        raise ValidationError(errors)

    state = await self.draft_repo.get(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        editor_user_id=actor.id,
    )

    if not state:
        state = AgreementDraftState(
            id=uuid4(),
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            editor_user_id=actor.id,
            base_version_id=base_version_id,
            content=document.model_dump(
                mode="json"
            ),
            content_hash=document_hash(
                document
            ),
            updated_at=self.clock.now(),
        )

        self.db.add(state)

    else:
        state.base_version_id = base_version_id
        state.content = document.model_dump(
            mode="json"
        )
        state.content_hash = document_hash(
            document
        )
        state.updated_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.db.commit()

    return {
        "saved": True,
        "base_version_id": str(
            base_version_id
        ),
        "saved_at": state.updated_at,
    }

3.2.22 Finalization
async def finalize(
    self,
    *,
    agreement_id,
    workspace_id,
    actor,
    expected_base_version_id,
):

    agreement = await self.repository.get_for_update(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    draft = await self.draft_repo.get(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        editor_user_id=actor.id,
    )

    if not draft:
        raise DomainError(
            "No editable draft found."
        )

    if (
        agreement.current_version_id
        != expected_base_version_id
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            "Agreement changed while editing."
        )

    document = AgreementDocument.model_validate(
        draft.content
    )

    errors = self.validator.validate(
        document
    )

    if errors:
        raise ValidationError(errors)

    current = await self.version_repo.get(
        agreement.current_version_id
    )

    version = AgreementVersion(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        version_number=current.version_number + 1,
        content=document.model_dump(
            mode="json"
        ),
        content_hash=document_hash(
            document
        ),
        created_by=actor.id,
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
        parent_version_id=current.id,
    )

    self.db.add(version)

    await self.db.flush()

    agreement.current_version_id = version.id
    agreement.updated_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.db.delete(draft)

    await self.audit.record(
        actor_id=actor.id,
        action="AGREEMENT_VERSION_CREATED",
        resource_type="AGREEMENT",
        resource_id=agreement.id,
        metadata={
            "version_id": str(version.id),
            "content_hash": version.content_hash,
        },
    )

    await self.db.commit()

    return version
3.2.23 Frontend editor

Use a mature structured editor rather than building a text editor from scratch.

The important abstraction is:

Editor UI
   ↓
Structured document JSON
   ↓
API

Example editor component:

type AgreementDocument = {
  schema_version: number;
  blocks: DocumentBlock[];
};

type DocumentEditorProps = {
  value: AgreementDocument;
  onChange: (value: AgreementDocument) => void;
};

export function DocumentEditor({
  value,
  onChange,
}: DocumentEditorProps) {
  return (
    <div>
      {value.blocks.map((block) => (
        <EditorBlock
          key={String(block.id)}
          block={block}
          onChange={(updated) => {
            onChange({
              ...value,
              blocks: value.blocks.map((item) =>
                String(item.id) ===
                String(block.id)
                  ? updated
                  : item
              ),
            });
          }}
        />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
3.2.24 Block rendering
function EditorBlock({
  block,
  onChange,
}: {
  block: DocumentBlock;
  onChange: (block: DocumentBlock) => void;
}) {
  switch (block.type) {
    case "heading":
      return (
        <input
          value={block.runs
            .map((run) => run.text)
            .join("")}
          onChange={(event) =>
            onChange({
              ...block,
              runs: [
                {
                  text: event.target.value,
                  marks: {},
                },
              ],
            })
          }
        />
      );

    case "paragraph":
      return (
        <textarea
          value={block.runs
            .map((run) => run.text)
            .join("")}
          onChange={(event) =>
            onChange({
              ...block,
              runs: [
                {
                  text: event.target.value,
                  marks: {},
                },
              ],
            })
          }
        />
      );

    default:
      return null;
  }
}

This is the conceptual rendering layer. For production UX, use a proper rich-text editor library mapped into your document schema rather than shipping this minimal textarea implementation.

3.2.28 Document validation UI

Document cannot be submitted.

3.2.29 Agreement-type-specific structure

Your agreement_type_rules from 3.1 can now determine expected sections.

For example, the configured agreement type can specify:

{
  "required_sections": [
    "parties",
    "scope",
    "term"
  ]
}

Then:

required = await rule_service.required_sections(
    agreement.agreement_type_id
)

Validate actual document structure against those configured rules.

3.2.30 Do not hardcode legal sections

Avoid:

REQUIRED_SECTIONS = [
    "scope",
    "payment",
    "termination",
]

globally.

Different products and agreement types will need different structures.

Use actual database-backed product configuration.

3.2.31 Document preview

Provide:

Edit
Preview

The same structured JSON should feed a renderer.

class DocumentRenderer:

    def render_html(
        self,
        document: AgreementDocument,
    ) -> str:

        output = []

        for block in document.blocks:

            if block.type == "heading":
                text = "".join(
                    run.text
                    for run in block.runs
                )

                output.append(
                    f"<h{block.level}>"
                    f"{escape(text)}"
                    f"</h{block.level}>"
                )

            elif block.type == "paragraph":
                text = "".join(
                    run.text
                    for run in block.runs
                )

                output.append(
                    f"<p>{escape(text)}</p>"
                )

        return "".join(output)

Always escape user-entered content.

Never directly concatenate untrusted HTML.

3.2.32 Rendering safety

Never do:

return user_html

because that can introduce:

XSS
script injection
malicious links
unsafe embedded content

The renderer should generate HTML from your controlled document schema.

3.2.35 Structural diff

Because blocks have IDs:

def diff_documents(
    before: AgreementDocument,
    after: AgreementDocument,
):

    before_map = {
        str(block.id): block
        for block in before.blocks
    }

    after_map = {
        str(block.id): block
        for block in after.blocks
    }

    changes = []

    for block_id, old in before_map.items():

        if block_id not in after_map:
            changes.append({
                "type": "REMOVED",
                "block_id": block_id,
            })
            continue

        if old != after_map[block_id]:
            changes.append({
                "type": "MODIFIED",
                "block_id": block_id,
                "before": old.model_dump(
                    mode="json"
                ),
                "after": after_map[
                    block_id
                ].model_dump(
                    mode="json"
                ),
            })

    for block_id, new in after_map.items():

        if block_id not in before_map:
            changes.append({
                "type": "ADDED",
                "block_id": block_id,
                "after": new.model_dump(
                    mode="json"
                ),
            })

    return changes

This becomes the foundation for later redlining.

3.2.36 Editor collaboration

Don't attempt full real-time collaborative editing yet.

For the shipping version, start with:

User A opens document
        ↓
User B also opens document
        ↓
A saves
        ↓
B receives "new version available"
        ↓
B reviews
        ↓
B updates from latest version

This is safer than naïve last-write-wins behavior.

3.2.37 WebSocket event

Reuse your existing real-time infrastructure.

Event:

{
  "type": "AGREEMENT_VERSION_CREATED",
  "agreement_id": "actual-id",
  "version_id": "actual-id"
}

The notification payload should not expose document content unnecessarily.

@router.get(
    "/agreements/{agreement_id}/draft"
)
async def get_draft(
    agreement_id: UUID,
    current_user=Depends(require_user),
):

    draft = await draft_repo.get(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,

3.2.48 Important production rule

There are now three different things:

1. Draft state
   → editable

2. Agreement version
   → immutable snapshot

3. Rendered document
   → derived output

Never confuse them.

Architecture:

                  Agreement
                     │
                     ▼
             Current Version
                     │
              ┌──────┴──────┐
              ▼             ▼
         Structured       Hash
          Document
              │
       ┌──────┴──────┐
       ▼             ▼
      HTML          Later DOCX/PDF
   rendering          rendering

Draft:

Editor
  ↓
DraftState
  ↓
Finalize
  ↓
ImmutableVersion
3.2.49 Real-data requirement

There is no production data embedded in this architecture.

The document content must come from:

actual user input
actual uploaded document
actual configured template
actual approved content

Not:

fake agreement
demo clause
synthetic customer
fake party
placeholder legal text

The only generated values such as UUIDs, timestamps, hashes, and internal identifiers are system-generated technical values, not fabricated business information.

3.2.50 What 3.2 gives the product

The Agreement startup now has:

Real user
    ↓
Real workspace
    ↓
Real agreement
    ↓
Real parties
    ↓
Structured document
    ↓
Draft editor
    ↓
Autosave
    ↓
Validation
    ↓
Immutable version
    ↓
Hash
    ↓
Preview
    ↓
Version comparison

That is the first point where the application becomes a real agreement-authoring product, rather than just a database for agreement records.

3.3 — Templates, Reusable Agreement Types & Document Generation

This milestone builds the template system on top of 3.2.

The goal is:

User
 ↓
Create Agreement
 ↓
Choose configured Agreement Type
 ↓
Choose available Template
 ↓
Load template version
 ↓
Fill actual data
 ↓
Generate structured document
 ↓
Edit
 ↓
Save draft
 ↓
Create immutable version

The critical rule remains:

Templates are versioned configuration. They must never silently change an existing agreement.

A template update affects new documents, not documents already created from an older template version.

3.3.1 Architecture

Add:

backend/app/templates/
├── models.py
├── schemas.py
├── repository.py
├── service.py
├── validator.py
├── renderer.py
├── compiler.py
├── variables.py
└── router.py

Frontend:

web/app/
├── templates/
│   ├── page.tsx
│   ├── new/
│   ├── [id]/
│   └── [id]/versions/
│
└── agreements/
    └── new/
        └── template/
3.3.2 Template lifecycle

Use:

DRAFT
 ↓
REVIEW
 ↓
PUBLISHED
 ↓
RETIRED

Never edit a published template in place.

Instead:

Template
 ├── Version 1 → retired
 ├── Version 2 → published
 └── Version 3 → draft

3.3.5 Template variables

Templates often contain variable fields.

For example:

{{ party_a_name }}
{{ party_b_name }}
{{ effective_date }}
{{ agreement_reference }}

Do not implement this using arbitrary Jinja/Python execution.

Create a controlled variable system.

class TemplateVariable(Base):
    __tablename__ = "template_variables"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

    template_version_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey(
            "template_versions.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
    )

    key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(150),
        nullable=False,
    )

    label: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    data_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(50),
        nullable=False,
    )

    required: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
    )

    source_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(50),
        nullable=False,
    )

Possible source types:

USER_INPUT
WORKSPACE

3.3.8 Template variable resolution

Create:

class TemplateContextResolver:

    async def resolve(
        self,
        *,
        template_version,
        agreement,
        actor,
    ):

        variables = {}

        for definition in (
            await self.variable_repo.list(
                template_version.id
            )
        ):

            variables[
                definition.key
            ] = await self.resolve_one(
                definition=definition,
                agreement=agreement,
                actor=actor,
            )

        return variables

The important part is resolve_one().

3.3.9 Real data resolution

Example:

async def resolve_one(
    self,
    *,
    definition,
    agreement,
    actor,
):

    if definition.source_type == "AGREEMENT":

        return await self.agreement_data.resolve(
            definition.key,
            agreement.id,
        )

    if definition.source_type == "PARTY":

        return await self.party_data.resolve(
            definition.key,
            agreement.id,
        )

    if definition.source_type == "WORKSPACE":

        return await self.workspace_data.resolve(
            definition.key,
            agreement.organization_id,
        )

    if definition.source_type == "USER_INPUT":

        return None

    raise ValueError(
        f"Unsupported variable source: "
        f"{definition.source_type}"
    )

No made-up data.

Missing required values remain missing.

3.3.10 Required variables

Suppose the template requires:

party_a_name
party_b_name
effective_date

but the agreement has no effective date.

Do not generate:

2026-09-01

because that date would be fabricated.

Return:

{
  "status": "INCOMPLETE",
  "missing_variables": [
    "effective_date"
  ]
}
3.3.11 Template compiler

The compiler takes:

Template Version
+
Real Context
+
Explicit User Inputs

and produces:

Structured Agreement Document

Compiler:

class TemplateCompiler:

    def __init__(
        self,
        validator,
        variable_resolver,
        normalizer,
    ):
        self.validator = validator
        self.variable_resolver = variable_resolver
        self.normalizer = normalizer

    async def compile(
        self,
        *,
        template_version,
        agreement,
        actor,
        user_inputs,
    ):

        context = (
            await self.variable_resolver.resolve(
                template_version=template_version,
                agreement=agreement,
                actor=actor,
            )
        )

        context.update(user_inputs)

        self.validator.validate_context(
            template_version,
            context,
        )

        output = self.render_document(
            template_version.document_schema,
            context,
        )

        document = self.normalizer.normalize(
            output
        )

        self.validator.validate_document(
            document
        )

        return document
3.3.12 Never use arbitrary template code execution

Avoid:

eval(template)

and:

exec(template)

and unrestricted:

template.render(**globals())

Templates must operate on a controlled data model.

3.3.13 Template syntax

Use a restricted syntax such as:

{{ variable }}

and conditional structures:

{{#if optional_section}}
...
{{/if}}

The parser should allow only known operations.

Example AST:

{
  "type": "variable",
  "key": "party_a_name"
}

or:

{
  "type": "conditional",
  "condition": {
    "variable": "has_schedule"
  },
  "children": []
}

No arbitrary expressions.

3.3.14 Template block

Extend the document schema with:

class TemplateParagraph(BaseModel):
    id: UUID
    type: Literal["paragraph"]
    runs: list[
        TextRun | TemplateVariableRun
    ]

Variable run:

class TemplateVariableRun(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["variable"]
    key: str
