3.3.17 Create template service
async def create_template(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    payload,
):

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=payload.organization_id,
        permission="templates.create",
    )

    agreement_type = await self.agreement_type_repo.get(
        payload.agreement_type_id
    )

    if not agreement_type:
        raise NotFoundError(
            "Agreement type not found."
        )

    template = Template(
        organization_id=payload.organization_id,
        agreement_type_id=payload.agreement_type_id,
        name=payload.name.strip(),
        description=payload.description,
        active=True,
        created_by=actor.id,
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
        updated_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(template)

    await self.db.commit()

    return template
3.3.18 Template version creation
async def create_version(
    self,
    *,
    template_id,
    actor,
    document_schema,
):

    template = await self.template_repo.get(
        template_id
    )

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=template.organization_id,
        permission="templates.update",
    )

    latest = await self.version_repo.latest(
        template_id
    )

    next_number = (
        latest.version_number + 1
        if latest
        else 1
    )

    content_hash = hash_json(
        document_schema
    )

    version = TemplateVersion(
        template_id=template.id,
        version_number=next_number,
        document_schema=document_schema,
        content_hash=content_hash,
        status="DRAFT",
        created_by=actor.id,
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(version)

    await self.db.commit()

    return version
3.3.19 Publish template
async def publish_template_version(
    self,
    *,
    template_version_id,
    actor,
):

    version = await self.version_repo.get(
        template_version_id
    )

    template = await self.template_repo.get(
        version.template_id
    )

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=template.organization_id,
        permission="templates.publish",
    )

    if version.status != "DRAFT":
        raise DomainError(
            "Only draft template versions can be published."
        )

    await self.template_validator.validate(
        version
    )

    current = await self.version_repo.current_published(
        template.id
    )

    if current:
        current.status = "RETIRED"

    version.status = "PUBLISHED"
    version.published_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.db.commit()

    return version
3.3.20 Critical template immutability

Never:

published_template.document_schema = new_schema

A published version must never be edited.

Create:

Version 2

instead.

3.3.22 Template selection query
query = (
    select(Template)
    .join(
        TemplateVersion,
        TemplateVersion.template_id
        == Template.id,
    )
    .where(
        Template.organization_id
        == workspace_id,
        Template.agreement_type_id
        == agreement_type_id,
        Template.active.is_(True),
        TemplateVersion.status == "PUBLISHED",
    )
    .distinct()
)

This prevents unpublished templates from being used.

3.3.24 Validate template belongs to the workspace

Never trust only the submitted IDs.

template = await db.scalar(
    select(Template)
    .join(
        Organization,
        Organization.id
        == Template.organization_id,
    )
    .where(
        Template.id == template_id,
        Template.organization_id
        == workspace_id,
    )
)

if not template:
    raise NotFoundError(
        "Template not found."
    )

Then confirm:

template.agreement_type_id == payload.agreement_type_id

and:

template_version.template_id == template.id
3.3.25 Generate flow
async def generate_from_template(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    workspace_id,
    payload,
):

    template = await self.template_repo.get_authorized(
        template_id=payload.template_version_id,
        workspace_id=workspace_id,
    )

    template_version = (
        await self.version_repo.get(
            payload.template_version_id
        )
    )

    if template_version.status != "PUBLISHED":
        raise DomainError(
            "Template version is not published."
        )

    agreement = await self.agreement_service.create(
        actor=actor,
        payload=CreateAgreementRequest(
            organization_id=workspace_id,
            agreement_type_id=payload.agreement_type_id,
            title=payload.title,
        ),
    )

    document = await self.compiler.compile(
        template_version=template_version,
        agreement=agreement,
        actor=actor,
        user_inputs=payload.user_inputs,
    )

    await self.document_service.save_generated_draft(
        agreement=agreement,
        document=document,
        template_version_id=template_version.id,
        actor=actor,
    )

    return agreement

3.3.30 Dynamic form renderer
type VariableDefinition = {
  key: string;
  label: string;
  data_type: string;
  required: boolean;
  source_type: string;
};

function VariableField({
  variable,
  value,
  onChange,
}: {
  variable: VariableDefinition;
  value: unknown;
  onChange: (value: unknown) => void;
}) {
  switch (variable.data_type) {
    case "DATE":
      return (
        <input
          type="date"
          required={variable.required}
          value={(value as string) ?? ""}
          onChange={(event) =>
            onChange(event.target.value)
          }
        />
      );

    case "BOOLEAN":
      return (
        <input
          type="checkbox"
          checked={Boolean(value)}
          onChange={(event) =>
            onChange(event.target.checked)
          }
        />
      );

    default:
      return (
        <input
          type="text"
          required={variable.required}
          value={(value as string) ?? ""}
          onChange={(event) =>
            onChange(event.target.value)
          }
        />
      );
  }
}

3.3.37 Compiler failure handling

Suppose a required variable is unavailable.

Return:

{
  "status": "INCOMPLETE",
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "REQUIRED_VALUE_MISSING",
      "variable": "effective_date"
    }
  ]
}

Don't generate a partial production document containing:

TBD
INSERT DATE
[CLIENT NAME]
<COMPANY>

unless those are explicitly intended editable fields in your product.

3.3.38 No unresolved production placeholders

Before a document can be moved to review:

remaining = compiler.find_unresolved_variables(
    document
)

if remaining:
    raise DomainError(
        "Document contains unresolved variables."
    )

This gives you:

Draft generated
   ↓
Unresolved variables?
   ├── YES → block review
   └── NO
         ↓
       Review
3.3.39 Generated content can still be edited

Templates provide the starting structure.

After generation:

Template Version 4
       ↓
Generated Draft
       ↓
User edits
       ↓
Draft state
       ↓
Agreement Version 1

Once editing begins, the agreement becomes its own document.

Changing the template later does not retroactively modify it.

3.3.41 Template validation

Validation should include:

✓ valid document schema
✓ known block types
✓ known variable types
✓ variable references exist
✓ no duplicated variable keys
✓ conditional references valid
✓ required metadata exists
✓ no unsupported expressions
✓ no unresolved template syntax
✓ agreement type compatibility
3.3.42 Validator
class TemplateValidator:

    async def validate(
        self,
        template_version,
    ):

        errors = []

        document = (
            AgreementDocument.model_validate(
                template_version.document_schema
            )
        )

        definitions = await self.variable_repo.list(
            template_version.id
        )

        keys = {
            definition.key
            for definition in definitions
        }

        referenced = (
            self.extract_variable_references(
                document
            )
        )

        missing_definitions = (
            referenced - keys
        )

        for key in missing_definitions:
            errors.append(
                f"UNKNOWN_VARIABLE:{key}"
            )

        duplicates = (
            len(keys)
            != len(definitions)
        )

        if duplicates:
            errors.append(
                "DUPLICATE_VARIABLE_KEYS"
            )

        if errors:
            raise ValidationError(
                errors
            )
3.3.43 Template compatibility

Make sure the template belongs to the selected agreement type.

if (
    template.agreement_type_id
    != agreement.agreement_type_id
):
    raise DomainError(
        "Template is incompatible with "
        "agreement type."
    )
3.3.44 Template ownership

A workspace must not use another workspace's private template.

Query:

select(Template)
.where(
    Template.id == template_id,
    Template.organization_id == workspace_id,
)

System-wide templates, if you later support them, should use an explicit visibility model rather than bypassing tenant checks.

3.3.45 Template visibility

Possible values:

class TemplateVisibility:
    PRIVATE = "PRIVATE"
    WORKSPACE = "WORKSPACE"
    PLATFORM = "PLATFORM"

PLATFORM templates can be distributed centrally, but the authorization layer must explicitly allow them.

3.3.46 Template provenance in agreement

Agreement:

Agreement
│
├── Created from:
│      Template ABC
│      Version 4
│      Hash XYZ
│
└── Current document
       Version 1

This is very useful for auditing and future debugging.

3.3.48 Transaction safety

Generating from a template should be atomic where practical:

create agreement
+
create template-source record
+
create generated draft
+
audit
+
outbox event

all in one transaction.

If compilation fails, do not leave behind a half-created business object unless you have explicitly designed resumable generation.

A better production approach is:

validate inputs first
 ↓
compile
 ↓
validate output
 ↓
transactionally create agreement
3.3.49 Generation service

A cleaner implementation is:

async def generate(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    workspace_id,
    payload,
):

    template_version = (
        await self.template_repo.get_published_authorized(
            template_version_id=
                payload.template_version_id,
            workspace_id=workspace_id,
            agreement_type_id=
                payload.agreement_type_id,
        )
    )

    agreement_context = (
        await self.context_service.preview_context(
            actor=actor,
            workspace_id=workspace_id,
            agreement_type_id=
                payload.agreement_type_id,
        )
    )

    document = await self.compiler.compile(
        template_version=template_version,
        agreement_context=agreement_context,
        actor=actor,
        user_inputs=payload.user_inputs,
    )

    await self.validator.validate_generated(
        document
    )

    async with self.db.begin():

        agreement = (
            await self.agreement_service.create_in_transaction(
                actor=actor,
                organization_id=workspace_id,
                agreement_type_id=
                    payload.agreement_type_id,
                title=payload.title,
            )
        )

        await self.source_repo.create(
            agreement_id=agreement.id,
            template_id=template_version.template_id,
            template_version_id=template_version.id,
            template_hash=template_version.content_hash,
        )

        await self.draft_repo.create(
            agreement_id=agreement.id,
            editor_user_id=actor.id,
            base_version_id=agreement.current_version_id,
            content=document.model_dump(
                mode="json"
            ),
            content_hash=document_hash(document),
        )

        await self.audit.record(
            actor_id=actor.id,
            action="AGREEMENT_GENERATED_FROM_TEMPLATE",
            resource_type="AGREEMENT",
            resource_id=agreement.id,
            metadata={
                "template_version_id": str(
                    template_version.id
                )
            },
        )

        await self.outbox.publish(
            event_type="AGREEMENT_GENERATED",
            aggregate_id=agreement.id,
        )

    return agreement

3.4 — Parties, Contacts & Counterparty Management

This milestone makes parties and contacts reusable first-class records instead of storing a new copy of the same company/person every time an agreement is created.

The product flow becomes:

Workspace
   ↓
Parties & Contacts
   ├── Organizations
   ├── Individuals
   ├── Contacts
   └── Relationships
          ↓
Agreement
   ├── Party A
   └── Party B

The important rule is:

A party record is reusable, but the role that party plays in a specific agreement belongs to the agreement-party relationship.

So the same company can be:

Customer

in one agreement and:

Supplier

in another.

3.4.1 What this milestone adds
Parties
├── Organization records
├── Individual records
├── Contacts
├── Addresses
├── Identifiers
├── Relationships
├── Status
└── Search

Agreement relationships
├── Link party
├── Party role
├── Primary contact
├── Agreement-specific contact
├── Party status
└── Remove/unlink

Governance
├── Duplicate detection
├── Merge workflow
├── Access control
├── Audit
└── Workspace isolation
3.4.2 Database architecture

Add:

party_organizations

3.4.3 Organization party model

Do not reuse the application's organizations table for external counterparties.

Your application workspace:

organizations

and an external business party:

party_organizations

are different concepts.

from datetime import datetime
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import (
    Boolean,
    DateTime,
    ForeignKey,
    String,
    Text,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.database import Base


class PartyOrganization(Base):
    __tablename__ = "party_organizations"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

    workspace_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey(
            "organizations.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

    legal_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    display_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
    )

    country_code: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(2),
    )

    website: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(500),
    )

    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        Text,
    )

    active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=True,
    )

    created_by: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(

        nullable=False,

    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(

3.4.5 Why organizations and individuals are separate

A company may have:

Legal entity
  ↓
many contacts

An individual is:

one person

Do not represent both through an unstructured JSON field.

It will make search, relationships, deduplication, and permissions much harder.

3.4.10 Database constraint

PostgreSQL can enforce that.

ALTER TABLE agreement_party_links
ADD CONSTRAINT ck_one_party_reference
CHECK (
    (
        party_organization_id IS NOT NULL
        AND party_individual_id IS NULL
    )
    OR
    (
        party_organization_id IS NULL
        AND party_individual_id IS NOT NULL
    )
);
3.4.11 Unique relationship

Prevent accidentally linking the same party to the same agreement twice in the same role.

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_agreement_party_org_role
ON agreement_party_links(
    agreement_id,
    party_organization_id,
    role
)
WHERE party_organization_id IS NOT NULL;

And the equivalent for individuals.

    legal_name: str = Field(
        min_length=1,
        max_length=255,

    display_name: str | None = None

    country_code: str | None = None

3.4.13 Create organization party
async def create_party_organization(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    workspace_id,
    payload,
):

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
        permission="parties.create",
    )

    now = self.clock.now()

    party = PartyOrganization(
        workspace_id=workspace_id,
        legal_name=payload.legal_name.strip(),
        display_name=(
            payload.display_name.strip()
            if payload.display_name
            else None
        ),
        country_code=payload.country_code,
        website=payload.website,
        description=payload.description,
        active=True,
        created_by=actor.id,
        created_at=now,
        updated_at=now,
    )

    self.db.add(party)

    await self.db.commit()

    return party

The party's own record does not need to change.

3.4.20 Party search

Search should operate on actual workspace data.

query = (
    select(PartyOrganization)
    .where(
        PartyOrganization.workspace_id
        == workspace_id
    )
)

if search:
    value = f"%{search.strip()}%"

    query = query.where(
        PartyOrganization.legal_name.ilike(value)
        |
        PartyOrganization.display_name.ilike(value)
    )

Later add PostgreSQL full-text indexes.

3.4.25 Duplicate detection

A shipping application needs to prevent:

Acme Corporation
ACME CORPORATION
Acme Corp.
Acme Corporation Ltd

becoming four accidental records.

Do not automatically merge them.

Instead detect candidates.

class PartyDuplicateCandidate:

    party_id: UUID
    matching_party_id: UUID
    matching_fields: list[str]
    confidence: float
3.4.26 Deterministic duplicate checks

Start with strong exact matches:

registered identifier
+
country

or:

normalized legal name
+
country

Example:

def normalize_name(value: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(
        value.lower().strip().split()
    )

Then:

candidate = await repo.find_by_identifier(
    identifier_type,
    identifier_value,
)

An exact identifier match is much stronger than name similarity.

3.4.27 Similarity detection

Later you can add a similarity service.

But:

similarity = possible duplicate

not:

similarity = same company

The user must confirm merging.

3.4.28 Merge workflow

Add:

POST /api/parties/merge-requests

Flow:

Potential duplicates
       ↓
Review
       ↓
Select canonical party
       ↓
Show affected agreements
       ↓
Confirm
       ↓
Merge
       ↓
Audit

Never silently merge records.

3.4.29 Merge constraints

A merge should preserve history.

Example:

Party A ← duplicate
Party B ← canonical

Do not delete all references from Party A without history.

Store:

class PartyMergeRecord(Base):
    __tablename__ = "party_merge_records"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

        ForeignKey("organizations.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    source_party_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("party_organizations.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    target_party_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("party_organizations.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    merged_by: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    merged_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )
3.4.30 Archive versus delete

Use:

ACTIVE
ARCHIVED

rather than deleting party records from the normal user interface.

Why?

Because historical agreements may still reference the party.

3.4.31 Contact verification

Do not treat an email address as verified simply because someone typed it.

Use:

UNVERIFIED
VERIFIED

Only mark verified after a genuine verification flow or trusted configured integration.

3.4.32 External contact invitations

If a party contact needs access to the application later:

Party contact
    ↓
Invitation
    ↓
User account

But creating a contact record must not automatically create a platform user account.

These are different entities.

3.4.36 API authorization

Every party endpoint must verify:

authenticated user
        ↓
active workspace
        ↓

        ↓

        ↓
party workspace_id

Never accept:

party_id

as sufficient authorization.

3.4.37 Agreement creation changes

3.1 originally allowed free-form party information.

Now upgrade it so the preferred process is:

existing party
OR
create new party

Then:

AgreementPartyLink

references the canonical party record.

3.4.38 Legacy migration

Existing agreement_party records, if already created from 3.1, should be migrated.

Migration strategy:

Existing agreement party
       ↓
Attempt deterministic match
       ↓
Existing party?
   ┌───┴───┐
  YES      NO
   │        │
Link      Create
   │        │
   └────┬───┘
        ↓
AgreementPartyLink

Never silently merge ambiguous matches.

3.4.39 Migration safety

Create a report:

matched_exact
created_new
ambiguous
failed

Anything ambiguous must be reviewable.

Do not invent mappings.

3.4.47 Party data quality

Add quality states:

COMPLETE
INCOMPLETE
NEEDS_REVIEW
ARCHIVED

A quality warning might say:

Party profile incomplete.

Missing:
• registered address
• organization identifier

The system should not fabricate these values.

3.4.48 Optional enrichment

Later, a real configured external provider may enrich:

legal name
registration information
registered address
corporate relationships

But the architecture must record:

provider
retrieval timestamp
source identifier
source data
verification status

External enrichment should never silently overwrite user-verified information.

3.4.49 Source precedence

When data conflicts:

User-verified data
        ↓
Trusted configured provider
        ↓
Unverified external source

The actual precedence policy should be configurable.

Do not arbitrarily overwrite the customer's data.

3.4.50 AI integration

AI can help identify:

possible duplicate
possible organization name variation
possible party classification
possible contact extraction

But:

AI says same company

should become:

DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE

not:

MERGED

without the appropriate deterministic validation and user/administrator action.

 ├── Commercial activity

3.5 — Agreement Sharing, Invitations & Controlled Collaboration

This milestone adds secure collaboration around an individual agreement.

The architecture becomes:

Workspace
   ↓
Agreement
   ↓
Agreement Participants
   ├── Internal users
   ├── External contacts
   └── Invited participants
          ↓
     Permissions
          ↓
   Collaboration
   ├── View
   ├── Comment
   ├── Edit
   └── Review

The critical rule:

Sharing one agreement must never grant access to the whole workspace.

3.5.1 What this milestone adds
Agreement Sharing
├── Internal participant access
├── External participant invitations
├── Agreement-specific roles
├── Permission matrix
├── Invitation tokens
├── Invitation expiry
├── Invitation revocation
├── Participant removal
├── Access suspension
├── Comments
├── Activity
└── Real-time collaboration events

ADD CONSTRAINT ck_participant_identity
CHECK (

3.5.4 Agreement-specific roles

Use configurable roles.

class AgreementParticipantRole:
    OWNER = "OWNER"
    EDITOR = "EDITOR"
    REVIEWER = "REVIEWER"
    COMMENTER = "COMMENTER"
    VIEWER = "VIEWER"
    EXTERNAL_REVIEWER = "EXTERNAL_REVIEWER"

The role belongs to the agreement.

A user can therefore be:

OWNER on Agreement A
VIEWER on Agreement B
EDITOR on Agreement C
3.5.5 Why not rely only on workspace roles?

Because workspace membership answers:

“What can this person generally do in this workspace?”

Agreement permissions answer:

“What can this person do with this specific agreement?”

Both checks are required.

3.5.6 Agreement access service
class AgreementAccessService:

    async def check(
        self,
        *,
        user_id,
        agreement_id,
        permission,
    ):

        agreement = await self.agreement_repository.get(
            agreement_id
        )

        if not agreement:
            raise NotFoundError()

        membership = await self.membership_repository.get(
            organization_id=agreement.organization_id,
            user_id=user_id,
        )

        if not membership or not membership.active:
            return False

        participant = (
            await self.participant_repository.get_user_participant(
                agreement_id=agreement_id,
                user_id=user_id,
            )
        )

        if not participant or not participant.active:
            return False

        return getattr(
            participant,
            permission,
            False,
        )

3.5.9 Never store invitation tokens

When generating:

import hashlib
import secrets


def generate_invitation_token() -> tuple[str, str]:

    raw_token = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)

    token_hash = hashlib.sha256(
        raw_token.encode()
    ).hexdigest()

    return raw_token, token_hash

Store only:

token_hash

The raw token goes through your secure invitation delivery mechanism.

       ↓

       ↓
Send secure invitation
       ↓

       ↓

       ↓

       ↓

3.5.12 Invitation service
async def create_invitation(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    agreement_id,
    workspace_id,
    payload,
):

    agreement = await self.agreement_repository.get(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    allowed = await self.access_service.check(
        user_id=actor.id,
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        permission="can_invite",
    )

    if not allowed:
        raise PermissionError(
            "You cannot invite participants."
        )

    raw_token, token_hash = (
        generate_invitation_token()
    )

    invitation = AgreementInvitation(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        email=payload.email.lower(),
        party_contact_id=payload.party_contact_id,
        role=payload.role,
        token_hash=token_hash,
        expires_at=self.clock.now()
        + self.invitation_lifetime,
        invited_by=actor.id,
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(invitation)

    await self.db.commit()

    await self.notification_service.send_agreement_invitation(
        invitation=invitation,
        raw_token=raw_token,
    )

    return invitation

The delivery layer should send the actual secure invitation URL.

3.5.13 Invitation acceptance
POST /api/agreement-invitations/{token}/accept

The service:

async def accept_invitation(
    self,
    *,
    raw_token,
    authenticated_user,
):

    token_hash = hash_token(
        raw_token
    )

    invitation = (
        await self.repository.find_by_hash(
            token_hash
        )
    )

    if not invitation:
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    if invitation.revoked_at:
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    if invitation.accepted_at:
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    if invitation.expires_at <= self.clock.now():
        raise InvalidInvitation()

    if (
        authenticated_user.email.lower()
        != invitation.email.lower()
    ):
        raise PermissionError(
            "Invitation email does not match authenticated user."
        )

    participant = AgreementParticipant(
        agreement_id=invitation.agreement_id,
        user_id=authenticated_user.id,
        role=invitation.role,
        can_view=True,
        can_comment=(
            invitation.role
            in {"COMMENTER", "REVIEWER", "EDITOR"}
        ),
        can_edit=(
            invitation.role == "EDITOR"
        ),
        active=True,
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(participant)

    invitation.accepted_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.db.commit()

    return participant
3.5.14 External collaborator does not become workspace member

This is essential.

After invitation acceptance:

External user
   ↓
Agreement participant

not:

External user
   ↓
Workspace member

They should only see what the agreement participant permissions allow.

3.5.17 Participant removal
DELETE /api/agreements/{id}/participants/{participant_id}

Prefer revocation:

participant.active = False
participant.revoked_at = clock.now()

rather than deleting the historical record.

3.5.18 Access revocation

Once revoked:

Existing session
      ↓
Agreement request
      ↓
participant.active = false
      ↓
403

Do not rely on frontend logout.

3.5.19 Participant permission updates

    role: str
    can_view: bool
    can_comment: bool

The service must ensure that the actor has:

can_manage_access

for this agreement.

3.5.20 Do not allow privilege escalation

A participant shouldn't be able to simply submit:

{
  "can_manage_access": true
}

and grant themselves access.

Check the actor first.

3.5.21 External collaboration workspace

The external user should have a restricted interface:

Agreement Workspace
│
├── Document
├── Comments
├── Requested Actions
└── Activity

They should not receive:

Workspace dashboard
Workspace members
Other agreements
Workspace settings
Internal notifications
Private application data

3.5.26 Create comment
async def create_comment(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    agreement_id,
    content,
    block_id=None,
):

    participant = await self.access_service.require_participant(
        actor.id,
        agreement_id,
    )

    if not participant.can_comment:
        raise PermissionError(
            "Comment permission required."
        )

    comment = AgreementComment(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        participant_id=participant.id,
        block_id=block_id,
        content=content.strip(),
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(comment)

    await self.db.commit()

    return comment

    )
3.5.30 Important distinction

Three records exist:

ACTIVITY
→ user-facing collaboration history

AUDIT
→ security/legal accountability

NOTIFICATION
→ user alert

Do not use one table for all three.

3.5.35 Invitation endpoint security

An invalid invitation should produce a generic response.

Avoid:

"Email john@example.com has no invitation."

because that can leak information.

Use:

"Invitation is invalid or expired."
3.5.36 Invitation expiration

Don't hardcode the expiration duration in application code.

Use application configuration:

class Settings(BaseSettings):

    agreement_invitation_ttl_hours: int

Environment:

AGREEMENT_INVITATION_TTL_HOURS=<configured production value>

Validate it during startup.

3.5.39 Sharing service
class AgreementSharingService:

    async def can_share(
        self,
        actor_id,
        agreement_id,
    ):

        participant = await (
            self.repository
            .get_user_participant(
                agreement_id,
                actor_id,
            )
        )

        if not participant:
            return False

        if not participant.active:
            return False

        return participant.can_invite
3.5.40 WebSocket events

When participant changes occur:

{
  "type": "AGREEMENT_PARTICIPANT_CHANGED",
  "agreement_id": "actual-id"
}

When comment added:

{
  "type": "AGREEMENT_COMMENT_CREATED",
  "agreement_id": "actual-id",
  "comment_id": "actual-id"
}

Only broadcast to currently authorized agreement participants.

3.5.41 Real-time authorization

Don't do:

broadcast_to_agreement(agreement_id)

without filtering recipients.

Instead:

participants = await participant_repo.active_users(
    agreement_id
)

for participant in participants:

    if await access_service.can_view(
        participant.user_id,
        agreement_id,
    ):
        await websocket_manager.send(
            participant.user_id,
            event,
        )
3.5.42 Sharing via link

Avoid permanent public links such as:

/agreement/123

with no authentication.

If you eventually support secure guest access, use:

cryptographically random token
+
short expiration
+
specific agreement
+
specific permissions
+
revocation
+
audit

For the first shipping version, authenticated invitations are safer.

3.5.43 Data leakage prevention

External participants must not receive:

internal comments
internal activity
workspace member information
internal financial data
private metadata
other agreements
internal administrative settings

Unless explicitly shared.

Separate:

INTERNAL_ACTIVITY
EXTERNAL_VISIBLE_ACTIVITY

where necessary.

3.5.44 Internal comments

You can support:

visibility = "INTERNAL"

versus:

visibility = "SHARED"

This is useful when the customer and counterparty collaborate on the same agreement but internal staff need private discussion.

3.5.45 Comment visibility
class CommentVisibility:
    INTERNAL = "INTERNAL"
    SHARED = "SHARED"

Query shared comments:

.where(
    AgreementComment.agreement_id == agreement_id,
    AgreementComment.visibility == "SHARED",
)

Internal users can additionally query internal comments if authorized.

3.5.53 Production rule

The most dangerous mistake would be implementing:

if user in organization:
    return agreement

That is not sufficient.

The correct rule is:

if (
    workspace_member
    and agreement_belongs_to_workspace
    and agreement_participant
    and participant_active
    and participant_can_view
):
    allow()
else:
    deny()

3.6 — Agreement Review, Approval & Sign-Off Workflow

This milestone turns collaboration into a controlled review and approval process.

The flow becomes:

Draft
  ↓
Internal Review
  ↓
Requested Changes?
  ├── YES → Edit → New Version → Review again
  └── NO
        ↓
Approval
        ↓
All required approvals complete
        ↓
READY FOR SIGN-OFF

The most important rule:

An approval belongs to one exact immutable agreement version. Editing the agreement creates a new version and automatically makes previous approvals stale.

3.6.1 What this milestone adds
Review
├── Review requests
├── Reviewers
├── Review stages
├── Sequential review
├── Parallel review
├── Comments
├── Request changes
└── Re-review

Approval
├── Approval requests
├── Approvers
├── Approval policies
├── Approval decisions
├── Approval deadlines
└── Approval history

Sign-off
├── Final review
├── All approvals validation
├── Version lock
└── Ready-for-signature state
3.6.2 Workflow architecture

Do not build a second workflow engine.

This milestone should sit on top of the workflow infrastructure:

Agreement
   ↓
Agreement Version
   ↓
Review/Approval Workflow
   ↓
Workflow Engine
   ├── Tasks
   ├── Decisions
   ├── Deadlines
   ├── Notifications
   └── Audit

3.6.5 Agreement state expansion

Update the agreement state machine from 3.1:

class AgreementStatus(StrEnum):
    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    IN_REVIEW = "IN_REVIEW"
    CHANGES_REQUESTED = "CHANGES_REQUESTED"
    PENDING_APPROVAL = "PENDING_APPROVAL"
    APPROVED = "APPROVED"
    READY_FOR_SIGNING = "READY_FOR_SIGNING"
    ARCHIVED = "ARCHIVED"

Allowed transitions:

ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS = {
    "DRAFT": {
        "IN_REVIEW",
    },

    "IN_REVIEW": {
        "CHANGES_REQUESTED",
        "PENDING_APPROVAL",
        "DRAFT",
    },

    "CHANGES_REQUESTED": {
        "DRAFT",
        "IN_REVIEW",
    },

    "PENDING_APPROVAL": {
        "CHANGES_REQUESTED",
        "APPROVED",
        "DRAFT",
    },

    "APPROVED": {
        "READY_FOR_SIGNING",
        "DRAFT",
    },

    "READY_FOR_SIGNING": set(),

    "ARCHIVED": set(),
}

Do not let clients submit arbitrary target statuses.

3.6.13 Approval is tied to exact version

This is non-negotiable.

Suppose:

Version 8

gets approved.

Then somebody edits the document:

Version 9

Version 8 approval must not remain valid for Version 9.

Check:

if approval.version_id != agreement.current_version_id:
    approval.status = "SUPERSEDED"

When Version 9 is created:

Version 8 approvals
       ↓
SUPERSEDED

Version 9
       ↓
new review/approval
3.6.14 Start review

Endpoint:

POST /api/agreements/{id}/review/start

Request:

class StartReviewRequest(BaseModel):
    expected_version_id: UUID

Service:

async def start_review(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    agreement_id,
    workspace_id,
    expected_version_id,
):

    agreement = await self.repo.get_for_update(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
        permission="agreements.submit_review",
    )

    if (
        agreement.current_version_id
        != expected_version_id
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            "Agreement version changed."
        )

    if agreement.status not in {
        "DRAFT",
        "CHANGES_REQUESTED",
    }:
        raise InvalidTransition()

    await self.validator.validate_for_review(
        agreement
    )

    agreement.status = "IN_REVIEW"

    await self.workflow_engine.start_review(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        version_id=agreement.current_version_id,
    )

    await self.db.commit()

    return agreement

3.6.18 Decision validation
async def decide(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    agreement_id,
    workspace_id,
    decision,
    comment,
    expected_version_id,
):

    agreement = await self.agreement_repo.get(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    if (
        agreement.current_version_id
        != expected_version_id
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            "Review is based on an outdated version."
        )

    request = await self.review_repo.get_for_user(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        version_id=expected_version_id,
        user_id=actor.id,
    )

    if not request:
        raise PermissionError(
            "You are not assigned to review this version."
        )

    if request.status != "PENDING":
        raise DomainError(
            "Review request has already been completed."
        )

    if decision == "APPROVE":

        request.status = "APPROVED"

    elif decision == "REQUEST_CHANGES":

        request.status = "CHANGES_REQUESTED"

    elif decision == "REJECT":

        request.status = "REJECTED"

    else:

        raise ValueError(
            "Unsupported review decision."
        )

    request.completed_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.db.commit()

    await self.workflow_engine.process_review_decision(
        request
    )
3.6.19 Request changes

When a reviewer requests changes:

IN_REVIEW
   ↓
CHANGES_REQUESTED
   ↓
DRAFT
   ↓
User edits
   ↓
New Version
   ↓
IN_REVIEW

Never modify the approved/reviewed version.

3.6.20 Why a new version is required

Example:

Version 4
 └── Reviewed

User changes payment clause

Version 5
 └── New review required

Version 4 remains historical evidence.

3.6.21 Approval start

Once review is complete:

POST /api/agreements/{id}/approval/start

The service checks:

current version exists
        ↓
review exists
        ↓
all required reviewers approved
        ↓
no unresolved review request
        ↓
approval policy exists
        ↓
start approval workflow
3.6.22 Approval service
async def start_approval(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    agreement_id,
    workspace_id,
):

    agreement = await self.repo.get_for_update(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
        permission="agreements.request_approval",
    )

    version = await self.version_repo.get(
        agreement.current_version_id
    )

    review_status = await self.review_service.get_status(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        version_id=version.id,
    )

    if not review_status.completed:
        raise DomainError(
            "Required review is incomplete."
        )

    policy = await self.policy_service.resolve(
        agreement
    )

    if not policy:
        raise DomainError(
            "No approval policy is configured."
        )

    workflow = await self.workflow_service.start(
        agreement=agreement,
        version=version,
        policy=policy,
    )

    agreement.status = "PENDING_APPROVAL"

    await self.db.commit()

    return workflow
3.6.23 Approval policy selection

Do not hardcode:

if agreement_type == "X":
    approval = ...

Resolve it from:

workspace
+
agreement type
+
configured active policy

with explicit precedence.

Example:

agreement-specific policy
        ↓
agreement-type policy
        ↓
workspace default

Only use a fallback if the application policy explicitly defines one.

3.6.24 Approval decision
class ApprovalDecisionRequest(BaseModel):
    decision: str
    comment: str | None = None
    expected_version_id: UUID

Allowed:

APPROVE
REJECT
REQUEST_CHANGES

Endpoint:

/api/agreements/{id}/approval/decision
3.6.25 Approval service
async def decide(
    self,
    *,
    actor,
    agreement_id,
    workspace_id,
    decision,
    comment,
    expected_version_id,
):

    agreement = await self.agreement_repo.get(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    if (
        agreement.current_version_id
        != expected_version_id
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            "Approval is for an outdated version."
        )

    approval = await self.repo.get_pending_for_user(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        version_id=expected_version_id,
        user_id=actor.id,
    )

    if not approval:
        raise PermissionError(
            "You are not an approver for this version."
        )

    if approval.status != "PENDING":
        raise DomainError(
            "Approval is no longer pending."
        )

    if decision == "APPROVE":
        approval.status = "APPROVED"

    elif decision == "REJECT":
        approval.status = "REJECTED"

    elif decision == "REQUEST_CHANGES":
        approval.status = "CHANGES_REQUESTED"

    else:
        raise ValueError(
            "Invalid approval decision."
        )

    approval.decision_comment = comment
    approval.decided_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.db.commit()

    await self.workflow_engine.process_approval_decision(
        approval
    )

    return approval
3.6.26 Sequential approval

Example:

Legal
 ↓
Finance
 ↓
Executive

Finance does not receive an active approval request until Legal completes.

3.6.27 Parallel approval

Example:

           Agreement
          /         \
     Legal           Finance
          \         /
             ↓
          Executive

Legal and Finance can approve independently.

The workflow engine determines the state.

3.6.28 Minimum approvals

Suppose:

5 approvers assigned
minimum = 3

The stage completes once:

3 APPROVED

subject to no rejection/required reviewer rules.

The policy must define exact behavior.

Do not assume every approval system treats a single rejection identically.

3.6.32 Sign-off readiness

The agreement can only become:

READY_FOR_SIGNING

when all required checks pass.

Create:

class SignOffValidator:

    async def validate(
        self,
        agreement_id,
        version_id,
    ):

        checks = []

        checks.append(
            await self.review_service.all_required_complete(
                agreement_id,
                version_id,
            )
        )

        checks.append(
            await self.approval_service.all_required_complete(
                agreement_id,
                version_id,
            )
        )

        checks.append(
            await self.party_service.has_required_parties(
                agreement_id
            )
        )

        return all(checks)
3.6.33 Final sign-off endpoint
POST /api/agreements/{id}/ready-for-signing

Service:

async def mark_ready_for_signing(
    self,
    *,
    agreement_id,
    actor,
    workspace_id,
    expected_version_id,
):

    agreement = await self.repo.get_for_update(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    if (
        agreement.current_version_id
        != expected_version_id
    ):
        raise ConflictError(
            "Current version changed."
        )

    await self.authorization.require(
        actor=actor,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
        permission="agreements.signoff",
    )

    ready = await self.signoff_validator.validate(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        version_id=expected_version_id,
    )

    if not ready:
        raise DomainError(
            "Agreement has incomplete review or approval requirements."
        )

    agreement.status = (
        AgreementStatus.READY_FOR_SIGNING
    )

    await self.audit.record(
        actor_id=actor.id,
        action="AGREEMENT_READY_FOR_SIGNING",
        resource_type="AGREEMENT",
        resource_id=agreement.id,
        metadata={
            "version_id": str(
                expected_version_id
            )
        },
    )

    await self.db.commit()

    return agreement
3.6.34 Version locking

Once ready for signing:

Version 12
     ↓
LOCKED
     ↓
Signing preparation

The user should no longer be able to edit that version.

If changes are required:

READY_FOR_SIGNING
       ↓
Create new draft/version
       ↓
Review again
       ↓
Approval again

Never alter the locked version.

3.6.40 Workflow integration

The review/approval system should use your workflow engine for:

assignment
sequences
parallel branches

escalation

cancellation

The agreement service owns legal state.

The workflow engine owns workflow execution.

    ...

inside the agreement service.

Agreement
   ↓

   ↓
Workflow instance
   ↓

   ↓
Review/approval tasks

3.6.45 Approval supersession

When a new version is created:

await approval_repository.supersede_for_previous_version(
    agreement_id=agreement.id,
    previous_version_id=previous_version.id,
)

Then:

Version 5 approvals → SUPERSEDED
Version 6 → new approval cycle

This should happen transactionally with the version change.

3.6.48 Transaction boundary

When an approver approves:

update approval
+
workflow state
+
agreement state if necessary
+
audit event
+
outbox notification

should be committed consistently.

Example:

async with self.db.begin():

    approval.status = "APPROVED"
    approval.decided_at = self.clock.now()

    await self.workflow_engine.record_decision(...)

    await self.audit.record(...)

    await self.outbox.publish(
        event_type="APPROVAL_COMPLETED",
        aggregate_id=agreement.id,
    )
3.6.49 Failure scenario

Suppose:

Approver clicks Approve

but the worker crashes.

You must not get:

UI says approved
database says pending

The API response is based on the committed transaction.

Notifications can be retried through the outbox afterward.

3.6.50 Deadline scanner

Use the workflow scheduler to find:

review due
approval due
overdue approval
overdue review

Don't create a second scheduler.

3.6.56 Frontend sign-off
function SignOffPanel({
  checks,
}: {
  checks: {
    name: string;
    complete: boolean;
  }[];
}) {
  const ready = checks.every(
    (check) => check.complete
  );

  return (
    <section>
      <h2>Sign-off Readiness</h2>

      {checks.map((check) => (
        <div key={check.name}>
          {check.complete ? "✓" : "○"}{" "}
          {check.name}
        </div>
      ))}

      <button
        disabled={!ready}
      >
        Ready for Signing
      </button>
    </section>
  );
}

The button is disabled for UX, but the backend must independently perform all checks.

3.6.57 Real-data rule

Nothing in this workflow requires synthetic production data.

Reviewers are:

actual application users

Approvals are:

actual workflow assignments

Agreement versions are:

actual stored versions

Comments are:

actual reviewer content

Policies are:

actual workspace configuration

No fake approvals should ever be inserted into production.

3.7 — Electronic Signature & Agreement Execution

This milestone takes an agreement from:

READY_FOR_SIGNING
        ↓
Signer Setup
        ↓
Signing Session
        ↓
Signer Authentication
        ↓
Document Review
        ↓
Consent
        ↓
Signature Placement
        ↓
Signature
        ↓
Execution Evidence
        ↓
EXECUTED

The core rule is:

The exact approved agreement version is frozen for signing. Signing must never modify that version.

3.7.7 Why the execution package exists

An agreement may continue having later drafts after signing.

The execution package says:

THIS exact version
+
THESE exact signers
+
THESE exact fields
+
THIS exact document hash

are what is being executed.

3.7.8 Signers
class ExecutionSigner(Base):

3.7.9 Signer identity rule

Do not let the sender type:

"John Smith"

and treat that as identity.

A signer must correspond to:

authenticated application user

or:

identified external participant/contact

with appropriate verification.

inside a normal database field.

3.7.13 One-time signing token
import hashlib
import secrets


def create_signing_token():

    raw = secrets.token_urlsafe(48)

    digest = hashlib.sha256(
        raw.encode("utf-8")
    ).hexdigest()

    return raw, digest

Store only:

digest

Never store the raw token.

        ↓

3.7.15 Create execution package
async def create_execution_package(
    self,
    *,
    agreement_id,
    actor,
    workspace_id,
):

    agreement = await self.agreement_repo.get_for_update(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        organization_id=workspace_id,
    )

    if not agreement:
        raise NotFoundError()

    if agreement.status != (
        "READY_FOR_SIGNING"
    ):
        raise DomainError(
            "Agreement is not ready for signing."
        )

    version = await self.version_repo.get(
        agreement.current_version_id
    )

    if not version:
        raise DomainError(
            "Current agreement version is missing."
        )

    package = ExecutionPackage(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        version_id=version.id,
        document_hash=version.content_hash,
        status="PENDING",
        locked=True,
        created_by=actor.id,
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(package)

    await self.db.flush()

    return package
3.7.16 Verify immutable version

Before creating the package:

if version.content_hash != calculate_content_hash(
    version.content
):
    raise IntegrityError(
        "Agreement version hash mismatch."
    )

That catches unexpected corruption.

3.7.18 Signer authorization

Do not assume:

agreement participant = authorized signatory

A participant may only be a reviewer.

The system needs an explicit signer role:

REVIEWER
OWNER
APPROVER
SIGNATORY

Only an actual signatory can be added to execution.

3.7.20 Field validation
class SignatureFieldValidator:

    def validate_geometry(
        self,
        field,
    ):

        if field.page_number < 1:
            raise ValidationError(
                "Invalid page number."
            )

        if field.x < 0 or field.y < 0:
            raise ValidationError(
                "Invalid field position."
            )

        if field.width <= 0:
            raise ValidationError(
                "Invalid field width."
            )

        if field.height <= 0:
            raise ValidationError(
                "Invalid field height."
            )

Also validate against the actual rendered document dimensions.

3.7.23 Session activation
async def activate_next_signer(
    self,
    execution_package_id,
):

    pending = await self.signer_repo.next_pending(
        execution_package_id
    )

    if not pending:
        return None

    raw_token, token_hash = create_signing_token()

    session = SigningSession(
        execution_package_id=execution_package_id,
        signer_id=pending.id,
        token_hash=token_hash,
        status="ACTIVE",
        expires_at=(
            self.clock.now()
            + self.signing_session_ttl
        ),
    )

    self.db.add(session)

    pending.status = "READY"

    await self.db.commit()

    await self.notification_service.send_signing_request(
        signer=pending,
        raw_token=raw_token,
    )

    return session
3.7.24 Signer authentication

Authentication strength should be configurable.

For example:

ACCOUNT AUTHENTICATION

or:

STEP-UP MFA

or:

provider-supported authentication

Do not hardcode one legal standard for every jurisdiction/use case.

3.7.25 Consent

Before signing:

☐ I have reviewed this document.
☐ I agree to use electronic signing.
☐ I understand that my signature will be associated
   with this agreement.

The exact wording should be configurable based on your legal/product requirements.

Store the fact that consent was given.

3.7.30 Apply signature

The backend should:

verify session
 ↓
verify signer
 ↓
verify package
 ↓
verify current document hash
 ↓
verify field belongs to signer
 ↓
verify consent
 ↓
validate signature payload
 ↓
store signature artifact
 ↓
hash artifact
 ↓
create signature event
 ↓
mark field complete
3.7.31 Signature endpoint
POST /api/signing/sessions/{session_id}/fields/{field_id}/sign

Request:

class ApplySignatureRequest(BaseModel):
    signature_type: str
    signature_reference: str

The actual signature artifact should be processed through the secure storage layer.

3.7.32 Signature service
async def apply_signature(
    self,
    *,
    session,
    field,
    signer,
    payload,
):

    if session.status != "ACTIVE":
        raise DomainError(
            "Signing session is not active."
        )

    if field.signer_id != signer.id:
        raise PermissionError(
            "Signature field belongs to another signer."
        )

    if field.completed:
        raise DomainError(
            "Signature field is already completed."
        )

    if not await self.consent_repo.exists(
        session.id,
        signer.id,
    ):
        raise DomainError(
            "Electronic signing consent is required."
        )

    package = await self.package_repo.get(
        session.execution_package_id
    )

    version = await self.version_repo.get(
        package.version_id
    )

    if (
        version.content_hash
        != package.document_hash
    ):
        raise IntegrityError(
            "Execution document has changed."
        )

    artifact = await self.signature_storage.store(
        payload.signature_reference
    )

    artifact_hash = await self.signature_storage.hash(
        artifact
    )

    field.value_reference = artifact.key
    field.completed = True

    event = SignatureEvent(
        execution_package_id=package.id,
        signer_id=signer.id,
        session_id=session.id,
        event_type="SIGNATURE_APPLIED",
        field_id=field.id,
        document_hash=package.document_hash,
        occurred_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(event)

    await self.db.commit()

    return event
3.7.33 Never trust the client document

The client must not submit:

{
  "document_hash": "whatever"
}

and have the server trust it.

The server retrieves the immutable version itself and calculates/verifies the hash.

3.7.34 Complete signer

After all required fields are complete:

required_fields = await field_repo.required_for_signer(
    signer.id
)

if not all(
    field.completed
    for field in required_fields
):
    raise DomainError(
        "Required signing fields are incomplete."
    )

Then:

signer.status = SIGNED
session.status = COMPLETED
signer.signed_at = now
3.7.35 Complete execution

After every signer is complete:

signers = await signer_repo.list(
    package.id
)

if not all(
    signer.status == "SIGNED"
    for signer in signers
):
    return

Then:

Execution Package
        ↓
COMPLETED
        ↓
Agreement
        ↓
EXECUTED

3.7.55 Download endpoint
@router.get(
    "/agreements/{agreement_id}/executed/download"
)
async def download_executed(
    agreement_id: UUID,
    current_user=Depends(require_user),
    workspace_id: UUID = Depends(
        get_active_workspace_id
    ),
):

    executed = await executed_repo.get_authorized(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        workspace_id=workspace_id,
        user=current_user,
    )

    if not executed:
        raise NotFoundError()

    url = await storage.create_presigned_url(
        key=executed.document_storage_key,
        expires_in_seconds=300,
    )

    return {
        "url": url
    }

The final production value for the expiry should come from configuration.

3.7.56 Integrity verification

Add:

GET /api/agreements/{id}/execution/verify

Response:

{
  "valid": true,
  "agreement_version_hash_valid": true,
  "executed_document_hash_valid": true,
  "execution_evidence_valid": true
}

The implementation should calculate actual hashes instead of trusting stored values.

3.7.57 Verification service
async def verify_execution(
    self,
    agreement_id,
    actor,
):

    package = await self.package_repo.get_authorized(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        actor=actor,
    )

    version = await self.version_repo.get(
        package.version_id
    )

    current_hash = calculate_content_hash(
        version.content
    )

    version_valid = (
        current_hash
        == package.document_hash
    )

    executed = await self.executed_repo.get(
        agreement_id
    )

    document_bytes = (
        await self.storage.read(
            executed.document_storage_key
        )
    )

    document_hash = sha256_bytes(
        document_bytes
    )

    executed_valid = (
        document_hash
        == executed.document_hash
    )

    return {
        "valid": (
            version_valid
            and executed_valid
        ),
        "agreement_version_hash_valid":
            version_valid,
        "executed_document_hash_valid":
            executed_valid,
    }

CREATE INDEX ix_execution_signers_user
ON execution_signers(
    user_id,
    status
);

CREATE INDEX ix_signature_fields_signer
ON signature_fields(
    signer_id,
    completed
);

CREATE INDEX ix_signing_sessions_signer
ON signing_sessions(
    signer_id,
    status
);

CREATE INDEX ix_signature_events_package
ON signature_events(
    execution_package_id,
    occurred_at
);

CREATE INDEX ix_execution_evidence_package
ON execution_evidence(
    execution_package_id
);
3.7.60 Critical uniqueness

Only one active execution package should normally exist for an agreement at a time.

Use a PostgreSQL partial unique index:

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_active_execution_package
ON execution_packages(agreement_id)
WHERE status IN (
    'PENDING',
    'IN_PROGRESS'
);

This prevents accidental parallel executions.

3.7.62 End-to-end test
async def test_complete_execution_flow():

    agreement = await create_ready_for_signing_agreement()

    package = await execution_service.create_package(
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        actor=agreement.owner,
        workspace_id=agreement.organization_id,
    )

    signer = await execution_service.add_signer(
        package_id=package.id,
        participant_id=actual_signatory.id,
    )

    field = await execution_service.add_signature_field(
        package_id=package.id,
        signer_id=signer.id,
        field_type="SIGNATURE",
        page_number=1,
        x=100,
        y=700,
        width=200,
        height=50,
    )

    session = await signing_service.create_session(
        signer.id
    )

    await signing_service.start_session(
        session.id
    )

    await signing_service.give_consent(
        session.id
    )

    await signing_service.apply_signature(
        session=session,
        field=field,
        signer=signer,
        payload=actual_signature_payload,
    )

    await signing_service.complete_session(
        session.id
    )

    executed = await execution_service.get_executed(
        agreement.id
    )

    assert executed is not None

Test-only data stays isolated from production.

3.7.63 Real-data requirement

actual agreement
actual approved version

actual evidence

It does not require:

fake signers

fake execution dates
fake production execution evidence

Technical values generated by the system—UUIDs, timestamps, hashes and cryptographic tokens—are legitimate system-generated values.

3.8 — Post-Execution Agreement Repository & Document Management

Now that an agreement can be executed, the next requirement is making sure the executed agreement becomes a reliable long-term record.

The flow becomes:

EXECUTED AGREEMENT
       ↓
Secure Repository
       ↓
Documents
       ├── Executed document
       ├── Supporting documents
       ├── Attachments
       └── Evidence
       ↓
Metadata
       ↓
Search
       ↓
Controlled Access
       ↓
Archive / Retention

The key rule:

The repository must never modify the executed document itself. Any new file or corrected document is stored as a separate immutable record with its own hash and provenance.

3.8.6 Private object storage

Files should never be stored under a public URL.

Storage:

private bucket
   ↓
generated storage key
   ↓
encrypted object

Example:

agreements/
  {agreement_id}/
    documents/
      {document_id}/
        original

The storage key is internal.

Users receive short-lived authorized download URLs.

3.8.7 Storage abstraction
from typing import Protocol


class ObjectStorage(Protocol):

    async def put(
        self,
        *,
        key: str,
        content,
        content_type: str,
    ) -> None:
        ...

    async def get(
        self,
        *,
        key: str,
    ):
        ...

    async def delete(
        self,
        *,
        key: str,
    ) -> None:
        ...

    async def create_download_url(
        self,
        *,
        key: str,
        expires_in_seconds: int,
    ) -> str:
        ...

Then your actual S3-compatible provider implements it.

3.8.8 Upload architecture
Browser
   ↓
Request upload authorization
   ↓
Backend authorizes agreement
   ↓
Presigned upload URL
   ↓
Private object storage
   ↓
Upload completed
   ↓
Backend verifies object
   ↓

   ↓

   ↓

Do not send large files through the FastAPI process unnecessarily.

3.8.9 Upload request
class DocumentUploadRequest(BaseModel):
    filename: str
    mime_type: str
    size_bytes: int
    document_type: str

Validate:

if payload.size_bytes <= 0:
    raise ValueError("Invalid file size.")

if payload.size_bytes > settings.max_document_size_bytes:
    raise ValueError("File exceeds configured limit.")

The limit must come from configuration.

3.8.10 Generate storage key
from uuid import uuid4


def build_storage_key(
    agreement_id,
    document_id,
    filename,
):
    return (
        f"agreements/"
        f"{agreement_id}/"
        f"documents/"
        f"{document_id}/"
        f"original"
    )

Never use the raw filename as the storage path.

3.8.11 Upload authorization endpoint
POST /api/agreements/{id}/documents/upload-url
@router.post(
    "/agreements/{agreement_id}/documents/upload-url"
)
async def create_upload_url(
    agreement_id: UUID,
    payload: DocumentUploadRequest,
    current_user=Depends(require_user),
    workspace_id: UUID = Depends(
        get_active_workspace_id
    ),
):

    await agreement_access.require(
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        user=current_user,
        permission="agreements.documents.upload",
        workspace_id=workspace_id,
    )

    document_id = uuid4()

    storage_key = build_storage_key(
        agreement_id,
        document_id,
        payload.filename,
    )

    url = await storage.create_upload_url(
        key=storage_key,
        content_type=payload.mime_type,
        expires_in_seconds=300,
    )

    return {
        "document_id": str(document_id),
        "storage_key": storage_key,
        "upload_url": url,
    }

3.8.13 File integrity

Calculate SHA-256:

import hashlib


def sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

Record:

document_hash
size
mime type
created_at
storage key

3.8.21 Repository search

query = (

3.8.22 Search must be permission-aware

SELECT * FROM agreement_documents

and then filter in the browser.

Correct:

 ↓

This avoids leaking document names from inaccessible agreements.

3.8.38 Agreement access still applies

A user can't bypass agreement authorization simply because they know:

document_id

The document must resolve to an agreement the user can access.

3.8.39 Document access service
class DocumentAccessService:

    async def require(
        self,
        *,
        document_id,
        user,
        permission,
    ):

        document = await self.repository.get(
            document_id
        )

        if not document:
            raise NotFoundError()

        agreement = await self.agreement_repository.get(
            document.agreement_id
        )

        if not agreement:
            raise NotFoundError()

        await self.agreement_access.require(
            agreement_id=agreement.id,
            user=user,
            permission=permission,
        )

        return document

3.8.41 Integrity verification

Endpoint:

GET /api/documents/{id}/verify

Service:

async def verify_document(
    self,
    document,
):

    data = await self.storage.get(
        key=document.storage_key
    )

    actual_hash = sha256_bytes(data)

    return {
        "valid": actual_hash
        == document.content_hash,
        "stored_hash":
            document.content_hash,
        "actual_hash":
            actual_hash,
    }

      ↓

      ↓

      ↓

      ↓
repository record

Do not upload it a second time manually.

3.8.52 Integration with 3.5

A document's access is still:

Workspace membership
        +
Agreement participation
        +
Document permission

An external collaborator should only see documents that are explicitly available to them.

3.8.53 Document sharing policy

Add:

class DocumentVisibility:
    INTERNAL = "INTERNAL"
    SHARED = "SHARED"

A document should default to internal unless explicitly shared through the agreement collaboration system.

This prevents accidental external exposure.

3.9 — Advanced Agreement Search, Filters & Global Search

This milestone turns the app's growing data into a fast, workspace-aware search system.

The flow becomes:

User
 ↓
Search
 ↓
Authorization scope
 ↓
Search engine
 ├── Agreements
 ├── Parties
 ├── Contacts
 ├── Documents
 ├── Versions
 └── Metadata
 ↓
Ranked results
 ↓
Authorized records only

The most important rule:

Authorization happens as part of the query, not after results are returned.

A user must never receive a result first and have the frontend hide it afterward.

3.9.1 What this milestone adds
Global Search
├── Agreement search
├── Party search
├── Contact search
├── Document search
├── Version search
├── Metadata search
├── Exact search
├── Full-text search
├── Prefix search
├── Filters
├── Sorting
├── Pagination
├── Search suggestions
├── Recent searches
└── Saved searches

Security
├── Workspace isolation
├── Agreement-level permissions
├── Document permissions
└── Result-level authorization
3.9.2 Search architecture

Use PostgreSQL first.

                         SEARCH REQUEST
                              │
                              ▼
                       Query Parser
                              │
                    ┌─────────┼─────────┐
                    ▼         ▼         ▼
                 Lexical   Filters    Scope
                    │         │         │
                    └─────────┼─────────┘
                              ▼
                     Permission-aware SQL
                              │
                              ▼
                         Ranking
                              │
                              ▼
                         Pagination
                              │
                              ▼
                       Search Results

Later, when scale actually requires it, you can introduce OpenSearch without changing the public search API.

3.9.3 Search result types
from enum import StrEnum


class SearchObjectType(StrEnum):
    AGREEMENT = "AGREEMENT"
    PARTY = "PARTY"
    CONTACT = "CONTACT"
    DOCUMENT = "DOCUMENT"
    VERSION = "VERSION"
3.9.4 Unified result schema
from datetime import datetime
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel


class SearchResult(BaseModel):
    object_type: SearchObjectType
    object_id: UUID

    title: str
    subtitle: str | None = None

    score: float

    workspace_id: UUID

    agreement_id: UUID | None = None

    updated_at: datetime | None = None

Do not return unrestricted raw database rows.

Return only fields appropriate for search results.

3.9.5 Search request
class SearchRequest(BaseModel):
    query: str

    object_types: list[SearchObjectType] = []

    status: list[str] = []

    agreement_type_ids: list[UUID] = []

    party_ids: list[UUID] = []

    created_from: datetime | None = None
    created_to: datetime | None = None

    updated_from: datetime | None = None
    updated_to: datetime | None = None

    limit: int = 25
    offset: int = 0

Restrict limits:

payload.limit = min(
    max(payload.limit, 1),
    100,
)

payload.offset = max(
    payload.offset,
    0,
)
3.9.6 Normalize search input
def normalize_search_query(
    value: str,
) -> str:

    return " ".join(
        value.strip().split()
    )

Reject empty searches unless explicitly supporting browsing.

query = normalize_search_query(
    payload.query
)

if not query:
    raise ValueError(
        "Search query cannot be empty."
    )
3.9.7 Agreement search vector

Extend the agreement search vector from 3.1.

ALTER TABLE agreements
ADD COLUMN search_vector tsvector
GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
    to_tsvector(
        'simple',
        coalesce(title, '') || ' ' ||
        coalesce(description, '') || ' ' ||

Then create a tsvector search representation.

3.9.12 Search repository
class SearchRepository:

    def __init__(self, db):
        self.db = db

    async def search_agreements(
        self,
        *,
        workspace_id,
        query_text,
        statuses,
        agreement_type_ids,
        party_ids,
        limit,
        offset,
    ):

        ts_query = func.plainto_tsquery(
            "simple",
            query_text,
        )

        query = (
            select(
                Agreement.id,
                Agreement.title,
                Agreement.description,
                Agreement.updated_at,
                func.ts_rank(
                    Agreement.search_vector,
                    ts_query,
                ).label("score"),
            )
            .where(
                Agreement.organization_id
                == workspace_id,
                Agreement.search_vector
                .op("@@")(ts_query),
            )
        )

        if statuses:
            query = query.where(
                Agreement.status.in_(
                    statuses
                )
            )

        if agreement_type_ids:
            query = query.where(
                Agreement.agreement_type_id.in_(
                    agreement_type_ids
                )
            )

        if party_ids:
            query = (
                query
                .join(
                    AgreementPartyLink,
                    AgreementPartyLink.agreement_id
                    == Agreement.id,
                )
                .where(
                    AgreementPartyLink.party_organization_id.in_(
                        party_ids
                    )
                )
            )

        query = (
            query
            .order_by(
                desc("score"),
                Agreement.updated_at.desc(),
            )
            .offset(offset)
            .limit(limit)
        )

        rows = await self.db.execute(query)

        return rows.all()
3.9.13 Agreement access filtering

Workspace membership alone is not enough if your application supports agreement-specific access.

Add the authorization join.

Conceptually:

Agreement
   ↓
Workspace membership
   +
Agreement participant
   ↓
View permission

Query example:

query = (
    select(Agreement)
    .join(
        AgreementParticipant,
        AgreementParticipant.agreement_id
        == Agreement.id,
    )
    .where(
        Agreement.organization_id
        == workspace_id,
        AgreementParticipant.user_id
        == user_id,
        AgreementParticipant.active.is_(True),
        AgreementParticipant.can_view.is_(True),
    )
)

This should become the standard search scope.

3.9.14 Avoid duplicate results

Joining participants can produce duplicates.

Use:

query = query.distinct(
    Agreement.id
)

or construct the query with EXISTS.

EXISTS is often cleaner:

participant_exists = exists(
    select(1)
    .where(
        AgreementParticipant.agreement_id
        == Agreement.id,
        AgreementParticipant.user_id
        == user_id,
        AgreementParticipant.active.is_(True),
        AgreementParticipant.can_view.is_(True),
    )
)

Then:

query = query.where(
    participant_exists
)
3.9.15 Global search service
class GlobalSearchService:

    async def search(
        self,
        *,
        actor,
        workspace_id,
        request,
    ):

        await self.authorization.require(
            actor=actor,
            organization_id=workspace_id,
            permission="search.use",
        )

        query_text = normalize_search_query(
            request.query
        )

        results = []

        allowed_types = (
            request.object_types
            or list(SearchObjectType)
        )

        if (
            SearchObjectType.AGREEMENT
            in allowed_types
        ):
            results.extend(
                await self.search_repo.search_agreements(
                    workspace_id=workspace_id,
                    user_id=actor.id,
                    query_text=query_text,
                    statuses=request.status,
                    agreement_type_ids=(
                        request.agreement_type_ids
                    ),
                    party_ids=request.party_ids,
                    limit=request.limit,
                    offset=request.offset,
                )
            )

        if SearchObjectType.PARTY in allowed_types:
            results.extend(
                await self.search_parties(
                    ...
                )
            )

        if SearchObjectType.CONTACT in allowed_types:
            results.extend(
                await self.search_contacts(
                    ...
                )
            )

        if SearchObjectType.DOCUMENT in allowed_types:
            results.extend(
                await self.search_documents(
                    ...
                )
            )

        return self.rank_and_limit(
            results,
            request.limit,
        )
3.9.16 Don't run every search independently without a limit

A global search across five object types could accidentally request:

100 agreements
100 parties
100 contacts
100 documents
100 versions

for one request.

Instead establish an overall result budget.

SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS = 100

Better yet, put it in configuration.

3.9.17 Result ranking

A simple ranking order:

exact title match
        ↓
prefix title match
        ↓
lexical relevance
        ↓
party relevance
        ↓
recency

Implement using database ranking where possible.

3.9.18 Exact-match boost

PostgreSQL ranking can be supplemented.

exact_match = case(
    (
        func.lower(
            Agreement.title
        ) == query_text.lower(),
        10.0,
    ),
    else_=0.0,
)

Then:

total_score = (
    exact_match
    + lexical_score
)

Don't depend exclusively on application-side ranking after retrieving huge result sets.

3.9.19 Filter model

Add reusable filter definitions:

class SearchFilter(BaseModel):
    field: str
    operator: str
    value: object

But do not accept arbitrary SQL operators.

Allow-list them:

ALLOWED_OPERATORS = {
    "equals",
    "contains",
    "starts_with",
    "before",
    "after",
    "in",
}
3.9.20 Saved searches

Users may save useful queries.

class SavedSearch(Base):
    __tablename__ = "saved_searches"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

    workspace_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey(
            "organizations.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
    )

    user_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey(
            "users.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
    )

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(255),
        nullable=False,
    )

    query_definition: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        nullable=False,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),

3.9.21 Saved-search security

Saved searches belong to the user by default.

Do not make:

user A's saved search

visible to:

user B

unless you explicitly support workspace-shared saved searches.

3.9.22 Create saved search
POST /api/search/saved

Request:

class SaveSearchRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str
    definition: SearchRequest

Service:

async def save_search(
    self,
    *,
    user_id,
    workspace_id,
    payload,
):

    search = SavedSearch(
        workspace_id=workspace_id,
        user_id=user_id,
        name=payload.name.strip(),
        query_definition=payload.definition.model_dump(
            mode="json"
        ),
        created_at=self.clock.now(),
        updated_at=self.clock.now(),
    )

    self.db.add(search)

    await self.db.commit()

    return search
3.9.23 Re-run saved searches safely

A saved search may become stale.

Example:

saved filter references
agreement type X

but later the type is archived.

On execution:

load definition
 ↓
validate filter values
 ↓
apply current authorization
 ↓
execute

Never store raw SQL as the saved query.

3.9.26 Suggestion query
query = (
    select(
        Agreement.id,

        Agreement.organization_id
        == workspace_id,
