3.9.29 Search result component
type SearchResult = {
  object_type: string;
  object_id: string;
  title: string;
  subtitle?: string;
};

export function SearchResults({
  results,
}: {
  results: SearchResult[];
}) {
  return (
    <div>
      {results.map((result) => (
        <button
          key={`${result.object_type}:${result.object_id}`}
          onClick={() => {
            navigateToResult(result);
          }}
        >
          <strong>
            {result.title}
          </strong>

          {result.subtitle && (
            <small>
              {result.subtitle}
            </small>
          )}

          <span>
            {result.object_type}
          </span>
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
3.9.30 Search navigation

Don't generate arbitrary URLs.

Use a centralized resolver:

function navigateToResult(
  result: SearchResult
) {
  switch (result.object_type) {
    case "AGREEMENT":
      router.push(
        `/agreements/${result.object_id}`
      );
      break;

    case "PARTY":
      router.push(
        `/parties/${result.object_id}`
      );
      break;

    case "DOCUMENT":
      router.push(
        `/documents/${result.object_id}`
      );
      break;

    default:
      break;
  }
}
3.9.31 Search result security on navigation

Even though search already checked authorization, the destination API must check authorization again.

Search authorization is not a replacement for resource authorization.

3.9.32 Search by exact reference

Many business users search for:

AGR-12345

Support exact reference searches.

exact_reference = func.lower(
    Agreement.reference_number
) == query_text.lower()

This should receive a high ranking.

Acme Contact

AgreementPartyLink
 ↓

3.9.34 Search by document

User:

statement

should find authorized documents with:

filename
description

 ↓

3.9.35 Search highlighted snippets

For document content, eventually return:

Agreement.pdf

"...payment shall be made within
30 days of receipt..."

The snippet must come from actual indexed document text.

Don't let an LLM invent the snippet.

3.9.36 PostgreSQL snippet generation

PostgreSQL can support headline generation with appropriate FTS configuration.

Conceptually:

ts_headline(
    'simple',
    extracted_content,
    plainto_tsquery('simple', :query)
)

The application should then sanitize any generated HTML/highlight markup before displaying it.

3.9.38 Search pagination

Prefer cursor-based pagination for very large datasets eventually.

For now:

limit
offset

is acceptable.

But the API should cap the page size.

3.9.39 Search performance

Start by analyzing PostgreSQL query plans.

Use:

EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
...

Don't introduce another search engine just because it sounds more scalable.

Move to OpenSearch when real workload demonstrates the need.

3.9.40 Search cache

Do not blindly cache user search responses because authorization can change.

A safe cache key needs to incorporate:

workspace
user
permission context
query
filters
pagination

And cache invalidation must account for membership/access changes.

For the first production implementation, direct PostgreSQL queries are simpler and safer.

3.9.41 Search audit

Record only the information actually needed:

SEARCH_PERFORMED
SAVED_SEARCH_CREATED
SAVED_SEARCH_UPDATED
SAVED_SEARCH_DELETED

Avoid storing sensitive full query text indefinitely unless there is a product reason.

3.9.42 Permissions

Add:

search.use
search.saved.view
search.saved.create
search.saved.update
search.saved.delete
search.history.view
search.history.delete
3.9.43 Workspace-wide saved searches

Later you can support:

PRIVATE
WORKSPACE_SHARED

For now, private saved searches reduce accidental information exposure.

3.9.44 Search service authorization

The core service should never accept:

workspace_id

and assume it is legitimate.

Verify:

membership = await membership_repo.get(
    organization_id=workspace_id,
    user_id=actor.id,
)

if not membership or not membership.active:
    raise PermissionError(
        "Workspace access denied."
    )

Then apply the required search permission.

3.9.45 Global search result merging

Suppose:

Agreement score = 0.91
Party score = 0.84
Document score = 0.78

Normalize scores before merging because PostgreSQL ranking behavior can differ by object type.

Example:

def normalize_score(
    score: float,
    maximum: float,
) -> float:

    if maximum <= 0:
        return 0.0

    return score / maximum

Then apply object-type weights from configuration.

async def test_global_search_cannot_leak_other_workspace_data():

        owner=user

        title="Unique Secret Agreement",
    )

    results = await search_service.search(
        actor=user,
        workspace_id=workspace_a.id,
        request=SearchRequest(
            query="Unique Secret Agreement"
        ),
    )

    assert all(
        result.workspace_id
        == workspace_a.id
        for result in results.results
    )

    )

        workspace=workspace,

3.10 — Notifications, Inbox & Action Center

This milestone gives the standalone Agreement startup a central operational inbox so users do not have to discover important actions by opening individual agreements.

The flow becomes:

Agreement / Workspace Event
        ↓
Event Bus / Outbox
        ↓
Notification Engine
        ↓
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│ In-App Inbox                           │
│ Email                                  │
│ Push                                   │
│ WebSocket real-time update             │
└───────────────────────────────────────┘
        ↓
User Action
        ↓
Existing domain service

The critical rule is:

A notification is not an authorization mechanism and not the source of truth. It is a pointer to an action or event that the user is already authorized to access.

3.10.1 What this milestone adds
Notification System
├── In-app notifications
├── Email notifications
├── Push notifications
├── WebSocket updates
├── Read/unread
├── Priority
├── Category
├── Expiration
├── Deduplication
└── Delivery tracking

Inbox
├── All
├── Unread
├── Action required
├── Mentions
├── Agreements
├── Approvals
├── Signing
└── System

Action Center
├── Review
├── Approval
├── Invitation
├── Signature
├── Comment
└── Other pending actions

Preferences
├── In-app
├── Email
├── Push
├── Per-category settings
└── Quiet hours
3.10.2 Notification architecture

Do not have individual services directly send emails.

Bad:

agreement_service.send_email(...)

Better:

Domain Service
      ↓
Transactional Outbox
      ↓
Notification Event
      ↓
Notification Resolver
      ↓
Notification Record
      ↓
Delivery Workers
      ├── Email
      ├── Push
      └── WebSocket

This prevents lost notifications when transactions and external delivery fail independently.

3.10.11 Notification resolver
class NotificationResolver:

    async def resolve(
        self,
        event,
    ):

        if event.event_type == "APPROVAL_ASSIGNED":
            return await self.resolve_approval(
                event
            )

        if event.event_type == "REVIEW_ASSIGNED":
            return await self.resolve_review(
                event
            )

        if event.event_type == "COMMENT_CREATED":
            return await self.resolve_comment(
                event
            )

        if event.event_type == "SIGNING_REQUESTED":
            return await self.resolve_signing(
                event
            )

        return []
3.10.12 Approval notification

Suppose a real workflow assigns an approval to a user.

Create:

Notification(
    user_id=actual_approver.id,
    organization_id=agreement.organization_id,
    category="APPROVAL",
    event_type="APPROVAL_ASSIGNED",
    title="Approval required",
    body="An agreement requires your approval.",
    priority="HIGH",
    resource_type="AGREEMENT",
    resource_id=agreement.id,
    action_type="OPEN_APPROVAL",
    action_reference=str(approval.id),
    created_at=clock.now(),
)

Do not put the complete agreement text into the notification.

3.10.13 Action center

The action center is different from ordinary notifications.

An action item means:

Something is currently waiting for the user.

Examples:

Review Agreement A
Approve Agreement B
Sign Agreement C
Accept Invitation D
Respond to Comment E

3.10.15 Notification versus action item

Example:

Notification:
"John commented on Agreement A"

Action item:
"Review requested changes for Agreement A"

A comment may generate a notification without creating an action item.

An approval assignment creates both.

3.10.16 Action item state

Don't use:

read = true

to mean an action is complete.

Action state should be based on the source workflow/resource.

For example:

PENDING
COMPLETED
CANCELLED
EXPIRED
3.10.17 Action center query
query = (
    select(ActionItem)
    .where(
        ActionItem.user_id == user_id,
        ActionItem.organization_id == workspace_id,
        ActionItem.completed_at.is_(None),
        ActionItem.cancelled_at.is_(None),
    )
    .order_by(
        ActionItem.priority.desc(),
        ActionItem.due_at.asc().nullslast(),
        ActionItem.created_at.desc(),
    )
)

For robust ordering, map priorities to explicit numeric ranking rather than relying on alphabetical ordering.

3.10.18 Action item source validation

An action item can become stale if the source workflow completes elsewhere.

For example:

Approval task
 ↓
Approver completes it
 ↓
ActionItem must become completed

Don't require the user to manually mark it completed.

3.10.19 Action lifecycle
Workflow creates task
       ↓
ActionItem PENDING
       ↓
Notification created
       ↓
User opens
       ↓
User completes domain action
       ↓
Workflow completes
       ↓
ActionItem COMPLETED

The source workflow is the authority.

3.10.21 Notification query
@router.get("/notifications")
async def list_notifications(
    current_user=Depends(require_user),
    workspace_id: UUID = Depends(
        get_active_workspace_id
    ),
    unread_only: bool = False,
    limit: int = 50,
):

    limit = min(
        max(limit, 1),
        100,
    )

    query = (
        select(Notification)
        .where(
            Notification.user_id
            == current_user.id,
            Notification.organization_id
            == workspace_id,
        )
        .order_by(
            Notification.created_at.desc()
        )
        .limit(limit)
    )

    if unread_only:
        query = query.where(
            Notification.read_at.is_(None)
        )

    return (
        await db.scalars(query)
    ).all()
3.10.22 Mark notification read
@router.post(
    "/notifications/{notification_id}/read"
)
async def mark_read(
    notification_id: UUID,
    current_user=Depends(require_user),
):

    notification = await notification_repo.get_for_user(
        notification_id=notification_id,
        user_id=current_user.id,
    )

    if not notification:
        raise NotFoundError()

    if notification.read_at is None:
        notification.read_at = clock.now()

        await db.commit()

    return {
        "read": True
    }

3.10.28 Real-time notifications

Use WebSocket.

When the notification is created:

Database
 ↓
Outbox
 ↓
Notification worker
 ↓
WebSocket manager
 ↓
Connected user
 ↓
UI updates

Event:

{
  "type": "NOTIFICATION_CREATED",
  "notification_id": "actual-id"
}

The client then fetches the authorized notification record rather than trusting an arbitrary event payload.

3.10.29 WebSocket authorization

Connection:

WSS
 ↓
JWT validation
 ↓
user identity
 ↓
active session
 ↓
allowed workspace

Subscriptions must be user-scoped.

Don't permit:

subscribe(user_id="somebody-else")
3.10.30 WebSocket event delivery
async def send_notification(
    user_id,
    notification_id,
):

    connection = await websocket_manager.get(
        user_id
    )

    if not connection:
        return

    await connection.send_json(
        {
            "type": "NOTIFICATION_CREATED",
            "notification_id": str(
                notification_id
            ),
        }
    )

The connection is already authenticated.

3.10.31 Email provider abstraction

Don't hardcode one provider inside notification logic.

from typing import Protocol


class EmailProvider(Protocol):

    async def send(
        self,
        *,
        recipient: str,
        subject: str,
        html: str,
        text: str,
        idempotency_key: str,
    ):
        ...

Then providers can be configured.

3.10.32 Push provider abstraction
class PushProvider(Protocol):

    async def send(
        self,
        *,

    ):
        ...

No fake device tokens.

Only registered real devices receive push notifications.

3.10.34 Email delivery retries

Use exponential backoff.

def retry_delay(
    attempt: int,
    base_seconds: int,
    max_seconds: int,
) -> int:

    delay = (
        base_seconds
        * (2 ** attempt)
    )

    return min(
        delay,
        max_seconds,
    )

All values should come from configuration.

3.10.35 Idempotency

Suppose the email worker crashes after sending but before committing the delivery state.

A retry could send twice.

Use:

notification_id
+
channel
+
recipient

as part of a provider-supported idempotency key where available.

Example:

idempotency_key = (
    f"notification:{notification.id}:"
    f"channel:{channel}"
)
3.10.36 Delivery status
PENDING
PROCESSING
DELIVERED
FAILED
CANCELLED
3.10.37 Notification deduplication

Some events can fire repeatedly.

For example:

workflow retried
 ↓
same approval notification

Create an event fingerprint.

fingerprint = sha256(
    f"{event_type}:{aggregate_id}:{recipient_id}:{logical_action_id}"
    .encode()
).hexdigest()

Store:

notification_fingerprint

with a uniqueness constraint.

3.10.38 Deduplication constraint
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_notification_fingerprint
ON notifications(
    user_id,
    event_type,
    resource_type,
    resource_id,
    action_type
);

Use this carefully; some events legitimately need multiple notifications over time. A better production implementation can include a logical event instance ID.

3.10.39 Better deduplication

Add:

event_instance_id: Mapped[UUID | None]

Then:

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_notification_event_instance
ON notifications(
    user_id,
    event_instance_id
)
WHERE event_instance_id IS NOT NULL;

This is safer.

3.10.40 Expiring notifications

Some notifications become irrelevant:

Invitation expired
Approval completed
Signing request cancelled
Review request superseded

The notification should then show:

No longer actionable

rather than pretending it is still active.

3.10.41 Notification action resolution

When user clicks:

Approve

the browser should navigate to:

/agreements/{id}/approval

The page/API checks authorization and current workflow state again.

A stale notification cannot bypass current business rules.

3.10.42 Notification actions must be idempotent

A user could click twice.

The underlying:

approval

service must handle the second operation safely.

That's already part of the domain workflow.

The notification system does not need to implement approval logic itself.

3.10.43 Email content

Email should contain:

what happened
why the user was notified
what action is required
safe application link

Do not put sensitive document content into email by default.

Example:

An agreement requires your approval.

Agreement: [actual agreement name]
Action: Approval required

Open Agreement

3.10.54 Notification service
class NotificationService:

    async def create_for_event(
        self,
        *,
        event,
    ):

        recipients = (
            await self.recipient_resolver.resolve(
                event
            )
        )

        policy = self.policy.resolve(
            event.event_type
        )

        created = []

        for recipient in recipients:

            if not await self.authorization.can_notify(
                recipient.user_id,
                event,
            ):
                continue

            notification = Notification(
                user_id=recipient.user_id,
                organization_id=recipient.organization_id,
                category=policy.category,
                event_type=event.event_type,
                title=policy.title,
                body=policy.body,
                priority=policy.priority,
                resource_type=event.aggregate_type,
                resource_id=event.aggregate_id,
                action_type=policy.action_type,
                action_reference=(
                    recipient.action_reference
                ),
                event_instance_id=event.id,
                created_at=self.clock.now(),
            )

            self.db.add(notification)

            created.append(notification)

        await self.db.commit()

        return created
3.10.55 Recipient resolver

This is security-sensitive.

For a review event:

Workflow reviewer

For an approval event:

Assigned approver

For a comment:

Authorized participants

For invitation:

Invited email owner

Do not simply notify every workspace member.

3.10.56 Example comment recipient logic
participants = (
    await participant_repository.active_participants(
        agreement_id
    )
)

for participant in participants:

    if participant.can_view:
        recipients.append(
            participant.user_id
        )

Internal/private comment rules must further restrict recipients.

3.10.57 Security

A notification's existence can itself leak information.

Example:

"Approval requested for confidential agreement"

would leak that the agreement exists.

Therefore, the notification resolver must only create notifications for users who are already authorized to see the underlying resource.

3.10.58 Audit

Track:

NOTIFICATION_CREATED
NOTIFICATION_DELIVERED
NOTIFICATION_FAILED
NOTIFICATION_READ
ACTION_ITEM_CREATED
ACTION_ITEM_COMPLETED
ACTION_ITEM_EXPIRED

Don't audit every polling request.

3.10.59 Delivery worker
@shared_task(
    name="notifications.process_deliveries"
)
def process_deliveries():

    return run_async(
        notification_delivery_service.process_batch()
    )

Batching prevents one job per notification from creating unnecessary queue overhead.

3.10.60 Delivery service
async def process_batch(
    self,
    batch_size: int = 100,
):

    deliveries = await self.repo.claim_pending(
        limit=batch_size
    )

    for delivery in deliveries:

        try:

            await self.send(delivery)

            await self.repo.mark_delivered(
                delivery.id
            )

        except RetryableDeliveryError as exc:

            await self.repo.schedule_retry(
                delivery.id,
                error_code=exc.code,
            )

        except Exception:

            await self.repo.mark_failed(
                delivery.id
            )

The production batch_size should be configurable.

3.10.61 Claiming work safely

Multiple workers may process simultaneously.

Use database row locking:

SELECT id
FROM notification_deliveries
WHERE status = 'PENDING'
  AND (
      next_attempt_at IS NULL
      OR next_attempt_at <= now()
  )
ORDER BY created_at
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
LIMIT :batch_size;

This prevents duplicate worker ownership.

3.10.63 Frontend notification center
"use client";

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

type Notification = {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  body: string;
  category: string;
  priority: string;
  read: boolean;
  action_type?: string;
  resource_id?: string;
  created_at: string;
};

export function NotificationCenter() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<
    Notification[]
  >([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    async function load() {
      const token =
        localStorage.getItem(
          "user_access_token"
        );

      if (!token) return;

      const response = await fetch(
        `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/notifications`,
        {
          headers: {
            Authorization:
              `Bearer ${token}`,
          },
          cache: "no-store",
        }
      );

      if (!response.ok) return;

      setItems(
        await response.json()
      );
    }

    load();
  }, []);

  return (
    <div>
      {items.map((item) => (
        <button
          key={item.id}
          onClick={() => {
            openNotification(item);
          }}
        >
          <strong>
            {item.title}
          </strong>

          <p>
            {item.body}
          </p>

          {!item.read && (
            <span>
              New
            </span>
          )}
        </button>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
3.10.64 Notification action routing
function openNotification(
  notification: Notification
) {
  switch (
    notification.action_type
  ) {
    case "OPEN_APPROVAL":
      router.push(
        `/agreements/${notification.resource_id}/approval`
      );
      break;

    case "OPEN_REVIEW":
      router.push(
        `/agreements/${notification.resource_id}/review`
      );
      break;

    case "OPEN_SIGNING":
      router.push(
        `/agreements/${notification.resource_id}/sign`
      );
      break;

    default:
      router.push(
        `/notifications/${notification.id}`
      );
  }
}

The destination still requires authorization.

3.11 — Agreement Activity, Audit Trail & Full History

This milestone gives every agreement a reliable history showing what happened, who did it, when it happened, and which version/resource was affected.

The important distinction is:

ACTIVITY
→ user-facing timeline

AUDIT
→ protected security/accountability record

DOMAIN EVENTS
→ internal application events

NOTIFICATIONS
→ user alerts

They should remain separate even though they may originate from the same action.

3.11.1 What this milestone adds
Agreement History
├── Created
├── Edited
├── Version created
├── Party added/removed
├── Participant added/removed
├── Comment created/resolved
├── Review started/completed
├── Approval completed
├── Signing started/completed
├── Document uploaded/downloaded
├── Agreement archived/restored
└── Other domain events

Audit
├── Actor
├── Timestamp
├── Action
├── Resource
├── Previous state
├── New state
├── Request/correlation ID
├── IP/device references where required
├── Integrity hash
└── Previous-event hash

History
├── Timeline
├── Filters
├── Version view
├── Event details
└── Export
3.11.2 Architecture
                USER ACTION
                     │
                     ▼
              DOMAIN SERVICE
                     │
             ┌───────┼────────┐
             ▼       ▼        ▼
          Database   Audit   Outbox
             │       │        │
             │       │        └── Notifications
             │       │
             │       └── Protected audit history
             │
             └── Activity projection

The database transaction should keep the domain change, audit event, and outbox event consistent.

3.11.6 Hash-chain audit

The audit system should detect tampering.

Conceptually:

Event 1
 hash = H(event1)

Event 2
 previous_hash = H(event1)
 hash = H(event2 + previous_hash)

Event 3
 previous_hash = H(event2)
 hash = H(event3 + previous_hash)
3.11.7 Canonical audit payload
def canonical_audit_payload(
    *,
    organization_id,
    agreement_id,
    actor_user_id,
    action,
    resource_type,
    resource_id,
    version_id,
    correlation_id,
    request_id,
    metadata,
    previous_event_hash,
    created_at,
):

    payload = {
        "organization_id": str(
            organization_id
        ),
        "agreement_id": (
            str(agreement_id)
            if agreement_id
            else None
        ),
        "actor_user_id": (
            str(actor_user_id)
            if actor_user_id
            else None
        ),
        "action": action,
        "resource_type": resource_type,
        "resource_id": (
            str(resource_id)
            if resource_id
            else None
        ),
        "version_id": (
            str(version_id)
            if version_id
            else None
        ),
        "correlation_id": correlation_id,
        "request_id": request_id,
        "metadata": metadata,
        "previous_event_hash":
            previous_event_hash,
        "created_at":
            created_at.isoformat(),
    }

    return json.dumps(
        payload,
        sort_keys=True,
        separators=(",", ":"),
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ).encode("utf-8")

Then:

def calculate_audit_hash(
    payload: bytes,
) -> str:

    return hashlib.sha256(
        payload
    ).hexdigest()
3.11.8 Audit service
class AuditService:

    async def record(
        self,
        *,
        organization_id,
        agreement_id=None,
        actor_user_id=None,
        action,
        resource_type=None,
        resource_id=None,
        version_id=None,
        correlation_id=None,
        request_id=None,
        metadata=None,
    ):

        metadata = metadata or {}

        previous = (
            await self.repository
            .get_latest_for_organization(
                organization_id
            )
        )

        previous_hash = (
            previous.event_hash
            if previous
            else None
        )

        now = self.clock.now()

        payload = canonical_audit_payload(
            organization_id=organization_id,
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            actor_user_id=actor_user_id,
            action=action,
            resource_type=resource_type,
            resource_id=resource_id,
            version_id=version_id,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,
            request_id=request_id,
            metadata=metadata,
            previous_event_hash=previous_hash,
            created_at=now,
        )

        event_hash = calculate_audit_hash(
            payload
        )

        event = AuditEvent(
            organization_id=organization_id,
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            actor_user_id=actor_user_id,
            action=action,
            resource_type=resource_type,
            resource_id=resource_id,
            version_id=version_id,
            correlation_id=correlation_id,
            request_id=request_id,
            metadata_json=metadata,
            previous_event_hash=previous_hash,
            event_hash=event_hash,
            created_at=now,
        )

        self.db.add(event)

        return event
3.11.9 Important concurrency issue

A naïve:

get latest event
create next event

can produce two events with the same previous hash if two requests execute concurrently.

For production, serialize audit-chain writes or use a database-backed sequence/partition strategy.

One practical approach is an organization-level audit chain lock.

await self.audit_chain_lock.acquire(
    organization_id
)

Then:

read latest
 ↓
calculate
 ↓
insert
 ↓
commit
 ↓
release

Do not assume application-level async locks are sufficient across multiple processes.

The lock must coordinate across workers/instances.

3.11.10 PostgreSQL advisory lock

A PostgreSQL advisory lock can be used for the organization chain.

Conceptually:

SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(:organization_lock_key);

The key should be deterministically derived from the organization UUID.

Keep this implementation inside the audit repository rather than scattering lock logic throughout the application.

3.11.11 Prevent audit modification

Application users should not have:

UPDATE audit_events
DELETE FROM audit_events

permissions.

The application database role used by the web application should have only the minimum privileges required.

For stronger deployment:

application role
   ├── INSERT audit
   └── SELECT audit where allowed

separate privileged migration/operations role
   └── schema maintenance

"A new agreement version was created."

3.11.28 Audit versus activity

The audit contains more technical accountability information.

3.11.29 Request correlation

Make correlation IDs available throughout the request.

Middleware:

import uuid


@app.middleware("http")
async def correlation_middleware(
    request,
    call_next,
):

    correlation_id = (
        request.headers.get(
            "X-Correlation-ID"
        )
        or str(uuid.uuid4())
    )

    request.state.correlation_id = (
        correlation_id
    )

    response = await call_next(request)

    response.headers[
        "X-Correlation-ID"
    ] = correlation_id

    return response

Validate incoming IDs to prevent malformed header abuse.

3.11.34 Integrity verification endpoint

}
3.11.35 Verification
async def verify_chain(
    self,
    organization_id,
):

    events = await self.repo.list_in_order(
        organization_id
    )

    previous_hash = None

    checked = 0

    for event in events:

        payload = canonical_audit_payload(
            organization_id=event.organization_id,
            agreement_id=event.agreement_id,
            actor_user_id=event.actor_user_id,
            action=event.action,
            resource_type=event.resource_type,
            resource_id=event.resource_id,
            version_id=event.version_id,
            correlation_id=event.correlation_id,
            request_id=event.request_id,
            metadata=event.metadata_json,
            previous_event_hash=(
                event.previous_event_hash
            ),
            created_at=event.created_at,
        )

        calculated = calculate_audit_hash(
            payload
        )

        if calculated != event.event_hash:
            return {
                "valid": False,
                "failed_event_id": event.id,
            }

        if (
            event.previous_event_hash
            != previous_hash
        ):
            return {
                "valid": False,
                "failed_event_id": event.id,
            }

        previous_hash = event.event_hash
        checked += 1

    return {
        "valid": True,
        "events_checked": checked,
    }
3.11.36 Scale consideration

A single organization-wide chain can eventually become a write bottleneck.

If actual production throughput demonstrates this problem, evolve toward:

organization
   ↓
partitioned audit stream
   ↓
agreement-level or shard-level chains

But don't introduce unnecessary complexity before measuring real workload.

    still exists in database

Real-time updates are an optimization, not the source of truth.

3.11.61 Test — actor identity

Every user action should resolve actor identity from authentication.

async def test_client_cannot_impersonate_audit_actor():

        200,

        event.actor_user_id

The submitted actor_user_id must be ignored.

3.12 — Agreement Lifecycle, Deadlines, Renewals & Expiration Management

This milestone turns the stored agreement terms into a controlled lifecycle system.

The important rule is:

The system never invents a contract date, renewal period, notice period, or termination rule.

Every lifecycle fact must come from one of these sources:

An actual agreement version field.
A published template variable actually used to generate the agreement.
A verified extracted value from a document.
An explicit workspace/agreement configuration.
An explicit authorized user decision.

A generic legal default such as “30 days before expiry” is not allowed.

3.12.1 Architecture
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Agreement Version       │
                    │ Actual Contract Data    │
                    └────────────┬────────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Lifecycle Term Resolver  │
                    │                         │
                    │ start_date              │
                    │ end_date                │
                    │ renewal_rule             │
                    │ renewal_term             │
                    │ notice_period            │
                    │ termination_rule         │
                    └────────────┬────────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Lifecycle Engine         │
                    │                         │
                    │ State transitions        │
                    │ Deadline calculation     │
                    │ Renewal calculation      │
                    │ Expiration detection     │
                    └────────────┬────────────┘
                                 │
              ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
              ▼                  ▼                  ▼
      ┌──────────────┐   ┌──────────────┐   ┌──────────────┐
      │ Deadlines    │   │ Alerts       │   │ Renewals     │
      └──────┬───────┘   └──────┬───────┘   └──────┬───────┘
             │                  │                  │
             └──────────────────┼──────────────────┘
                                ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Workflow / Action Center │
                    └────────────┬────────────┘
                                 ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Notification / Email     │
                    │ WebSocket / Push         │
                    └─────────────────────────┘

                     Every mutation
                            │
                            ▼
                    Audit + Activity + Outbox
3.12.2 Lifecycle states

Do not collapse every lifecycle event into “expired”.

# backend/app/lifecycle/enums.py

The values themselves are application vocabulary, not business data.

3.12.4 Lifecycle source-of-truth resolver

This is the most important part.

The lifecycle engine must never guess.

resolver.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from sqlalchemy import select

from app.agreements.models import AgreementVersion
from .models import LifecycleTerm
from .enums import LifecycleTermType


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ResolvedLifecycleTerms:
    source_version_id: UUID
    effective_date: date | None
    expiry_date: date | None
    renewal_enabled: bool | None
    renewal_term: dict | None
    notice_period: dict | None
    termination_notice_period: dict | None


class LifecycleTermResolver:

    async def resolve(
        self,
        db: AsyncSession,
        agreement_id: UUID,
        version_id: UUID,
    ) -> ResolvedLifecycleTerms:

        result = await db.execute(
            select(LifecycleTerm).where(
                LifecycleTerm.agreement_id == agreement_id,
                LifecycleTerm.source_version_id == version_id,
                LifecycleTerm.verified.is_(True),
            )
        )

        terms = list(result.scalars())

        values = {
            LifecycleTermType.EFFECTIVE_DATE: None,
            LifecycleTermType.EXPIRY_DATE: None,
            LifecycleTermType.RENEWAL_ENABLED: None,
            LifecycleTermType.RENEWAL_TERM: None,
            LifecycleTermType.NOTICE_PERIOD: None,
            LifecycleTermType.TERMINATION_NOTICE_PERIOD: None,
        }

        for term in terms:
            values[term.term_type] = term.value

        return ResolvedLifecycleTerms(
            source_version_id=version_id,
            effective_date=self._date_value(
                values[LifecycleTermType.EFFECTIVE_DATE]
            ),
            expiry_date=self._date_value(
                values[LifecycleTermType.EXPIRY_DATE]
            ),
            renewal_enabled=self._bool_value(
                values[LifecycleTermType.RENEWAL_ENABLED]
            ),
            renewal_term=values[LifecycleTermType.RENEWAL_TERM],
            notice_period=values[LifecycleTermType.NOTICE_PERIOD],
            termination_notice_period=values[
                LifecycleTermType.TERMINATION_NOTICE_PERIOD
            ],
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _date_value(value):
        if value is None:
            return None

        if isinstance(value, dict):
            raw = value.get("date")
        else:
            raw = value

        if not raw:
            return None

        return date.fromisoformat(raw)

    @staticmethod
    def _bool_value(value):
        if value is None:
            return None

        if isinstance(value, dict):
            return bool(value.get("value"))

        return bool(value)

This intentionally refuses to derive lifecycle dates directly from arbitrary prose.

A future document-extraction system can populate lifecycle_terms, but that extracted value must be verified before it becomes a lifecycle fact.

3.12.5 Term verification

A real agreement may have extracted dates that need human confirmation.

Example lifecycle term:

{
  "term_type": "EXPIRY_DATE",
  "value": {
    "date": "2028-09-30"
  },
  "source_reference": {
    "source": "AGREEMENT_VERSION",
    "block_id": "..."
  },
  "verified": true
}

No term is usable until:

verified = true

That prevents an unverified extraction from silently becoming a contractual deadline.

3.12.6 Deadline calculation

Create a dedicated date arithmetic service.

deadlines.py
from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta

from .models import LifecycleDeadline
from .enums import LifecycleDeadlineType


class LifecycleDateCalculator:

    @staticmethod
    def add_term(
        value: date,
        term: dict,
    ) -> date:

        if not term:
            raise ValueError("Missing configured renewal term")

        unit = term.get("unit")
        amount = term.get("amount")

        if not isinstance(amount, int) or amount <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Invalid lifecycle term amount")

        if unit == "DAY":
            return value + timedelta(days=amount)

        if unit == "MONTH":
            return value + relativedelta(months=amount)

        if unit == "YEAR":
            return value + relativedelta(years=amount)

        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported lifecycle term unit: {unit}")

    @staticmethod
    def at_timezone(
        value: date,
        timezone_name: str,
    ) -> datetime:

        return datetime.combine(
            value,
            time.min,
            tzinfo=ZoneInfo(timezone_name),
        )

Notice there is no:

expiry - timedelta(days=30)

anywhere.

That would be a hidden legal/business assumption.

3.12.7 Renewal engine

Renewal needs to distinguish:

RENEW
DO_NOT_RENEW
PENDING

from:

TERMINATE

These are separate actions.

renewal.py
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from sqlalchemy import select

from .models import RenewalRecord
from .resolver import LifecycleTermResolver
from .deadlines import LifecycleDateCalculator
from .enums import RenewalDecision


class RenewalService:

    def __init__(self):
        self.resolver = LifecycleTermResolver()
        self.calculator = LifecycleDateCalculator()

    async def prepare_renewal(
        self,
        db: AsyncSession,
        *,
        organization_id: UUID,
        agreement_id: UUID,
        version_id: UUID,
    ) -> RenewalRecord:

        terms = await self.resolver.resolve(
            db,
            agreement_id,
            version_id,
        )

        if terms.expiry_date is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Agreement does not have a verified expiry date"
            )

        if terms.renewal_enabled is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Renewal behavior is not configured"
            )

        next_term_start = None
        next_term_end = None

        if terms.renewal_enabled:

            if not terms.renewal_term:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Renewal is enabled but no renewal term is configured"
                )

            next_term_start = terms.expiry_date

            next_term_end = self.calculator.add_term(
                terms.expiry_date,
                terms.renewal_term,
            )

        record = RenewalRecord(
            organization_id=organization_id,
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            source_version_id=version_id,
            current_term_end=terms.expiry_date,
            renewal_enabled=terms.renewal_enabled,
            renewal_term=terms.renewal_term,
            decision=RenewalDecision.PENDING,
            next_term_start=next_term_start,
            next_term_end=next_term_end,
        )

        db.add(record)

        await db.flush()

        return record

    async def decide(
        self,
        db: AsyncSession,
        *,
        renewal_id: UUID,
        user_id: UUID,
        decision: RenewalDecision,
    ) -> RenewalRecord:

        result = await db.execute(
            select(RenewalRecord)
            .where(RenewalRecord.id == renewal_id)
            .with_for_update()
        )

        record = result.scalar_one()

        if record.decision != RenewalDecision.PENDING:
            raise ValueError(
                "Renewal decision has already been finalized"
            )

        record.decision = decision
        record.decision_by = user_id
        record.decision_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        await db.flush()

        return record
3.12.8 Renewal decision behavior

The engine must behave like this:

                         Agreement expiry
                                │
                                ▼
                     Renewal configured?
                       /            \
                     NO              YES
                     │                │
                     ▼                ▼
                normal expiry    Renewal window
                                      │
                                      ▼
                               Decision required
                                /            \
                              RENEW       DO_NOT_RENEW
                                │              │
                                ▼              ▼
                         next term        NON_RENEWED

A DO_NOT_RENEW decision must not automatically become:

TERMINATED

because non-renewal and termination have different meanings.

3.12.9 Lifecycle state machine
service.py
from datetime import date
from enum import StrEnum

from .enums import LifecycleState


class LifecycleTransitionError(Exception):
    pass


class LifecycleStateMachine:

    ALLOWED = {
        LifecycleState.NOT_STARTED: {
            LifecycleState.ACTIVE,
            LifecycleState.CANCELLED,
        },

        LifecycleState.ACTIVE: {
            LifecycleState.EXPIRING,
            LifecycleState.SUSPENDED,
            LifecycleState.TERMINATION_PENDING,
            LifecycleState.AMENDED,
            LifecycleState.NON_RENEWAL_PENDING,
            LifecycleState.EXPIRED,
        },

        LifecycleState.EXPIRING: {
            LifecycleState.ACTIVE,
            LifecycleState.EXPIRED,
            LifecycleState.NON_RENEWAL_PENDING,
            LifecycleState.TERMINATION_PENDING,
            LifecycleState.AMENDED,
        },

        LifecycleState.NON_RENEWAL_PENDING: {
            LifecycleState.ACTIVE,
            LifecycleState.NON_RENEWED,
            LifecycleState.AMENDED,
        },

        LifecycleState.TERMINATION_PENDING: {
            LifecycleState.ACTIVE,
            LifecycleState.TERMINATED,
            LifecycleState.AMENDED,
        },

        LifecycleState.SUSPENDED: {
            LifecycleState.ACTIVE,
            LifecycleState.TERMINATED,
            LifecycleState.AMENDED,
        },

        LifecycleState.EXPIRED: {
            LifecycleState.AMENDED,
        },

        LifecycleState.NON_RENEWED: {
            LifecycleState.AMENDED,
        },

        LifecycleState.TERMINATED: {
            LifecycleState.AMENDED,
        },

        LifecycleState.AMENDED: {
            LifecycleState.ACTIVE,
            LifecycleState.EXPIRING,
            LifecycleState.CANCELLED,
        },

        LifecycleState.CANCELLED: set(),
    }

    @classmethod
    def transition(
        cls,
        current: LifecycleState,
        target: LifecycleState,
    ) -> LifecycleState:

        if target not in cls.ALLOWED.get(current, set()):
            raise LifecycleTransitionError(
                f"Invalid lifecycle transition: "
                f"{current} -> {target}"
            )

        return target

This prevents arbitrary state changes from the API.

3.12.10 Recalculation after amendments

This is critical.

Suppose:

Version 4:
expiry = 2027-12-31

Then an amendment produces:

Version 5:
expiry = 2029-12-31

The old lifecycle deadlines cannot remain active.

When a new agreement version is finalized:

new version
    ↓
detect lifecycle-affecting fields
    ↓
invalidate derived lifecycle deadlines
    ↓
mark lifecycle recalculation_required=true
    ↓
re-resolve verified terms
    ↓
generate new deadlines
    ↓
audit

Add to agreement-version finalization:

async def mark_lifecycle_recalculation(
    db,
    agreement_id,
):
    lifecycle = await get_lifecycle_for_update(
        db,
        agreement_id,
    )

    if lifecycle:
        lifecycle.recalculation_required = True

Then the lifecycle worker recalculates from the new immutable version.

3.12.11 Idempotent lifecycle scanner

Use Celery/worker scheduling.

tasks.py
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from celery import shared_task
from sqlalchemy import select

from app.db.session import async_session_factory
from .models import AgreementLifecycle
from .service import LifecycleService


@shared_task(
    bind=True,
    autoretry_for=(Exception,),
    retry_backoff=True,
    max_retries=5,
)
def scan_agreement_lifecycles(self):

    import asyncio

    asyncio.run(_scan())


async def _scan():

    async with async_session_factory() as db:

        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        result = await db.execute(
            select(AgreementLifecycle)
            .where(
                AgreementLifecycle.next_check_at <= now
            )
            .with_for_update(
                skip_locked=True
            )
        )

        lifecycles = list(result.scalars())

        service = LifecycleService()

        for lifecycle in lifecycles:

            await service.process_lifecycle(
                db,
                lifecycle.agreement_id,
            )

        await db.commit()

SKIP LOCKED prevents multiple workers from processing the same lifecycle record simultaneously.

3.12.12 Lifecycle processing
from datetime import datetime, timezone, date

from sqlalchemy import select

from app.agreements.models import Agreement
from .models import AgreementLifecycle
from .enums import LifecycleState


class LifecycleService:

    async def process_lifecycle(
        self,
        db,
        agreement_id,
    ):

        result = await db.execute(
            select(AgreementLifecycle)
            .where(
                AgreementLifecycle.agreement_id == agreement_id
            )
            .with_for_update()
        )

        lifecycle = result.scalar_one()

        # Resolve current authoritative version.
        agreement = await self._load_authorized_agreement(
            db,
            agreement_id,
        )

        version_id = agreement.current_version_id

        terms = await self.resolver.resolve(
            db,
            agreement_id,
            version_id,
        )

        today = date.today()

        target_state = self._calculate_state(
            today=today,
            effective_date=terms.effective_date,
            expiry_date=terms.expiry_date,
        )

        if target_state != lifecycle.current_state:

            LifecycleStateMachine.transition(
                lifecycle.current_state,
                target_state,
            )

            lifecycle.current_state = target_state

            await self._record_lifecycle_event(
                db,
                agreement_id=agreement_id,
                old_state=lifecycle.current_state,
                new_state=target_state,
                version_id=version_id,
            )

        lifecycle.source_version_id = version_id
        lifecycle.effective_date = terms.effective_date
        lifecycle.expiry_date = terms.expiry_date
        lifecycle.recalculation_required = False

        await self._recalculate_deadlines(
            db=db,
            agreement=agreement,
            terms=terms,
        )

        lifecycle.next_check_at = self._next_check_time(
            terms,
            today,
        )

    def _calculate_state(
        self,
        *,
        today,
        effective_date,
        expiry_date,
    ):

        if effective_date and today < effective_date:
            return LifecycleState.NOT_STARTED

        if expiry_date and today >= expiry_date:
            return LifecycleState.EXPIRED

        return LifecycleState.ACTIVE

The production version should layer configured renewal/termination/suspension workflows over this base state resolution rather than allowing ad-hoc controller logic.

3.12.13 Deadline invalidation

Old deadlines must never remain active after the source agreement version changes.

from sqlalchemy import update

from .models import LifecycleDeadline
from .enums import DeadlineStatus


async def invalidate_version_deadlines(
    db,
    agreement_id,
    old_version_id,
):

    await db.execute(
        update(LifecycleDeadline)
        .where(
            LifecycleDeadline.agreement_id == agreement_id,
            LifecycleDeadline.source_version_id == old_version_id,
            LifecycleDeadline.status == DeadlineStatus.PENDING,
        )
        .values(
            status=DeadlineStatus.CANCELLED
        )
    )

This gives you historical traceability without deleting anything.

3.12.14 Expiration alerts

There should be no hardcoded alert offsets.

Instead, configure lifecycle alert schedules.

For example, a workspace may actually configure:

{
  "alert_type": "UPCOMING_EXPIRY",
  "offset": {
    "amount": 45,
    "unit": "DAY"
  }
}

Another workspace could configure:

{
  "alert_type": "UPCOMING_EXPIRY",
  "offset": {
    "amount": 90,
    "unit": "DAY"
  }
}

The engine simply executes configuration.

It never assumes a universal notice period.

3.12.19 Notification idempotency

When the worker detects a deadline:

async def create_lifecycle_alert(
    db,
    *,
    organization_id,
    agreement_id,
    deadline,
    alert_type,
    recipients,
):

    # Unique constraint prevents duplicate alerts.
    alert = LifecycleAlert(
        organization_id=organization_id,
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        deadline_id=deadline.id,
        alert_type=alert_type,
        due_at=deadline.due_at,
        recipients=recipients,
    )

    db.add(alert)

    try:
        await db.flush()
    except IntegrityError:
        await db.rollback()
        return None

    return alert

The unique database constraint is the final protection against duplicate lifecycle alerts.

The audit record must include:

{
  "agreement_id": "...",
  "agreement_version_id": "...",
  "source_version_id": "...",
  "lifecycle_deadline_id": "...",
  "old_state": "...",
  "new_state": "...",
  "reason": "...",
  "correlation_id": "..."
}

Do not allow the client to provide the actor identity.

3.12.21 Important workflow rule

A lifecycle engine should not automatically perform legally consequential actions merely because a date passed.

For example:

Expiry reached
    ↓
EXPIRED

is different from:

Expiry reached
    ↓
TERMINATE COUNTERPARTY RELATIONSHIP

The second requires an explicit configured workflow.

Likewise:

DO_NOT_RENEW

does not imply:

TERMINATE

And:

EXPIRING

does not imply:

DO_NOT_RENEW

The system should surface the required action, not silently invent one.

3.12.22 Workspace lifecycle configuration

Workspace administrators need a configuration model rather than application constants.

Add:

class LifecyclePolicy(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lifecycle_policies"

    id = mapped_column(PGUUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True, default=uuid4)

    organization_id = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("organizations.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
        unique=True,
    )

    alert_schedule = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
    )

    timezone = mapped_column(
        String(64),
        nullable=False,
    )

    enabled = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=True,
    )

For example, the actual user configuration can contain:

{
  "alerts": [
    {
      "event": "UPCOMING_EXPIRY",
      "offset": {
        "amount": 60,
        "unit": "DAY"
      }
    },
    {
      "event": "NOTICE_DEADLINE",
      "offset": {
        "amount": 7,
        "unit": "DAY"
      }
    }
  ]
}

The application does not assume those values. They exist because the workspace configured them.

3.12.24 Lifecycle recalculation transaction

When a new agreement version becomes current:

BEGIN
   │
   ├── create immutable agreement version
   │
   ├── change current_version_id
   │
   ├── mark lifecycle.recalculation_required
   │
   ├── cancel deadlines derived from previous version
   │
   ├── write domain event
   │
   ├── write audit event
   │
   └── write outbox event
COMMIT

Then:

outbox
   ↓
lifecycle worker
   ↓
resolve new version
   ↓
calculate deadlines
   ↓
create new derived records

This avoids a partially updated lifecycle.

3.12.25 Security

Lifecycle endpoints must never accept:

{
  "organization_id": "some-other-workspace"
}

and trust it.

Instead:

agreement = await require_agreement_permission(
    db,
    user=current_user,
    agreement_id=agreement_id,
    permission="can_view",
)

The server derives:

organization_id
agreement ownership
participant access
workspace membership

from the authenticated session and DB.

For action endpoints:

VIEW
    ↓
can_view

RENEWAL DECISION
    ↓
can_manage_workflow

TERM VERIFICATION
    ↓
can_manage_workflow / configured privileged permission

POLICY CONFIGURATION
    ↓
organization administrator
3.12.26 Timezone correctness

Never use:

datetime.now()

for lifecycle processing.

Use UTC internally:

datetime.now(timezone.utc)

Store workspace timezone:

Asia/Colombo
Europe/London
America/New_York
...

and convert only for presentation/deadline interpretation.

The lifecycle calculation itself must explicitly establish whether a contract date is a date-only value or a timezone-specific datetime.

3.13 — Agreement Obligations, Tasks & Performance Tracking

This milestone separates the legal obligation from the operational task used to fulfill it.

That distinction matters:

Agreement
   ↓
Agreement Version
   ↓
Obligation
   ↓
Requirement / Schedule
   ↓
Task
   ↓
Evidence
   ↓
Completion / Exception
   ↓
Performance history

An obligation is not just a reminder.

It represents something the contract actually requires, while tasks represent the operational work used to satisfy that requirement.

3.13.1 Core design

The system should support:

One-time obligations
Recurring obligations
Event-triggered obligations
Milestone obligations
Payment-related obligations
Delivery obligations
Reporting obligations
Review obligations
Notice obligations
Maintenance obligations
Evidence-required obligations
Party-specific obligations

But the platform must not invent the obligation.

Every obligation originates from:

AGREEMENT_VERSION
TEMPLATE
STRUCTURED_TERM
VERIFIED_EXTRACTION
EXPLICIT_USER_ENTRY

The source must always remain traceable.

3.13.2 Architecture
                     ┌───────────────────────┐
                     │ Agreement Version     │
                     └───────────┬───────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                     ┌───────────────────────┐
                     │ Obligation Definition │
                     │                       │
                     │ What must happen?     │
                     │ Who must perform?     │
                     │ When?                 │
                     │ How often?            │
                     │ Evidence required?    │
                     └───────────┬───────────┘
                                 │
                ┌────────────────┼─────────────────┐
                ▼                ▼                 ▼
        ┌──────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐
        │ Deadline     │ │ Recurrence    │ │ Dependencies │
        └──────┬───────┘ └───────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘
               └──────────────────┼────────────────┘
                                  ▼
                       ┌───────────────────────┐
                       │ Obligation Instances  │
                       └──────────┬────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
                       ┌───────────────────────┐
                       │ Operational Tasks     │
                       └──────────┬────────────┘
                                  │
               ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐
               ▼                  ▼                  ▼
          Evidence            Exceptions        Completion
               │                  │                  │
               └──────────────────┼──────────────────┘
                                  ▼
                       ┌───────────────────────┐
                       │ Performance History   │
                       └───────────────────────┘
3.13.3 Why there are two levels

Do not make:

obligation = task

For example:

Supplier must provide quarterly compliance report.

That is one contractual obligation.

It may create:

2027 Q1 task
2027 Q2 task
2027 Q3 task
2027 Q4 task
...

So:

Obligation
    ↓
Recurring obligation
    ↓
Many obligation instances
    ↓
Many tasks

This gives the system proper historical performance tracking.

from datetime import datetime, date
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import (
    Boolean,
    Date,
    DateTime,
    ForeignKey,
    Index,
    Integer,
    String,
    Text,
    UniqueConstraint,
    text,
)
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB, UUID as PGUUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.db.base import Base

from .enums import (
    ObligationStatus,
    ObligationFrequency,
    ObligationTrigger,
    ObligationInstanceStatus,
    TaskStatus,
    EvidenceType,
    EvidenceVerificationStatus,
    ExceptionType,
    ExceptionStatus,
)


class Obligation(Base):
    __tablename__ = "obligations"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

    organization_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("organizations.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    agreement_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("agreements.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    source_version_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("agreement_versions.id", ondelete="RESTRICT"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(500),
        nullable=False,
    )

    description: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    status: Mapped[ObligationStatus] = mapped_column(
        String(32),
        nullable=False,
        default=ObligationStatus.DRAFT,
    )

    frequency: Mapped[ObligationFrequency] = mapped_column(
        String(32),
        nullable=False,
        default=ObligationFrequency.ONCE,
    )

    recurrence_rule: Mapped[dict | None] = mapped_column(
        JSONB
    )

    trigger_type: Mapped[ObligationTrigger] = mapped_column(
        String(32),
        nullable=False,
    )

    trigger_definition: Mapped[dict | None] = mapped_column(
        JSONB
    )

    requires_evidence: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
    )

    evidence_definition: Mapped[dict | None] = mapped_column(
        JSONB
    )

    assignee_user_id: Mapped[UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
    )

    responsible_party_id: Mapped[UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("party_organizations.id"),
    )

    source_reference: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
    )

    effective_from: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(Date)
    effective_until: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(Date)

    created_by: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
        server_default=text("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"),
    )

    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
        server_default=text("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"),
    )

    __table_args__ = (
        Index(
            "ix_obligations_agreement",
            "organization_id",
            "agreement_id",
        ),
    )

3.13.6 Source references

An obligation needs a machine-readable origin.

Example:

{
  "source_type": "AGREEMENT_VERSION",
  "version_id": "...",
  "block_id": "...",
  "field_path": "blocks[12].content"
}

Or a template-derived obligation:

{
  "source_type": "TEMPLATE",
  "template_id": "...",
  "template_version_id": "...",
  "variable_key": "..."
}

Or explicit user creation:

{
  "source_type": "USER_ENTRY",
  "created_from_ui": true
}

Do not allow:

"source": "system"

without enough provenance to reproduce why the obligation exists.

3.13.7 Obligation extraction

The first production implementation should support explicit and structured extraction.

Do not automatically scan arbitrary legal text and create obligations without validation.

Use:

agreement version
      ↓
structured fields / configured extraction
      ↓
candidate obligation
      ↓
human verification
      ↓
ACTIVE

Later, an NLP/LLM extraction layer can produce:

candidate obligation

but not:

active contractual obligation

without verification.

This is important because an incorrect extraction can create false operational work or falsely suggest breach.

3.13.8 Obligation creation service
service.py
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from .models import Obligation
from .enums import (
    ObligationStatus,
    ObligationFrequency,
    ObligationTrigger,
)


class ObligationService:

    async def create(
        self,
        db: AsyncSession,
        *,
        organization_id: UUID,
        agreement_id: UUID,
        source_version_id: UUID,
        title: str,
        description: str,
        frequency: ObligationFrequency,
        trigger_type: ObligationTrigger,
        trigger_definition: dict | None,
        recurrence_rule: dict | None,
        requires_evidence: bool,
        evidence_definition: dict | None,
        assignee_user_id: UUID | None,
        responsible_party_id: UUID | None,
        source_reference: dict,
        created_by: UUID,
    ) -> Obligation:

        obligation = Obligation(
            organization_id=organization_id,
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            source_version_id=source_version_id,
            title=title,
            description=description,
            status=ObligationStatus.DRAFT,
            frequency=frequency,
            recurrence_rule=recurrence_rule,
            trigger_type=trigger_type,
            trigger_definition=trigger_definition,
            requires_evidence=requires_evidence,
            evidence_definition=evidence_definition,
            assignee_user_id=assignee_user_id,
            responsible_party_id=responsible_party_id,
            source_reference=source_reference,
            created_by=created_by,
        )

        db.add(obligation)

        await db.flush()

        return obligation
3.13.9 Activation checks

An obligation cannot become ACTIVE just because someone clicked a button.

Validate:

agreement exists
↓
agreement belongs to workspace
↓
source version exists
↓
source version is valid
↓
responsible party/assignee exists when required
↓
due/trigger configuration valid
↓
recurrence configuration valid
↓
evidence configuration valid
↓
no stale source version
↓
activate
3.13.10 Recurrence engine

The recurrence engine must not use hidden defaults.

Example stored rule:

{
  "frequency": "MONTHLY",
  "interval": 1,
  "day_of_month": 15
}

Or:

{
  "frequency": "QUARTERLY",
  "interval": 1,
  "month_offset": 0,
  "day": 10
}

Or custom:

{
  "frequency": "CUSTOM",
  "rule": "..."
}

The service owns validation for the supported rule vocabulary.

3.13.11 Generate obligation instances
recurrence.py
from datetime import date, timedelta
from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta


class RecurrenceEngine:

    def next_period(
        self,
        *,
        previous_start: date | None,
        previous_end: date | None,
        rule: dict,
    ) -> tuple[date, date]:

        frequency = rule.get("frequency")
        interval = rule.get("interval", 1)

        if not isinstance(interval, int) or interval <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Invalid recurrence interval")

        if previous_start is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Previous period required for recurring calculation"
            )

        if previous_end is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Previous period end required"
            )

        if frequency == "DAILY":

            start = previous_end + timedelta(days=1)
            end = start

        elif frequency == "WEEKLY":

            start = previous_end + timedelta(days=1)
            end = start + timedelta(days=6)

        elif frequency == "MONTHLY":

            start = previous_end + timedelta(days=1)
            end = start + relativedelta(months=interval) - timedelta(days=1)

        elif frequency == "QUARTERLY":

            start = previous_end + timedelta(days=1)
            end = start + relativedelta(
                months=3 * interval
            ) - timedelta(days=1)

        elif frequency == "YEARLY":

            start = previous_end + timedelta(days=1)
            end = start + relativedelta(
                years=interval
            ) - timedelta(days=1)

        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported recurrence frequency: {frequency}"
            )

        return start, end

The production implementation should handle month-end and leap-year boundaries explicitly.

3.13.12 Database idempotency

Do not let the scheduler create duplicates.

The constraint:

UniqueConstraint(
    "obligation_id",
    "period_start",
    "period_end",
)

means:

worker 1 → creates Q1
worker 2 → attempts Q1
worker 2 → DB rejects duplicate

The service catches the conflict and treats it as already processed.

3.13.13 Obligation → task generation

One active obligation instance can create one or more tasks.

Example:

Obligation:
"Submit quarterly compliance report"

Instance:
2027-01-01 → 2027-03-31

Tasks:
1. Collect source data
2. Prepare report
3. Internal review
4. Submit report

These task definitions can eventually come from configurable obligation playbooks.

For the initial implementation:

one obligation instance → one primary task

is sufficient.

Task creation
async def create_task_for_instance(
    db,
    *,
    instance,
    obligation,
):

    task = ObligationTask(
        organization_id=instance.organization_id,
        obligation_id=obligation.id,
        obligation_instance_id=instance.id,
        title=obligation.title,
        description=obligation.description,
        assigned_to=obligation.assignee_user_id,
        due_at=instance.due_at,
        status=TaskStatus.TODO,
    )

    db.add(task)

    await db.flush()

    return task
3.13.14 Task state machine
TASK_TRANSITIONS = {
    TaskStatus.TODO: {
        TaskStatus.IN_PROGRESS,
        TaskStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    TaskStatus.IN_PROGRESS: {
        TaskStatus.BLOCKED,
        TaskStatus.COMPLETED,
        TaskStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    TaskStatus.BLOCKED: {
        TaskStatus.IN_PROGRESS,
        TaskStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    TaskStatus.COMPLETED: set(),
    TaskStatus.CANCELLED: set(),
}

Never accept:

completed → todo

through the normal API.

Historical state transitions belong in activity/audit.

3.13.15 Completing an obligation

An obligation instance should not become completed just because a task was marked completed.

Evaluate:

Task completed?
+
Required evidence supplied?
+
Required evidence verified?
+
Required workflow approvals?
+
No unresolved blocking exception?

Then:

FULFILLED

Otherwise:

COMPLETED TASK
      ↓
evaluation
      ↓
awaiting evidence

This avoids false fulfillment.

3.13.16 Evidence

Evidence can reference the repository system already created in 3.8.

For example:

Obligation Instance
      ↓
Evidence
      ↓
Agreement Document
      ↓
Private Object Storage

Do not duplicate the uploaded file.

Store:

document_id

and derive access through the existing document authorization model.

3.13.17 Evidence service
class ObligationEvidenceService:

    async def attach_document(
        self,
        db,
        *,
        user,
        instance,
        document,
    ):

        await self._authorize_document(
            user=user,
            document=document,
            instance=instance,
        )

        evidence = ObligationEvidence(
            organization_id=instance.organization_id,
            obligation_instance_id=instance.id,
            document_id=document.id,
            evidence_type=EvidenceType.DOCUMENT,
            value={
                "document_id": str(document.id)
            },
            uploaded_by=user.id,
        )

        db.add(evidence)

        await db.flush()

        return evidence

No second storage system.

3.13.18 Evidence verification

Some obligations require confirmation that evidence is sufficient.

Example flow:

Evidence submitted
       ↓
PENDING
       ↓
Reviewer checks
    /      \
VERIFY     REJECT
   │          │
   ▼          ▼
VERIFIED   REJECTED

Rejected evidence should remain historically visible.

Do not physically delete it.

3.13.19 Exceptions

A missed obligation should create an exception.

Example:

due date reached
     ↓
not completed
     ↓
MISSED_DEADLINE
     ↓
OPEN exception
     ↓
assigned investigator
     ↓
resolution
exceptions.py
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from .models import ObligationException
from .enums import ExceptionType, ExceptionStatus


async def open_exception(
    db,
    *,
    instance,
    opened_by,
    exception_type: ExceptionType,
    description: str,
):

    exception = ObligationException(
        organization_id=instance.organization_id,
        obligation_instance_id=instance.id,
        exception_type=exception_type,
        status=ExceptionStatus.OPEN,
        description=description,
        opened_by=opened_by.id,
    )

    instance.exception_open = True

    db.add(exception)

    await db.flush()

    return exception
3.13.20 Breach detection

Be careful here.

The platform can detect:

deadline missed
required evidence missing
task incomplete
configured acceptance criteria failed

But it should not automatically claim:

“The counterparty breached the contract.”

Instead use:

OPERATIONAL_EXCEPTION
POSSIBLE_NON_COMPLIANCE

until the appropriate authorized user/workflow determines the contractual status.

This keeps the system operationally useful without turning an internal classifier into an unsupported legal conclusion.

3.13.21 Performance tracking

Now we can calculate real performance metrics.

For each obligation:

Total instances
Completed
On time
Late
Overdue
Exceptions
Waived
Evidence rejection rate
Average completion delay

Example:

Compliance Reporting

Instances             12
Completed             11
On time               10
Late                   1
Overdue                0
Exceptions             1

On-time rate        90.9%

These are calculated from actual system records.

3.13.22 Performance service
performance.py
from sqlalchemy import select, func

from .models import ObligationInstance
from .enums import ObligationInstanceStatus


class ObligationPerformanceService:

    async def summary(
        self,
        db,
        *,
        organization_id,
        obligation_id,
    ):

        result = await db.execute(
            select(
                func.count(ObligationInstance.id).label("total"),

                func.count(
                    ObligationInstance.id
                ).filter(
                    ObligationInstance.status
                    == ObligationInstanceStatus.COMPLETED
                ).label("completed"),

                func.count(
                    ObligationInstance.id
                ).filter(
                    ObligationInstance.status
                    == ObligationInstanceStatus.OVERDUE
                ).label("overdue"),

                func.count(
                    ObligationInstance.id
                ).filter(
                    ObligationInstance.status
                    == ObligationInstanceStatus.BREACHED
                ).label("breached"),
            )
            .where(
                ObligationInstance.organization_id
                == organization_id,
                ObligationInstance.obligation_id
                == obligation_id,
            )
        )

        row = result.one()

        total = row.total or 0
        completed = row.completed or 0

        completion_rate = (
            completed / total * 100
            if total
            else None
        )

        return {
            "total": total,
            "completed": completed,
            "overdue": row.overdue or 0,
            "breached": row.breached or 0,
            "completion_rate": completion_rate,
        }

Do not label a None metric as 0%. No instances means there is no measured performance.

3.13.23 SLA versus contractual obligation

Do not mix:

internal SLA

with:

contractual obligation

Example:

Contract says:
"Customer must provide report by the 15th."

Workspace policy says:
"Internal owner reviews evidence within 2 business days."

These are two different things.

The database should keep source/provenance separate.

3.13.24 Task assignment

Task assignment must verify:

user
 ↓
workspace membership
 ↓
active member
 ↓
authorized role

For counterparty-responsible obligations:

responsible_party_id

is not a substitute for an application user.

That party may not have an Agreement account at all.

So the system can represent:

Responsible party = External Supplier
Internal task owner = Procurement Manager
3.13.25 External obligation participation

Later, a counterparty can get a restricted external portal.

For now:

internal user
    ↓
task ownership

and:

external party
    ↓
responsible party record

remain separate.

Never automatically turn a party record into an authenticated user.

3.13.26 Version handling

This is another critical rule.

Suppose:

Agreement Version 5
↓
Obligation:
"Monthly report"

Then Version 6 changes it to:

"Quarterly report"

The previous obligation must not silently mutate.

Instead:

Version 5 obligation
       ↓
SUPERSEDED

Version 6 obligation
       ↓
ACTIVE

Historical instances remain attached to Version 5.

3.13.27 Amendment processing

When a new agreement version becomes current:

new version
    ↓
find obligations sourced from previous version
    ↓
determine whether affected
    ↓
supersede affected obligations
    ↓
create replacement obligations
    ↓
cancel future instances
    ↓
preserve completed history

Do not rewrite historical performance.

3.13.28 Lifecycle integration

3.12 and 3.13 now connect:

Lifecycle ACTIVE
       ↓
Obligations ACTIVE
       ↓
Generate instances

When agreement becomes:

SUSPENDED

the system can apply the configured suspension behavior.

It should not automatically suspend obligations unless the obligation policy says it is suspension-sensitive.

Likewise:

EXPIRED

doesn't necessarily erase historical obligations.

It means:

future contractual activity

must be evaluated according to the agreement's lifecycle rules.

3.13.29 Scheduler

Create:

# backend/app/obligations/tasks.py

from celery import shared_task


@shared_task(
    bind=True,
    autoretry_for=(Exception,),
    retry_backoff=True,
    max_retries=5,
)
def scan_obligations(self):
    import asyncio

    asyncio.run(_scan())


async def _scan():

    from datetime import datetime, timezone

    from sqlalchemy import select

    from app.db.session import async_session_factory
    from .models import ObligationInstance
    from .service import ObligationSchedulerService

    async with async_session_factory() as db:

        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        result = await db.execute(
            select(ObligationInstance)
            .where(
                ObligationInstance.due_at <= now,
                ObligationInstance.status.in_([
                    "PENDING",
                    "IN_PROGRESS",
                ]),
            )
            .with_for_update(
                skip_locked=True
            )
        )

        instances = list(result.scalars())

        service = ObligationSchedulerService()

        for instance in instances:
            await service.process_due_instance(
                db,
                instance,
            )

        await db.commit()
3.13.30 Due-instance processing
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from .enums import (
    ObligationInstanceStatus,
    ExceptionType,
)


class ObligationSchedulerService:

    async def process_due_instance(
        self,
        db,
        instance,
    ):

        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        if (
            instance.status
            in {
                ObligationInstanceStatus.COMPLETED,
                ObligationInstanceStatus.WAIVED,
                ObligationInstanceStatus.CANCELLED,
            }
        ):
            return

        if instance.due_at and instance.due_at < now:

            instance.status = (
                ObligationInstanceStatus.OVERDUE
            )

            await self._ensure_exception(
                db,
                instance,
                ExceptionType.MISSED_DEADLINE,
            )

The production version should distinguish "overdue but still fulfillable" from a configured contractual breach state.

3.13.37 Authorization

The permission chain remains:

authenticated user
        ↓
workspace membership
        ↓
agreement belongs to workspace
        ↓
agreement participant / role
        ↓
obligation access

For example:

VIEW
→ can_view

CREATE OBLIGATION
→ can_edit / configured workflow permission

COMPLETE TASK
→ task assignee OR delegated permission

VERIFY EVIDENCE
→ reviewer / workflow permission

RESOLVE EXCEPTION
→ configured operational permission

WAIVE OBLIGATION
→ privileged approval permission

A client must never send:

{
  "organization_id": "..."
}

and have the server trust it.
