3.21.47 Source highlighting

Click candidate:

Effective date

The viewer jumps to:

page 3
coordinates

and highlights the exact source region.

This is one of the most important trust mechanisms.

3.21.48 Extraction progress

Show actual stages:

✓ File received
✓ Security scan
✓ File validated
✓ Text extraction
✓ OCR
✓ Layout analysis
✓ Clause segmentation
● Fact extraction
○ Validation
○ Review

Do not show 100% until the job genuinely reaches the completed state.

3.21.49 Ingestion API
POST /api/agreements/{id}/documents/import

GET  /api/ingestion/{job_id}
GET  /api/ingestion/{job_id}/progress

GET  /api/ingestion/{job_id}/clauses
GET  /api/ingestion/{job_id}/candidates
GET  /api/ingestion/{job_id}/conflicts

POST /api/ingestion/candidates/{id}/verify
POST /api/ingestion/candidates/{id}/reject

POST /api/ingestion/conflicts/{id}/resolve

POST /api/ingestion/{job_id}/retry
3.21.50 Import endpoint
@router.post(
    "/agreements/{agreement_id}/documents/import"
)
async def import_document(
    agreement_id: UUID,
    payload: ImportRequest,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    user=Depends(get_current_user),
):

    agreement = await require_agreement_permission(
        db,
        user=user,
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        permission="can_edit",
    )

    document = await document_service.resolve_uploaded_document(
        db,
        payload.document_id,
        agreement.id,
    )

    await document_service.require_clean(
        document
    )

    job = await ingestion_service.create_job(
        db,
        agreement=agreement,
        document=document,
        user=user,
    )

    await outbox_service.publish(
        db,
        event_type="INGESTION_REQUESTED",
        resource_id=job.id,
    )

    await db.commit()

    return job
3.21.51 Document ownership

Imported documents must already belong to the correct workspace.

Reject:

document from another workspace

even if the user happens to know its ID.

3.21.52 Ingestion task
@shared_task(
    bind=True,
    autoretry_for=(Exception,),
    retry_backoff=True,
    max_retries=5,
)
def process_ingestion(
    self,
    ingestion_job_id: str,
):

    import asyncio

    asyncio.run(
        _process_ingestion(
            ingestion_job_id
        )
    )
3.21.53 Pipeline implementation
class IngestionPipeline:

    async def process(
        self,
        db,
        job,
    ):

        try:

            await self.security_scan(
                db,
                job,
            )

            await self.validate_file(
                db,
                job,
            )

            extracted = await self.extract_text(
                db,
                job,
            )

            structured = await self.analyze_layout(
                db,
                job,
                extracted,
            )

            clauses = await self.segment_clauses(
                db,
                job,
                structured,
            )

            candidates = await self.extract_facts(
                db,
                job,
                clauses,
            )

            await self.validate_candidates(
                db,
                job,
                candidates,
            )

            await self.complete(
                db,
                job,
            )

        except Exception as exc:

            await self.fail(
                db,
                job,
                exc,
            )

            raise
3.21.54 Pipeline idempotency

Each stage must be idempotent.

For example:

EXTRACTION artifact exists
       ↓
don't extract again

unless:

extractor version changed
source hash changed
explicit reprocess
3.21.55 Parser versioning

Store:

parser version
OCR version
clause segmentation version
fact extraction model
extraction policy version

This allows later reproducibility.

3.21.56 Reprocessing

Suppose a better parser is deployed.

Do not modify the existing extraction artifact.

Create:

Extraction v1
     ↓
Extraction v2

Then compare results.

Existing verified domain facts remain unchanged until a user explicitly verifies a new candidate.

3.21.57 Re-extraction after document correction

If the uploaded document itself was wrong:

Document A
   ↓
replace / new document
   ↓
Document B

Do not mutate the existing extraction history.

Create a new ingestion job.

3.21.58 Clause-to-agreement mapping

Once candidates are verified, they can be associated with the structured agreement document.

For a block-based Agreement editor:

source document clause
       ↓
verified source reference
       ↓
agreement block

This association should only happen when the user explicitly imports/builds the agreement from the source.

The uploaded original document remains preserved.

3.21.59 Do not overwrite original contracts

Never:

upload contract
↓
AI extracts
↓
overwrite original

Instead:

Original uploaded document
        ↓
Immutable repository document
        ↓
Extraction layer
        ↓
Structured intelligence

The original remains evidence.

3.21.60 OCR errors

The system should detect suspicious OCR.

Examples:

very low OCR confidence
unusual character substitutions
missing pages
empty pages
garbled tables

Then create:

EXTRACTION_QUALITY_WARNING

rather than blindly extracting facts.

3.21.61 Page-count verification

Before extraction:

declared pages
actual pages

Check for:

missing page numbers
duplicate pages
unreadable pages

If the PDF has 72 pages but page extraction returns only 70, ingestion should not silently proceed as if complete.

3.21.62 Document quality score

Keep quality separate from semantic confidence.

Document Quality
93%

OCR Quality
88%

Clause Segmentation
97%

Extraction Confidence
91%

These metrics answer different questions.

3.21.63 Extraction quality model
class ExtractionQuality:

    def calculate(
        self,
        *,
        page_coverage,
        text_coverage,
        ocr_quality,
        structural_quality,
    ):

        return {
            "page_coverage": page_coverage,
            "text_coverage": text_coverage,
            "ocr_quality": ocr_quality,
            "structural_quality": structural_quality,
        }

Don't collapse the metrics into one score unless a policy explicitly defines how.

3.21.64 Table extraction

Contracts often contain:

pricing tables
service levels
milestones
payment schedules
renewal schedules

Table extraction needs:

rows
columns
cells
coordinates
headers
merged-cell relationships

Preserve the original table structure as much as possible.

3.21.65 Table provenance

A candidate extracted from:

Page 18
Table 2
Row 4
Column 3

should preserve:

{
  "page": 18,
  "table_id": "...",
  "row": 4,
  "column": 3
}

This lets a reviewer jump directly to the source.

3.21.66 Header/footer filtering

Repeated headers and footers can pollute extraction.

Do not delete them from the original artifact.

Instead mark:

block_type = HEADER
block_type = FOOTER

and exclude them from semantic contract text where appropriate.

3.21.67 Page numbers

Detect page-number blocks so:

"12"

doesn't become an extracted contractual amount or clause.

3.21.68 Candidate deduplication

Multiple extraction systems may identify the same fact.

Example:

Parser:
expiry date = 2028-12-31

LLM:
expiry date = 2028-12-31

Keep both evidence paths, but group them into one candidate family.

3.21.69 Candidate family
class ExtractionCandidateGroup(Base):

    __tablename__ = "extraction_candidate_groups"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(

This lets the UI show:

Expiry Date

2 extraction sources agree

or:

2 extraction sources disagree
3.21.70 Agreement metadata extraction

Verified metadata can update:

agreement title
reference number
description
agreement type

but use optimistic concurrency.

If a human edited the agreement meanwhile:

return 409

and ask the reviewer to reconcile.

Never silently overwrite user changes.

3.21.71 Import into agreement creation

For a completely new external contract:

Upload document
      ↓
extract
      ↓
review
      ↓
create agreement

Only after required candidates are verified should the platform create the authoritative agreement data.

3.21.72 Import workflow
UPLOAD
 ↓
SCAN
 ↓
EXTRACT
 ↓
REVIEW
 ↓
VERIFY
 ↓
CREATE AGREEMENT
 ↓
RUN RISK ANALYSIS
 ↓
CREATE LIFECYCLE
 ↓
CREATE OBLIGATIONS

This avoids creating a misleading agreement record before its source has been inspected.

3.21.73 Existing agreement ingestion

For an existing Agreement:

existing agreement
      ↓
upload source contract
      ↓
link document
      ↓
extract
      ↓
compare against current structured agreement

This is useful for migrating legacy contract repositories.

3.21.74 Extraction versus migration

These are different operations.

INGESTION
→ understand document

MIGRATION
→ promote verified data into Agreement domain

Keep the operations separate.

3.21.75 Migration preview

Before promoting many records:

Migration Preview

Agreements detected: 134

Metadata candidates:
124 complete
10 ambiguous

Lifecycle:
118 complete
16 missing/conflicting

Obligations:
...

Only explicit approval should start the migration.

3.21.76 Bulk ingestion

For enterprise imports:

Import batch
   ↓
document queue
   ↓
workers
   ↓
individual ingestion jobs
   ↓
candidate aggregation
   ↓
review queue

Never place an entire customer repository inside one massive transaction.

3.21.77 Ingestion batch
class IngestionBatch(Base):

3.21.78 Batch isolation

Each document gets an independent ingestion job.

One bad PDF should not stop:

document 1
document 2
document 3
...

from processing.

3.21.79 Ingestion search

3.9 search can index:

extracted clauses
verified metadata
candidate status
document titles

Do not index rejected candidates as authoritative agreement facts.

3.21.80 Risk extraction integration

After verified clause extraction:

Clause
 ↓
3.14 risk analysis

AI extraction should not directly create a final risk finding.

Instead:

extracted candidate
 ↓
source validation
 ↓
risk analyzer
 ↓
risk finding
3.21.81 Lifecycle integration

Verified lifecycle candidates:

effective date
expiry date
renewal rule
notice period

flow into 3.12.

Then:

Lifecycle recalculation
 ↓
new deadlines
 ↓
notifications
3.21.82 Obligation integration

Verified obligation candidates flow into 3.13:

Clause
 ↓
verified obligation
 ↓
instances
 ↓
tasks
3.21.83 Automation protection

3.19 automation must not trigger contractual actions from a raw extraction candidate.

Allowed:

Extraction candidate verified
      ↓
domain event
      ↓
automation

Not:

LLM extracted candidate
      ↓
automation

This is an important safety boundary.

3.21.84 Source-grounded document intelligence

Every authoritative fact should be traceable through:

Agreement
  ↓
Agreement Version
  ↓
Lifecycle/Obligation/Risk
  ↓
Verified extraction
  ↓
Source document
  ↓
Page
  ↓
Block
  ↓
Exact source region

That is the provenance chain.

3.21.89 Policy examples

The policy can control:

It must not allow arbitrary executable code.

3.21.90 Automatic promotion rules

For some low-risk metadata, an organization may choose:

high-confidence + deterministic source
→ auto-promote

For contractual terms:

human verification required

The policy decides.

The platform should default to the safer behavior.

3.21.91 Example promotion policy
{
  "metadata": {
    "reference_number": {
      "auto_promote": true
    }
  },
  "lifecycle_terms": {
    "auto_promote": false
  },
  "obligations": {
    "auto_promote": false
  },
  "risk_findings": {
    "auto_promote": false
  }
}

This does not invent any business data.

It configures processing behavior.

3.21.92 External source verification

A document may itself reference:

company registration number
tax identifier
government filing
license
certificate

A future connector may verify it against an authoritative external source.

The result should be:

OBSERVED
VERIFIED EXTERNALLY

not automatically overwrite the contract party data.

3.21.93 Document ingestion plus web/external research

Where configured, the system may retrieve public sources to investigate a candidate.

Example:

party candidate
 ↓
configured external registry
 ↓
actual returned record
 ↓
comparison
 ↓
verification candidate

Record:

source
URL/reference
retrieved_at
provider
response hash

No unverified web result becomes authoritative by itself.

3.21.94 Extraction confidence versus source reliability

Keep these separate.

Extraction confidence: 0.94
Source reliability: VERIFIED

versus:

Extraction confidence: 0.98
Source reliability: USER-UPLOADED DOCUMENT

A high-confidence model reading an unreliable/ambiguous source does not make the source reliable.

3.21.95 Candidate review priority

Review queue can prioritize:

contractual impact
confidence
conflict
business importance
risk category
deadline proximity

Example:

CRITICAL REVIEW

Conflicting expiry dates
Agreement expires soon

The user can work on the most important unresolved facts first.

3.21.96 Review priority policy

Again configurable:

class ExtractionReviewPriorityService:

    def calculate(
        self,
        *,
        candidate,
        agreement_context,
        policy,
    ):

        score = 0

        score += policy[
            "candidate_type_weights"
        ].get(
            candidate.candidate_type,
            0,
        )

        if candidate.confidence is not None:
            score += (
                1 - candidate.confidence
            ) * policy[
                "uncertainty_weight"
            ]

        return round(score, 4)
3.21.97 No fabricated fallback values

This milestone must enforce:

missing expiry date
→ missing

unknown party identifier
→ unknown

unreadable clause
→ unreadable

ambiguous amount
→ requires review

conflicting dates
→ conflict

Never:

TBD
N/A
30 days
unknown company
default currency
default renewal period

unless those are literally present in the source or explicitly configured.

3.21.103 API authorization

Only users with:

can_edit

can import a contract into an agreement.

Only users with configured workflow/verification permissions can:

verify candidates
resolve conflicts
promote contractual facts

The system does not trust:

candidate.verified = true

from the browser.

3.21.104 Candidate verification transaction

The promotion should be atomic:

BEGIN
   │
   ├── lock candidate
   ├── verify source
   ├── verify current agreement version
   ├── create authoritative fact
   ├── create provenance
   ├── update candidate
   ├── audit
   └── outbox
COMMIT

This prevents:

candidate VERIFIED
but domain fact missing

from becoming possible.

3.21.105 Optimistic concurrency

Suppose an administrator changes an agreement while extraction review is open.

Candidate references:

Version 8

but current agreement is:

Version 9

The promotion must fail with:

STALE_SOURCE_VERSION

The user then reviews the candidate against the new version.

3.21.106 Bulk verification

For candidates with identical deterministic evidence:

10 metadata candidates

the system may allow bulk verification if policy permits.

For contractual obligations and lifecycle terms, safer default:

individual verification

3.21.115 Performance

Large documents should be streamed through the pipeline.

Avoid:

entire_pdf.read()

into memory for very large files.

Use:

private storage
 ↓
stream/page chunks
 ↓
worker-local temporary storage

with cleanup after processing.

3.21.116 Resource limits

Configure:

maximum file size
maximum pages
maximum OCR time
maximum extracted text size
maximum table size
maximum model context

These are system safety limits, not contractual values.

3.21.117 Parsing malicious documents

A document may contain:

malformed PDF structures
zip bombs
decompression bombs
embedded scripts
recursive references
huge image dimensions

File validation and sandboxing must reject or contain these before normal parsing.

3.21.118 Extraction cache

You can cache extraction artifacts keyed by:

document_hash
parser_version
ocr_version
extraction_policy_version

Same source + same extraction configuration can reuse the result.

But cache hits must still remain scoped by organization/security policy.

3.21.119 No cross-tenant extraction cache leakage

Never use:

sha256(document)

alone as a global cache key.

Use:

organization_id
+
document_hash
+
extractor_version
+
policy_version

3.22 — Contract Change Management, Amendments, Redlines & Version Intelligence

The platform can already create immutable versions. This milestone adds the controlled change system around them.

The central chain becomes:

Existing Agreement
       ↓
Change Request / Amendment
       ↓
Source Document
       ↓
Structural Diff
       ↓
Semantic Diff
       ↓
Impact Analysis
       ↓
Review
       ↓
Approval
       ↓
New Immutable Version
       ↓
Recalculate Dependencies
       ↓
Lifecycle / Obligations / Monitoring / Risk / Graph

The key rule remains:

A proposed change is not the new contract. Only an approved immutable agreement version becomes authoritative.

3.22.1 What this milestone adds

The system will support:

Amendment requests
Change requests
Side-by-side version comparison
Clause-level redlines
Insertions
Deletions
Modifications
Moved clauses
Metadata changes
Lifecycle changes
Obligation changes
Party changes
Risk changes
Impact analysis
Approval of amendments
Change rationale
Change provenance
Change packages
Downstream recalculation

It should also answer:

What changed?

Who changed it?

Why did they change it?

Which exact version contained the change?

Which obligations changed because of it?

Which deadlines must be recalculated?

Which monitoring rules became stale?

Which risks changed?

3.22.4 Change request model

A change request is not itself a contract version.

from datetime import datetime
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import (
    DateTime,
    ForeignKey,
    Integer,
    String,
    Text,
    text,
)
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import (
    JSONB,
    UUID as PGUUID,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.db.base import Base


class ChangeRequest(Base):

    __tablename__ = "change_requests"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        primary_key=True,
        default=uuid4,
    )

    organization_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey(
            "organizations.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
    )

    agreement_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey(
            "agreements.id",
            ondelete="CASCADE",
        ),
        nullable=False,
    )

    base_version_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey(
            "agreement_versions.id",
            ondelete="RESTRICT",
        ),
        nullable=False,
    )

    proposed_version_id: Mapped[UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey(
            "agreement_versions.id",
            ondelete="RESTRICT",
        ),
    )

    request_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(64),
        nullable=False,
    )

    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(64),
        nullable=False,
    )

    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(500),
        nullable=False,
    )

    reason: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    requested_changes: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
        nullable=False,
    )

    source_reference: Mapped[dict | None] = mapped_column(
        JSONB,
    )

    created_by: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PGUUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
        server_default=text("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"),
    )

    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
        server_default=text("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"),
    )
3.22.5 Why proposed versions are separate

Suppose current version is:

Version 10

An editor creates proposed changes:

Change Request 17

It should produce:

Version 11 — PROPOSED

but Version 10 remains current.

Only after approval:

Version 11 → CURRENT

This prevents half-finished changes from affecting live lifecycle and obligation processing.

3.22.6 Proposed version state

Your existing agreement_versions table should be extended with a controlled state.

For example:

class AgreementVersionState(StrEnum):
    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    PROPOSED = "PROPOSED"
    APPROVED = "APPROVED"
    CURRENT = "CURRENT"
    SUPERSEDED = "SUPERSEDED"
    VOIDED = "VOIDED"

The actual state vocabulary should be integrated with the existing version implementation rather than creating a duplicate version table.

3.22.8 Structural diff engine

The structured editor from 3.2 already uses stable block IDs.

That makes structural comparison much more reliable.

Compare:

Version 10
   ↓
blocks[]

Version 11
   ↓
blocks[]

using block IDs.

3.22.9 Structural diff
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BlockDiff:

    block_id: str

    change_type: DiffChangeType

    before: dict | None
    after: dict | None

    old_index: int | None
    new_index: int | None


class StructuralDiffEngine:

    def compare(
        self,
        old_document: dict,
        new_document: dict,
    ) -> list[BlockDiff]:

        old_blocks = {
            block["id"]: (
                index,
                block,
            )
            for index, block
            in enumerate(
                old_document.get(
                    "blocks",
                    [],
                )
            )
        }

        new_blocks = {
            block["id"]: (
                index,
                block,
            )
            for index, block
            in enumerate(
                new_document.get(
                    "blocks",
                    [],
                )
            )
        }

        results = []

        all_ids = (
            set(old_blocks)
            | set(new_blocks)
        )

        for block_id in all_ids:

            old = old_blocks.get(block_id)
            new = new_blocks.get(block_id)

            if old is None:

                results.append(
                    BlockDiff(
                        block_id=block_id,
                        change_type=DiffChangeType.INSERTED,
                        before=None,
                        after=new[1],
                        old_index=None,
                        new_index=new[0],
                    )
                )

                continue

            if new is None:

                results.append(
                    BlockDiff(
                        block_id=block_id,
                        change_type=DiffChangeType.DELETED,
                        before=old[1],
                        after=None,
                        old_index=old[0],
                        new_index=None,
                    )
                )

                continue

            if old[1] != new[1]:

                change_type = (
                    DiffChangeType.MOVED
                    if old[1] == new[1]
                    else DiffChangeType.MODIFIED
                )

                results.append(
                    BlockDiff(
                        block_id=block_id,
                        change_type=change_type,
                        before=old[1],
                        after=new[1],
                        old_index=old[0],
                        new_index=new[0],
                    )
                )

        return results

There is an important correction here: the MOVED condition cannot be based on old[1] == new[1] inside the "content changed" branch. A better implementation separates content equality and position changes:

content_same = old[1] == new[1]
position_changed = old[0] != new[0]

if content_same and position_changed:
    change_type = DiffChangeType.MOVED
elif not content_same:
    change_type = DiffChangeType.MODIFIED
else:
    change_type = DiffChangeType.UNCHANGED

Use that corrected logic in production.

3.22.10 Corrected structural comparison
def compare_block(
    old,
    new,
):

    old_index, old_block = old
    new_index, new_block = new

    content_same = (
        old_block == new_block
    )

    position_changed = (
        old_index != new_index
    )

    if content_same and position_changed:
        return DiffChangeType.MOVED

    if not content_same:
        return DiffChangeType.MODIFIED

    return DiffChangeType.UNCHANGED

This preserves actual semantic distinctions.

3.22.11 Text-level redline

For modified blocks, produce token/word-level differences.

Use an established diff algorithm instead of writing custom string matching.

from difflib import SequenceMatcher


def word_diff(
    before: str,
    after: str,
):

    old = before.split()
    new = after.split()

    matcher = SequenceMatcher(
        a=old,
        b=new,
    )

    changes = []

    for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in matcher.get_opcodes():

        changes.append({
            "operation": tag,
            "before": old[i1:i2],
            "after": new[j1:j2],
        })

    return changes

This is for display, not contractual interpretation.

3.22.15 Semantic diff

Structural diff tells you:

Block 17 changed.

Semantic diff should tell you:

Payment deadline changed.

or:

Renewal term changed.

The semantic layer maps actual content changes to business concepts.

3.22.25 Signing invalidation

This is particularly important.

If:

Version 11

is already approved for signing, and then a substantive amendment changes it:

Version 12

the signing package for Version 11 cannot remain valid.

Flow:

Version 11
   ↓
Execution package
   ↓
Change
   ↓
Version 12
   ↓
Version 11 package invalidated

The signing engine must create a new package from Version 12 if the new version is approved.

3.22.26 Signing invalidation implementation
async def invalidate_execution_for_new_version(
    db,
    agreement_id,
    old_version_id,
):

    packages = await get_active_packages(
        db,
        agreement_id=agreement_id,
        version_id=old_version_id,
    )

    for package in packages:

        await execution_service.cancel_for_version_change(
            db,
            package_id=package.id,
        )

This should use the 3.7 execution service.

3.22.27 Review invalidation

Likewise:

Version 10
 ↓
approval
 ↓
Version 11 changes content

Old approval must not authorize Version 11.

This already exists conceptually in 3.6.

3.22 should automate the invalidation:

new proposed version
   ↓
previous pending approval/review
   ↓
SUPERSEDED
3.22.28 Change approval

Change approval should integrate with the existing workflow engine.

Change Request
      ↓
review
      ↓
approval
      ↓
new version becomes current

Do not create another approval implementation.

3.22.29 Approval validator

Before applying a change:

base version still current?
proposed version immutable?
required reviews complete?
required approvals complete?
risk gate satisfied?
change conflicts resolved?
critical impact reviewed?

Then:

APPLY
3.22.30 Applying an approved change
async def apply_change_request(
    db,
    *,
    change_request_id,
    user,
):

    request = await load_for_update(
        db,
        change_request_id,
    )

    agreement = await get_agreement_for_update(
        db,
        request.agreement_id,
    )

    if (
        agreement.current_version_id
        != request.base_version_id
    ):
        raise StaleAgreementVersionError()

    await validate_change_approval(
        db,
        request,
    )

    version = await promote_proposed_version(
        db,
        request.proposed_version_id,
    )

    old_version_id = (
        agreement.current_version_id
    )

    agreement.current_version_id = version.id

    await create_change_history(
        db,
        request=request,
        old_version_id=old_version_id,
        new_version_id=version.id,
    )

    await emit_domain_event(
        db,
        event_type="AGREEMENT_VERSION_CHANGED",
        agreement_id=agreement.id,
        version_id=version.id,
    )

All of this belongs in one transaction.

3.22.32 Why a dedicated change history?

The version history answers:

What versions existed?

The change history answers:

What changed from Version A to Version B and why?

Those are different questions.

{
  "changed_blocks": 4,

business negotiation

@shared_task(

3.22.48 Impact worker flow
async def _analyze_change_impact(
    agreement_id,
    previous_version_id,
    new_version_id,
):

    async with async_session_factory() as db:

        diff = await change_service.calculate_diff(
            db,
            agreement_id=agreement_id,
            previous_version_id=previous_version_id,
            new_version_id=new_version_id,
        )

        impacts = await impact_service.calculate(
            db,
            diff=diff,
        )

        await impact_service.persist(
            db,
            impacts,
        )

        await db.commit()
3.22.49 Impact resolution rules

Start deterministically.

Examples:

expiry date changed
→ lifecycle

renewal rule changed
→ lifecycle + renewal

obligation clause changed
→ obligation review

party changed
→ party relationships + graph

liability clause changed
→ risk re-analysis

payment clause changed
→ payment risk + obligation review

document appendix changed
→ document relationship review

These mappings are configuration-backed where appropriate.

3.22.50 Stale monitoring rule

Suppose:

Version 8
required quantity = 100

Monitoring expects:

quantity >= 100

Then Version 9 changes:

required quantity = 150

The old monitoring configuration is now stale.

Set:

MONITORING_STALE

and require review.

Do not silently change the monitoring rule.

3.22.51 Stale obligation

Likewise:

Version 8
monthly obligation

Version 9
quarterly obligation

The old obligation becomes:

SUPERSEDED

and Version 9 produces the replacement obligation after verification.

Historical monthly instances remain intact.

3.22.52 Lifecycle recalculation

If:

expiry date changed

then:

old deadlines → CANCELLED
new deadlines → CREATED

with:

source_version_id = new version
3.22.53 Risk re-analysis

Version change automatically produces:

risk_analysis_requested

using:

new version hash
+
new policy version

Old findings become:

SUPERSEDED

and new findings are produced.

3.22.54 Graph update

The graph should:

supersede old version relationships where appropriate
create new version node
create new relevant edges
preserve historical edges

Do not physically delete old graph history.

3.22.55 Analytics update

3.17 metrics update only after the new version becomes authoritative.

A proposed change must not change portfolio analytics.

PROPOSED VERSION
     ↓
NO PORTFOLIO CHANGE

After approval/application:

CURRENT VERSION
     ↓
PORTFOLIO CHANGE
3.22.56 Change-level risk

3.14 should analyze not only the resulting contract but the change itself.

Example:

Change:
Liability cap removed

Possible finding:

HIGH
Liability exposure increased relative to previous version.

Evidence:

Version 10
+
Version 11
+
changed clause

This is more useful than only showing the final state.

3.22.63 Change creation

When a user edits current agreement content:

Current Version
     ↓
create draft/proposed document
     ↓
create proposed version
     ↓
create change request

Do not directly modify the current version.

3.22.64 Change request version binding

A change request stores:

base_version_id

This prevents:

User A edits Version 10
User B creates Version 11
User A submits changes against stale Version 10

The server returns:

409 STALE_BASE_VERSION

and requires rebasing.

3.22.65 Rebase

For a sophisticated implementation:

Change Request
      ↓
base Version 10
      │
      │ concurrent new Version 11
      ▼
rebase
      ↓
Version 11 → proposed changes

The rebase engine should first detect conflicts.

3.22.66 Change conflicts

Example:

User A changes:

Payment = 30 days

User B changes the same block:

Payment = 45 days

A rebase should result in:

CONFLICT

rather than silently choosing either.

3.22.72 Change approval gate

Before approval:

Required:

✓ Structural diff completed
✓ Semantic analysis completed
✓ Conflicts resolved
✓ Required reviewers completed
✓ Required impact reviews completed
✓ Required risk checks completed

Then approval becomes possible.

The exact gates come from workflow/policy.

3.22.73 Change application gate

Before making Version 11 current:

base version still current
proposed version immutable
approval current
no unresolved critical conflict
required signatures/approvals satisfied
required impact actions completed or acknowledged

Then:

Version 11 → CURRENT
3.22.74 Existing approvals

An old approval is never reused automatically.

Example:

Version 10
Approved

Version 11 proposed

means:

Version 11
NOT APPROVED

even if only one small clause changed.

Whether a change qualifies for an expedited review must be explicit policy.

3.22.75 Minor administrative changes

A workspace may configure an approval bypass for defined administrative fields.

Example:

reference_number formatting
internal description
display label

But even then:

change
+
policy
+
audit

must remain recorded.

Do not create a generic "minor change" bypass that can accidentally include legal clauses.

3.22.76 Change classification

The system can classify a change:

ADMINISTRATIVE
OPERATIONAL
SUBSTANTIVE
CRITICAL

The classification should come from policy + analysis.

Don't let a browser tell the server:

{
  "change_class": "ADMINISTRATIVE"
}

and automatically bypass review.

3.22.77 Risk gate

Connect 3.14:

      ↓
risk impact
      ↓
policy
      ↓
allowed?

Example:

Critical risk increased
       ↓
legal review required
       ↓
approval blocked until reviewed
3.22.78 Lifecycle gate

Connect 3.12:

renewal term changed
      ↓
lifecycle recalculation required
      ↓
impact review

If lifecycle recalculation fails, don't apply the version unless the configured policy allows it.

3.22.79 Obligation gate

Connect 3.13:

obligation clause changed
      ↓
obligation impact
      ↓
existing instances reviewed
      ↓
replacement obligation created

Completed historical instances remain immutable.

3.22.80 Monitoring gate

Connect 3.15:

contract field changed
      ↓
monitoring definition stale
      ↓
review
      ↓
update monitoring configuration

Do not silently adjust an external monitoring query.

3.22.81 Graph gate

Connect 3.16:

party changed
dependency changed
agreement reference changed
      ↓
graph recalculation

The graph preserves historical edges.

3.22.82 Analytics behavior

Connect 3.17:

Proposed:

not included in authoritative portfolio metrics

Applied:

included after event processing

This avoids dashboard numbers changing before the amendment is actually effective.

3.22.83 Forecasting behavior

Connect 3.18:

New applied version can invalidate relevant forecasts.

For example:

renewal term changes
      ↓
existing renewal forecast affected
      ↓
new forecast run

Historical forecast remains preserved.

3.22.84 Automation behavior

Connect 3.19:

Only:

AGREEMENT_VERSION_CHANGED

after application should trigger automation.

Not:

CHANGE_REQUEST_CREATED

unless the organization explicitly configures a pre-approval workflow.

This avoids operational side effects from unapproved proposals.

3.22.94 Final version/change model

The platform now distinguishes:

    │

This is a much stronger model than simply incrementing a version number after every edit.

      ↓

3.23 — Contract Negotiation Workspace, Clause Playbooks & Collaborative Redlining

This milestone turns the change-management engine from a simple proposal/review flow into a real negotiation system.

The critical rule is:

Negotiation data is not the contract.

Negotiators can propose, reject, accept, counter, comment, and track positions, but only the approved resulting immutable agreement version becomes authoritative.

That separation prevents a negotiation participant from accidentally changing the live contract.

1. What 3.23 adds

The architecture becomes:

Agreement
   │
   ├── Current immutable Version
   │
   └── Change Request
          │
          └── Negotiation
                 │
                 ├── Negotiation Rounds
                 │
                 ├── Negotiation Issues
                 │       │
                 │       ├── Clause
                 │       ├── Current Position
                 │       ├── Target Position
                 │       ├── Fallback Position
                 │       └── Proposals
                 │               ├── Accept
                 │               ├── Reject
                 │               └── Counter
                 │
                 ├── Private Internal Notes
                 ├── External Shared Discussion
                 ├── Playbook Guidance
                 ├── Concessions
                 └── Negotiation History
                          │
                          ▼
                   Proposed Version
                          │
                          ▼
                    Risk Analysis
                          │
                          ▼
                      Approval
                          │
                          ▼
               Authoritative New Version

The system must never let an external proposal directly mutate the authoritative agreement.

4. Database models
Negotiation
# backend/app/negotiation/models.py

from uuid import UUID
from datetime import datetime

from sqlalchemy import (
    String,
    Text,
    Integer,
    Boolean,
    ForeignKey,
    DateTime,
    JSON,
    UniqueConstraint,
    Index,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.db.base import Base
from app.negotiation.enums import (
    NegotiationStatus,
    NegotiationParticipantType,
    NegotiationParticipantRole,
    NegotiationRoundStatus,
    NegotiationIssueStatus,
    NegotiationIssuePriority,
    NegotiationActorType,
    ProposalStatus,
    ConcessionType,
    PlaybookPositionType,
    PlaybookStatus,
    NegotiationVisibility,
)


class Negotiation(Base):
    __tablename__ = "negotiations"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    organization_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("organizations.id"),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

    agreement_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("agreements.id"),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

    change_request_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("change_requests.id"),
        nullable=False,
        unique=True,
    )

11. Playbook matching

The system can find the best applicable playbook version from actual configuration.

def resolve_playbook(
    *,
    organization_id,
    agreement_type_id,
    jurisdiction: str | None,
    effective_at,
    session,
):
    query = (
        select(NegotiationPlaybookVersion)
        .join(
            NegotiationPlaybook,
            NegotiationPlaybook.current_version_id
            == NegotiationPlaybookVersion.id,
        )
        .where(
            NegotiationPlaybook.organization_id == organization_id,
            NegotiationPlaybookVersion.organization_id == organization_id,
            NegotiationPlaybookVersion.effective_from <= effective_at,
        )
    )

    if agreement_type_id is not None:
        query = query.where(
            NegotiationPlaybookVersion.agreement_type_id
            == agreement_type_id
        )

    if jurisdiction is not None:
        query = query.where(
            NegotiationPlaybookVersion.jurisdiction == jurisdiction
        )

    return session.scalars(
        query.order_by(
            NegotiationPlaybookVersion.version_number.desc()
        )
    ).first()

No artificial fallback playbook should be created.

If the organization has not configured one:

{
  "playbook": null,
  "reason": "NO_APPLICABLE_PLAYBOOK"
}
12. Negotiation permissions

This must sit above the ordinary CRUD layer.

async def assert_negotiation_access(
    principal,
    negotiation,
    *,
    action: str,
):
    await assert_workspace_membership(
        principal,
        negotiation.organization_id,
    )

    await assert_agreement_access(
        principal,
        negotiation.agreement_id,
        action=action,
    )

    if action == "VIEW_INTERNAL":
        await assert_internal_negotiation_permission(principal)

    elif action == "EDIT_INTERNAL":
        await assert_negotiation_editor(principal)

    elif action == "VIEW_EXTERNAL":
        await assert_external_grant(principal, negotiation)

    elif action == "EDIT_EXTERNAL":
        await assert_external_collaborator(principal, negotiation)
13. Visibility system

Every negotiation object should resolve visibility through one service.

def visible_to_actor(
    *,
    participant_type: NegotiationParticipantType,
    visibility: NegotiationVisibility,
    actor_is_internal: bool,
) -> bool:

    if visibility == NegotiationVisibility.INTERNAL:
        return actor_is_internal

    if visibility == NegotiationVisibility.SHARED:
        return True

    return False

Do not filter private information only in React.

The API must remove it before serialization.

14. Proposal submission

A proposal must bind to an exact version.

async def create_proposal(
    db,
    negotiation,
    issue,
    actor,
    proposed_text: str,
    rationale: str | None,
):
    if issue.status in {
        NegotiationIssueStatus.ACCEPTED,
        NegotiationIssueStatus.REJECTED,
        NegotiationIssueStatus.WITHDRAWN,
    }:
        raise DomainError("Issue is no longer negotiable.")

    actual_block = await get_block(
        db,
        issue.source_version_id,
        issue.block_id,
    )

    if actual_block is None:
        raise DomainError("Clause no longer exists in source version.")

    if actual_block["id"] != issue.block_id:
        raise DomainError("Block identity mismatch.")

    if normalize_text(actual_block["content"]) != normalize_text(
        issue.current_position
    ):
        raise StaleNegotiationIssueError(
            "The issue is based on an outdated version."
        )

    proposal = NegotiationProposal(
        id=uuid4(),
        issue_id=issue.id,
        negotiation_id=negotiation.id,
        organization_id=negotiation.organization_id,
        source_version_id=issue.source_version_id,
        source_block_id=issue.block_id,
        actor_type=resolve_actor_type(actor),
        actor_user_id=actor.user_id,
        actor_external_identity_id=actor.external_identity_id,
        before_text=actual_block["content"],
        proposed_text=proposed_text,
        rationale=rationale,
        status=ProposalStatus.SUBMITTED,
        created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    )

    db.add(proposal)

    issue.status = NegotiationIssueStatus.PROPOSED

    return proposal

Notice that the server reads the real block from the immutable version.

The browser does not get to define before_text.

15. Counterproposal

A counterproposal must point to its parent.

async def create_counterproposal(
    db,
    proposal,
    actor,
    proposed_text,
    rationale,
):
    if proposal.status != ProposalStatus.SUBMITTED:
        raise DomainError(
            "Only submitted proposals can be countered."
        )

    issue = await get_issue(db, proposal.issue_id)

    current_position = proposal.proposed_text

    counter = await create_proposal(
        db=db,
        negotiation=await get_negotiation(
            db,
            proposal.negotiation_id,
        ),
        issue=issue,
        actor=actor,
        proposed_text=proposed_text,
        rationale=rationale,
    )

    counter.parent_proposal_id = proposal.id

    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.SUPERSEDED

    issue.status = NegotiationIssueStatus.COUNTERED

    return counter

This produces a real negotiation tree rather than simply overwriting text.

16. Accepting a proposal

Accepting a redline must not immediately change the contract.

It changes the negotiation state.

async def accept_proposal(db, proposal_id, actor):
    proposal = await get_for_update(db, proposal_id)

    negotiation = await get_negotiation_for_update(
        db,
        proposal.negotiation_id,
    )

    issue = await get_issue_for_update(
        db,
        proposal.issue_id,
    )

    await assert_negotiation_action(
        actor,
        negotiation,
        "ACCEPT_PROPOSAL",
    )

    current_version = await get_current_version(
        db,
        negotiation.agreement_id,
    )

    if current_version.id != negotiation.base_version_id:
        raise StaleNegotiationError(
            "The agreement has changed since this negotiation started."
        )

    actual_block = await get_block(
        db,
        proposal.source_version_id,
        proposal.source_block_id,
    )

    if actual_block is None:
        raise StaleNegotiationError(
            "Source clause no longer exists."
        )

    if normalize_text(actual_block["content"]) != normalize_text(
        proposal.before_text
    ):
        raise StaleNegotiationError(
            "Proposal is based on stale clause content."
        )

    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.ACCEPTED

    issue.current_position = proposal.proposed_text
    issue.status = NegotiationIssueStatus.ACCEPTED

    await record_concession_if_needed(
        db,
        issue=issue,
        proposal=proposal,
        actor=actor,
    )

    return proposal

The actual agreement remains unchanged.

17. Rejecting a proposal
async def reject_proposal(
    db,
    proposal_id,
    actor,
    reason: str | None,
):
    proposal = await get_for_update(db, proposal_id)

    await assert_negotiation_action(
        actor,
        proposal.negotiation_id,
        "REJECT_PROPOSAL",
    )

    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REJECTED

    issue = await get_issue_for_update(
        db,
        proposal.issue_id,
    )

    issue.status = NegotiationIssueStatus.REJECTED

    await append_activity(
        db,
        negotiation_id=proposal.negotiation_id,
        event_type="PROPOSAL_REJECTED",
        actor=actor,
        payload={
            "proposal_id": str(proposal.id),
            "issue_id": str(issue.id),
            "reason": reason,
        },
    )
18. Accept Selected

Negotiators need the ability to accept specific clauses while leaving others unresolved.

async def accept_selected(
    db,
    negotiation_id,
    proposal_ids,
    actor,
):
    async with db.begin():
        negotiation = await get_negotiation_for_update(
            db,
            negotiation_id,
        )

        await assert_negotiation_action(
            actor,
            negotiation,
            "ACCEPT_PROPOSALS",
        )

        proposals = await get_proposals_for_update(
            db,
            negotiation_id,
            proposal_ids,
        )

        if len(proposals) != len(proposal_ids):
            raise DomainError(
                "One or more proposals do not belong to this negotiation."
            )

        for proposal in proposals:
            await accept_proposal(
                db,
                proposal.id,
                actor,
            )

Everything happens inside one transaction.

19. Accept All

Never blindly accept every proposal.

First validate:

async def validate_accept_all(db, negotiation):
    unresolved = await count_unresolved_issues(
        db,
        negotiation.id,
    )

    if unresolved:
        raise DomainError(
            "Negotiation contains unresolved issues."
        )

    conflicting = await find_proposal_conflicts(
        db,
        negotiation.id,
    )

    if conflicting:
        raise DomainError(
            "Negotiation contains conflicting proposals."
        )

    stale = await validate_all_proposal_versions(
        db,
        negotiation.id,
    )

    if stale:
        raise StaleNegotiationError(
            "One or more proposals are stale."
        )

Then compile.

20. Compile accepted redlines into a proposed version

The compiler is extremely important.

async def compile_negotiated_version(
    db,
    negotiation_id,
):
    negotiation = await get_negotiation(
        db,
        negotiation_id,
    )

    base_version = await get_version(
        db,
        negotiation.base_version_id,
    )

    document = deep_copy(base_version.content)

    accepted = await get_accepted_proposals(
        db,
        negotiation_id,
    )

    grouped = group_by_block(
        accepted,
    )

    for block_id, proposals in grouped.items():
        if len(proposals) != 1:
            raise CompilationConflict(
                f"Multiple accepted proposals for block {block_id}"
            )

        proposal = proposals[0]

        block = locate_block(
            document,
            block_id,
        )

        if block is None:
            raise CompilationConflict(
                f"Block {block_id} not found."
            )

        if normalize_text(block["content"]) != normalize_text(
            proposal.before_text
        ):
            raise CompilationConflict(
                f"Block {block_id} changed since proposal."
            )

        block["content"] = proposal.proposed_text

    validate_document_structure(document)

    return document

The compiler:

reads the real immutable version
checks every block
applies only accepted changes
detects stale content
detects conflicting proposals
validates document structure

It never directly modifies the original version.

21. Creating the proposed version

Use the existing agreement_versions service.

Do not insert another custom agreement-version implementation here.

async def create_negotiated_proposed_version(
    db,
    negotiation,
    actor,
):
    compiled_document = await compile_negotiated_version(
        db,
        negotiation.id,
    )

    proposed_version = await agreement_version_service.create_proposed_version(
        db=db,
        agreement_id=negotiation.agreement_id,
        source_version_id=negotiation.base_version_id,
        content=compiled_document,
        created_by=actor.user_id,
        source="NEGOTIATION",
    )

    negotiation.proposed_version_id = proposed_version.id

    return proposed_version

This keeps 3.22 as the owner of version creation.

22. Negotiation state machine

Never allow arbitrary status updates.

ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS = {
    NegotiationStatus.DRAFT: {
        NegotiationStatus.NEGOTIATING,
        NegotiationStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    NegotiationStatus.NEGOTIATING: {
        NegotiationStatus.INTERNAL_REVIEW,
        NegotiationStatus.EXTERNAL_REVIEW,
        NegotiationStatus.DEADLOCKED,
        NegotiationStatus.READY_FOR_APPROVAL,
        NegotiationStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    NegotiationStatus.INTERNAL_REVIEW: {
        NegotiationStatus.NEGOTIATING,
        NegotiationStatus.EXTERNAL_REVIEW,
        NegotiationStatus.READY_FOR_APPROVAL,
        NegotiationStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    NegotiationStatus.EXTERNAL_REVIEW: {
        NegotiationStatus.NEGOTIATING,
        NegotiationStatus.INTERNAL_REVIEW,
        NegotiationStatus.DEADLOCKED,
        NegotiationStatus.READY_FOR_APPROVAL,
        NegotiationStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    NegotiationStatus.DEADLOCKED: {
        NegotiationStatus.NEGOTIATING,
        NegotiationStatus.CLOSED,
        NegotiationStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    NegotiationStatus.READY_FOR_APPROVAL: {
        NegotiationStatus.NEGOTIATING,
        NegotiationStatus.CLOSED,
        NegotiationStatus.CANCELLED,
    },

    NegotiationStatus.CLOSED: set(),
    NegotiationStatus.CANCELLED: set(),
}

Transition function:

def transition_negotiation(
    negotiation,
    target_status,
):
    allowed = ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.get(
        negotiation.status,
        set(),
    )

    if target_status not in allowed:
        raise InvalidNegotiationTransition(
            f"{negotiation.status} -> {target_status}"
        )

    negotiation.status = target_status
23. Deadlock detection

Do not use an LLM to decide:

“The parties are legally deadlocked.”

Instead use deterministic signals.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DeadlockPolicy:
    max_rounds: int | None
    max_rejections_per_issue: int | None
    no_progress_rounds: int | None

Then:

async def detect_deadlock(db, negotiation, policy):
    if policy.max_rounds is not None:
        if negotiation.current_round_number >= policy.max_rounds:
            return DeadlockReason.ROUND_LIMIT

    issues = await get_open_issues(
        db,
        negotiation.id,
    )

    for issue in issues:
        rejection_count = await count_rejections(
            db,
            issue.id,
        )

        if (
            policy.max_rejections_per_issue is not None
            and rejection_count
            >= policy.max_rejections_per_issue
        ):
            return DeadlockReason.REPEATED_REJECTION

    if await has_no_progress(
        db,
        negotiation,
        policy.no_progress_rounds,
    ):
        return DeadlockReason.NO_PROGRESS

    return None

Then the system can say:

{
  "deadlock_detected": true,
  "reason": "REPEATED_REJECTION"
}

rather than inventing psychological or legal conclusions.

24. AI negotiation intelligence

The AI layer gets a strict boundary.

Allowed:

summarize negotiation
find repeated objections
identify unresolved clauses
compare language
suggest alternatives
explain differences
flag possible risk changes
identify playbook conflicts

Not allowed:

automatically send counteroffer
automatically concede
automatically accept
automatically reject
change authoritative agreement
hide internal strategy
infer motivation
declare legal validity
override approval policy

Structured response:

class NegotiationAISuggestion(BaseModel):
    issue_id: UUID
    suggestion_type: str
    proposed_text: str | None
    explanation: str
    confidence: float
    source_references: list[dict]
    playbook_references: list[dict]

Every citation must be validated.

async def validate_ai_references(
    db,
    suggestion,
):
    for reference in suggestion.source_references:
        version_id = reference["version_id"]
        block_id = reference["block_id"]

        block = await get_block(
            db,
            version_id,
            block_id,
        )

        if block is None:
            raise InvalidAIReference(
                "AI referenced nonexistent contract content."
            )

The resulting object should be stored as:

SYSTEM_SUGGESTION

not as a human proposal.

30. Version safety

This is mandatory.

Suppose:

Current Version = V7
Negotiation started from V7

Someone independently changes the agreement:

V7 → V8

The negotiation is now stale.

Do not silently merge it.

async def ensure_negotiation_base_is_current(
    db,
    negotiation,
):
    current = await get_current_version(
        db,
        negotiation.agreement_id,
    )

    if current.id != negotiation.base_version_id:
        raise StaleNegotiationError(
            "Negotiation base version is no longer current."
        )

Then offer:

Rebase negotiation

rather than silently applying it.

31. Rebase

A useful 3.23 capability is negotiated-change rebasing.

V7
 │
 ├── Negotiation A
 │       └── changes block X
 │
 └── Independent update
         └── V8 changes block Y

Rebase A:
V8
 +
A's accepted changes to X
 =
Candidate V9

But if both change X:

V7
 │
 ├── Negotiation A → X
 │
 └── V8 → X

=> CONFLICT

Create:

class NegotiationRebaseConflict(Base):
    __tablename__ = "negotiation_rebase_conflicts"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)

    negotiation_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("negotiations.id"),
        nullable=False,
    )

    block_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    negotiation_content: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    current_content: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    resolution: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=True,
    )

    resolved: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
    )

This prevents silent data loss.

34. Router example
@router.post(
    "/negotiation-issues/{issue_id}/proposals",
    response_model=ProposalResponse,
)
async def create_proposal(
    issue_id: UUID,
    payload: ProposalCreate,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
):
    issue = await negotiation_repo.get_issue(
        db,
        issue_id,
    )

    if not issue:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail="Negotiation issue not found",
        )

    negotiation = await negotiation_repo.get(
        db,
        issue.negotiation_id,
    )

    await negotiation_permissions.assert_can_submit_proposal(
        principal,
        negotiation,
        visibility=issue.visibility,
    )

    async with db.begin():
        proposal = await negotiation_service.create_proposal(
            db=db,
            negotiation=negotiation,
            issue=issue,
            actor=principal,
            proposed_text=payload.proposed_text,
            rationale=payload.rationale,
        )

        await event_service.record(
            db,
            event_type="NEGOTIATION_PROPOSAL_CREATED",
            aggregate_id=negotiation.id,
            actor=principal,
            metadata={
                "issue_id": str(issue.id),
                "proposal_id": str(proposal.id),
            },
        )

    return proposal

Then each client fetches the resource through normal authorization.

That prevents accidental leakage through WebSocket events.

39. Submit for approval

The negotiation service should verify everything before handoff.

async def submit_for_approval(
    db,
    negotiation,
    actor,
):
    await validate_all_negotiation_issues(
        db,
        negotiation.id,
    )

    await ensure_base_version_current(
        db,
        negotiation,
    )

    proposed_version = await compile_negotiated_proposed_version(
        db,
        negotiation,
        actor,
    )

    await risk_service.validate_proposed_version(
        db,
        proposed_version.id,
    )

    await change_service.attach_negotiated_version(
        db,
        change_request_id=negotiation.change_request_id,
        proposed_version_id=proposed_version.id,
    )

    transition_negotiation(
        negotiation,
        NegotiationStatus.READY_FOR_APPROVAL,
    )

Then existing 3.6 approval workflow takes over.

40. Critical rule: no direct approval duplication

Do not implement:

NegotiationApproval

as a competing approval engine.

Negotiation should hand off to:

3.6 Review
3.6 Approval
3.22 Change Request
3.7 Signing

The ownership chain stays:

Negotiation
    ↓
Change Request
    ↓
Proposed Version
    ↓
Approval Workflow
    ↓
Applied Version
    ↓
Signing
41. Database constraints

Add strong constraints where practical:

negotiation.organization_id
    = change_request.organization_id

negotiation.organization_id
    = agreement.organization_id

round.organization_id
    = negotiation.organization_id

issue.organization_id
    = negotiation.organization_id

proposal.organization_id
    = negotiation.organization_id

For PostgreSQL, use composite foreign keys when the schema supports it.

This gives you another tenant-isolation layer beyond application authorization.

42. Row-level security

Keep PostgreSQL RLS as defense-in-depth.

Example:

CREATE POLICY negotiation_isolation
ON negotiations
USING (
    organization_id = current_setting(
        'app.organization_id',
        true
    )::uuid
);

Do the same for:

negotiation_rounds
negotiation_participants

negotiation_playbook_versions

External identities should not receive direct database access.

46. Idempotency

Actions such as:

accept proposal
reject proposal
compile negotiation
submit for approval

must be idempotent.

For example:

operation_key = (
    f"negotiation:{negotiation.id}:"
    f"accept-proposal:{proposal.id}"
)

Store processed operation identifiers using the existing idempotency infrastructure.

A repeated request must not create:

two concessions
two proposed versions
two audit chains
two approval workflows
47. Negotiation compilation algorithm

The production sequence should be:

1. Lock negotiation
2. Lock change request
3. Read current agreement version
4. Verify base_version == current_version
5. Load accepted proposals
6. Verify every proposal
7. Verify every source block
8. Detect duplicate block changes
9. Detect stale blocks
10. Detect conflicts
11. Compile candidate document
12. Validate document structure
13. Create immutable proposed version
14. Attach proposed version to change request
15. Run risk analysis asynchronously
16. Emit NEGOTIATION_READY_FOR_APPROVAL
17. Do NOT change current agreement version
18. Commit transaction
19. Publish outbox events

Only after approval:

Approval
   ↓
3.22 apply change
   ↓
current_version = proposed_version

You now have:

REAL AGREEMENT
      │
      ▼
CHANGE REQUEST
      │
      ▼
NEGOTIATION ROOM
      │
      ├── Internal participants
      ├── External participants

      ├── Negotiation rounds

             │

3.24 — Contract Clause Library, Standardization & Organizational Legal Policy

Now that 3.23 gives Agreement a negotiation environment, the next logical layer is a controlled clause library.

The purpose is not to create a universal legal database. It creates an organization-owned system for:

approved clause language
alternative clause variants
fallback language
prohibited language
approval-required language
clause metadata
applicability rules
versioning
provenance
negotiation reuse
template integration
risk integration
change-management integration

The fundamental rule remains:

The clause library provides organizational guidance. It does not replace legal judgment or become the authoritative contract.

1. Architecture

The overall pipeline becomes:

                 Organization
                      │
                      ▼
              Clause Library
                      │
         ┌────────────┼────────────┐
         ▼            ▼            ▼
      Templates    Playbooks    Negotiation
         │            │            │
         └────────────┼────────────┘
                      ▼
                Proposed Version
                      │
                      ▼
                 Risk Analysis
                      │
                      ▼
                    Review
                      │
                      ▼
                   Approval
                      │
                      ▼
             Authoritative Agreement

A clause can therefore move through:

Draft
  ↓
Internal Review
  ↓
Approved
  ↓
Published
  ↓
Reused
  ↓
Revised
  ↓
Deprecated

Previous versions remain historically available.

6. Why immutable clause versions matter

Suppose the organization approves:

Clause V3

and six months later changes it to:

Clause V4

An old agreement containing V3 must still show V3.

Otherwise:

Historical Agreement
        ↓
Current Library Clause
        ↓
Historical contract appears to have changed

which is unacceptable.

The contract stores its own immutable content.

The clause library is only a reusable source.

8. Applicability engine

The matcher should evaluate actual agreement context.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClauseContext:
    organization_id: UUID
    agreement_type_id: UUID | None
    jurisdiction: str | None
    counterparty_role: str | None
    effective_at: datetime

Then:

def applicability_matches(
    rule: ClauseApplicability,
    context: ClauseContext,
) -> bool:

    if rule.organization_id != context.organization_id:
        return False

    if (
        rule.agreement_type_id is not None
        and rule.agreement_type_id != context.agreement_type_id
    ):
        return False

    if (
        rule.jurisdiction is not None
        and rule.jurisdiction != context.jurisdiction
    ):
        return False

    if (
        rule.counterparty_role is not None
        and rule.counterparty_role
        != context.counterparty_role
    ):
        return False

    if rule.effective_from is not None:
        if context.effective_at < rule.effective_from:
            return False

    if rule.effective_until is not None:
        if context.effective_at > rule.effective_until:
            return False

    return True

12. Creating a clause from negotiated language

3.23 can feed approved negotiated language into 3.24.

But do not automatically publish it.

Flow:

Negotiation Proposal
      ↓
Accepted
      ↓
Human chooses:
"Save to Clause Library"
      ↓
Create Draft Clause
      ↓
Review
      ↓
Approval
      ↓
Publish

Service:

async def create_from_negotiation(
    db,
    negotiation,
    proposal,
    actor,
):
    await assert_can_manage_clause_library(
        actor,
        negotiation.organization_id,
    )

    clause = Clause(
        id=uuid4(),
        organization_id=negotiation.organization_id,
        name=build_clause_name(
            negotiation,
            proposal,
        ),
        category=derive_configured_category(
            negotiation,
            proposal,
        ),
        status=ClauseStatus.DRAFT,
        use_status=ClauseUseStatus.DISABLED,
        created_by=actor.user_id,
        created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        updated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    )

    db.add(clause)

    version = ClauseVersion(
        id=uuid4(),
        clause_id=clause.id,
        organization_id=negotiation.organization_id,
        version_number=1,
        variant_type=ClauseVariantType.STANDARD,
        text=proposal.proposed_text,
        content_hash=sha256_text(
            proposal.proposed_text
        ),
        source_type=ClauseSourceType.NEGOTIATED,
        source_reference={
            "negotiation_id": str(negotiation.id),
            "proposal_id": str(proposal.id),
        },
        review_status=ClauseReviewStatus.PENDING,
        created_by=actor.user_id,
        created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    )

    db.add(version)

    return clause, version

This keeps negotiation history intact.

14. Publishing

Publishing must atomically switch the current clause version.

async def publish_clause(
    db,
    clause_id,
    version_id,
    actor,
):
    clause = await get_clause_for_update(
        db,
        clause_id,
    )

    version = await get_clause_version(
        db,
        version_id,
    )

    if version.clause_id != clause.id:
        raise DomainError(
            "Clause version does not belong to clause."
        )

    if version.review_status != ClauseReviewStatus.APPROVED:
        raise DomainError(
            "Clause version has not been approved."
        )

    if clause.organization_id != actor.organization_id:
        raise AuthorizationError()

    clause.current_version_id = version.id
    clause.status = ClauseStatus.PUBLISHED
    clause.use_status = ClauseUseStatus.AVAILABLE

    await audit_service.record(
        db,
        event_type="CLAUSE_PUBLISHED",
        organization_id=clause.organization_id,
        actor=actor,
        metadata={
            "clause_id": str(clause.id),
            "clause_version_id": str(version.id),
        },
    )

Previous published versions remain immutable.

15. Deprecation

Do not delete clauses that were used historically.

async def deprecate_clause(
    db,
    clause,
    actor,
    reason,
):
    assert_can_manage_clause_library(
        actor,
        clause.organization_id,
    )

    clause.status = ClauseStatus.DEPRECATED
    clause.use_status = ClauseUseStatus.RESTRICTED

    await audit_service.record(
        db,
        event_type="CLAUSE_DEPRECATED",
        organization_id=clause.organization_id,
        actor=actor,
        metadata={
            "clause_id": str(clause.id),
            "reason": reason,
        },
    )

Existing agreements continue using their historical text.

16. Clause matching

The library should provide search and matching.

Given:

Agreement type
Clause category
Jurisdiction
Counterparty role
Policy
Current date

the server can return applicable clauses.

async def find_applicable_clauses(
    db,
    context: ClauseContext,
):
    versions = await clause_repository.find_published_versions(
        db,
        organization_id=context.organization_id,
    )

    results = []

    for version in versions:
        applicability = await repository.get_applicability(
            db,
            version.id,
        )

        if any(
            applicability_matches(rule, context)
            for rule in applicability
        ):
            results.append(version)

    return results

For large organizations this should eventually be SQL-driven rather than Python-loop based.

      ↓

      ↓

      ↓

Never:

    ↓

20. Detecting policy conflicts

Suppose:

Clause = AVAILABLE
Playbook = FORBIDDEN

The system should not allow the clause to be selected casually.

def evaluate_clause_use(
    clause_version,
    usage_rule,
    playbook_position,
):
    if playbook_position == PlaybookPositionType.FORBIDDEN:
        return ClauseUseDecision.BLOCKED

    if (
        playbook_position
        == PlaybookPositionType.APPROVAL_REQUIRED
    ):
        return ClauseUseDecision.APPROVAL_REQUIRED

    if usage_rule.requires_approval:
        return ClauseUseDecision.APPROVAL_REQUIRED

    return ClauseUseDecision.ALLOWED

25. Clause health

A useful organizational signal:

Clause Health

could be derived from actual history:

usage_count
negotiation_change_count
rejection_count
risk_findings_count
policy_conflict_count
current_status
last_reviewed_at

Do not invent a score.

Calculate from the organization's actual records.

26. Clause drift

You can now detect:

Published standard clause
             ↓
Negotiated contracts
             ↓
Repeated deviations

For example:

STANDARD CLAUSE
       │
       ├── Agreement A → unchanged
       ├── Agreement B → modified
       ├── Agreement C → modified
       ├── Agreement D → fallback
       └── Agreement E → counterparty version

If repeated actual negotiations depart from the standard, Agreement can surface:

“This clause has been modified frequently in recent negotiations.”

That is an observed pattern, not a legal conclusion.

28. Policy conflict detection

Before compiling a negotiated version:

Accepted proposal
      ↓
Does language correspond to forbidden organizational position?
      ↓
YES → approval gate
NO  → continue

But never let the policy engine silently rewrite the clause.

class ClausePolicyViolation(Exception):
    pass

Use:

async def validate_clause_policy(
    db,
    organization_id,
    issue,
    proposed_text,
):
    policy = await policy_service.get_active_policy(
        db,
        organization_id,
    )

    if policy is None:
        return

    result = await policy_engine.evaluate(
        policy=policy,
        issue=issue,
        proposed_text=proposed_text,
    )

    if result.blocked:
        raise ClausePolicyViolation(
            result.reason
        )

39. Critical security model

A clause can be:

internal
published
available

without being externally visible.

External users should generally see only the wording actually shared with them.

They must not receive:

organization playbook
forbidden alternatives
internal clause rationale
historical internal usage
private deviation analytics
internal risk data
approval rules
internal policy metadata
40. No hardcoded legal content

This milestone must contain zero built-in legal language.

Do not ship:

DEFAULT_LIABILITY_CLAUSE = "..."
DEFAULT_INDEMNITY_CLAUSE = "..."
DEFAULT_JURISDICTION = "..."

Do not ship:

LEGAL_REQUIREMENTS = {...}

unless the system is specifically being designed as a separately governed legal knowledge product.

Agreement itself should contain the machinery to store and govern organizational policy, not pretend its developers know the user's legal policy.

44. Most important correctness tests
Old clause versions never mutate
async def test_published_clause_version_is_immutable(...):
    version = await get_clause_version(...)

    original_hash = version.content_hash
    original_text = version.text

    with pytest.raises(ImmutableRecordError):
        await clause_service.update_published_version(
            version,
            "new text",
        )

    assert version.text == original_text
    assert version.content_hash == original_hash
Publishing does not modify historical agreements
async def test_clause_publish_does_not_change_old_agreement(...):
    historical = await get_agreement_version(
        db,
        old_agreement_version_id,
    )

    await clause_service.publish_clause(
        db,
        clause.id,
        new_clause_version.id,
        actor,
    )

    historical_after = await get_agreement_version(
        db,
        old_agreement_version_id,
    )

    assert historical_after.content == historical.content
Forbidden policy blocks use
async def test_forbidden_clause_requires_policy_block(...):
    result = await clause_policy_service.evaluate(...)

    assert result.decision == ClauseUseDecision.BLOCKED
External user cannot see internal clause metadata
async def test_external_cannot_read_clause_strategy(...):
    response = await external_client.get(
        f"/api/clauses/{clause.id}"
    )

    body = response.json()

    assert "internal_rationale" not in body
    assert "usage_analytics" not in body
    assert "policy_rules" not in body

3.25 — Contract Compliance, Regulatory Requirements & Policy Monitoring

3.24 gave Agreement an organizational clause/policy layer.

3.25 adds the ability to continuously answer:

“Does this agreement comply with the requirements that actually apply to it, and did those requirements change?”

This is the point where Agreement moves from being only a contract-management system toward a continuous contract compliance platform.

The system must distinguish four things:

External Requirement
        ↓
Organization Policy
        ↓
Agreement Compliance Assessment
        ↓
Human Decision / Remediation

None of these should be silently treated as legal truth.

1. Core architecture
                    REAL EXTERNAL SOURCES
                           │
                           ▼
                Regulatory Source Registry
                           │
                           ▼
                  Source Observation
                           │
                           ▼
                 Requirement Extraction
                           │
                           ▼
                 Requirement Versioning
                           │
                           ▼
               Applicability Determination
                           │
                ┌──────────┴──────────┐
                ▼                     ▼
        Organization Policy     Agreement Context
                │                     │
                └──────────┬──────────┘
                           ▼
                  Compliance Assessment
                           │
             ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
             ▼             ▼             ▼
          Compliant      Gap        Inconclusive
             │             │             │
             └─────────────┼─────────────┘
                           ▼
                  Human Review / Task
                           │
                           ▼
                 Remediation Workflow
                           │
                           ▼
                 Change / Amendment
2. What this milestone must not do

Do not build:

"AI lawyer"

Do not let the platform automatically declare:

"This contract is legally compliant."

Instead return structured outcomes:

COMPLIANT
NON_COMPLIANT
PARTIALLY_COMPLIANT
INCONCLUSIVE
NOT_APPLICABLE
REQUIRES_REVIEW

with evidence.

4. Requirement lifecycle
from enum import StrEnum


class RequirementStatus(StrEnum):
    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
    SUPERSEDED = "SUPERSEDED"
    RETIRED = "RETIRED"


class RequirementSourceType(StrEnum):
    REGULATOR = "REGULATOR"
    GOVERNMENT = "GOVERNMENT"
    INDUSTRY_BODY = "INDUSTRY_BODY"
    ORGANIZATION_POLICY = "ORGANIZATION_POLICY"
    CONTRACTUAL = "CONTRACTUAL"


class ComplianceStatus(StrEnum):
    COMPLIANT = "COMPLIANT"
    NON_COMPLIANT = "NON_COMPLIANT"
    PARTIALLY_COMPLIANT = "PARTIALLY_COMPLIANT"
    INCONCLUSIVE = "INCONCLUSIVE"
    NOT_APPLICABLE = "NOT_APPLICABLE"
    REQUIRES_REVIEW = "REQUIRES_REVIEW"


class GapStatus(StrEnum):
    OPEN = "OPEN"
    IN_REVIEW = "IN_REVIEW"
    REMEDIATING = "REMEDIATING"
    RESOLVED = "RESOLVED"
    ACCEPTED = "ACCEPTED"
    DISMISSED = "DISMISSED"


class EvidenceStatus(StrEnum):
    VERIFIED = "VERIFIED"
    UNVERIFIED = "UNVERIFIED"
    REJECTED = "REJECTED"


class ApplicabilityStatus(StrEnum):
    MATCHED = "MATCHED"
    NOT_MATCHED = "NOT_MATCHED"
    UNCERTAIN = "UNCERTAIN"
5. Regulatory source registry

Never hardcode regulatory websites directly into the compliance engine.

Create a configurable source registry.

class ComplianceSource(Base):
    __tablename__ = "compliance_sources"

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)

    organization_id: Mapped[UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("organizations.id"),
        nullable=True,
        index=True,
    )

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(300),
        nullable=False,
    )

    source_type: Mapped[RequirementSourceType] = mapped_column(
        String(40),
        nullable=False,
    )

    connector_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(100),
        nullable=False,
    )

    base_reference: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        Text,
        nullable=False,
    )

    active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean,
        nullable=False,
        default=False,
    )

    trust_policy: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSON,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
    )

    configuration: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(
        JSON,
        nullable=False,
        default=dict,
    )

    created_by: Mapped[UUID | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id"),
        nullable=True,
    )

    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
    )

The system can then support actual configured sources such as:

official regulator
government publication
registered industry body
organization's internal policy repository

without assuming which jurisdictions or regulators matter.
